state from the org: built in, on, turned off, inactive
in Setup, not set up, or not available (ADR-0138,
`0138-instant-totals-generated-trigger-deployed-by-the-admin.md`). Editing a rollup never
regenerates the trigger, because the rollup's settings live only in the definition. A
generated trigger is switched off like any other automation, through an Automation Setting
row (Section 10) named after the trigger, which the Builder creates with Is Package Default
false the first time it is turned off; removing the trigger is a deploy the administrator
makes from the Builder's removal package. Health Check findings for generated triggers are
deferred (ADR-0138).

Until a source entity has a rollup trigger (a registration of `RollupTriggerHandler` for it,
or its generated trigger active in Setup with its switch on), the Builder says plainly, when that source is chosen, that its totals are updated by
the nightly run and Recalculate and not instantly, does not offer Instantly alone, and refuses
a save or a mode change on the rollup list that would make such a rollup Instantly alone
(ADR-0136). Both and Every night are allowed; a Flow built from the template still makes Both
instant, which the engine cannot see.

**R-R13 Freshness stamps are written when the work is done.** A calculation writes
`Rollups_Last_Calculated__c` on a target record in the same write as its totals (Section
26), and a definition's Last Calculated is set when the run that covers it has finished,
not when it was queued (R-R5). Because unchanged values are not written (R-R11), a record
whose totals a run confirmed without changing keeps its earlier stamp; the definition's Last
Calculated is what says the run happened. Stamping every record on every run would rewrite
every target record every night, which is the load the changed-only rule removes.

**R-R14 One full run at a time, and nothing lost when a chunk stops.** A full recalculation
(the nightly run, Recalculate, Recalculate all) does not start while another is running: the
second start is refused, names the running job, and tells the admin to try again when it
finishes. A chunk of a full run that the platform stops with an error the run cannot catch
(a governor limit) has its target records written to the Rollup Queue (Section 14A), so they
are recalculated within minutes rather than at the next night.

**R-R15 Aggregates and the target types they fill.** Each aggregate fills only the target
types below; any other pairing is refused on save (R-R10) and by the planner.

| Aggregate | What it answers | Target attribute types |
|---|---|---|
| SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX | The total, the average, the smallest and the largest value of the Source Attribute. | number, currency, percent, date, datetime |
| COUNT | How many records match. | number, currency, percent, date, datetime (as before; a number is what makes sense) |
| FIRST, LAST | The Source Attribute of the record with the lowest (FIRST) or highest (LAST) Order By Attribute. | number, currency, percent, date, datetime, text, long text, picklist (from a picklist or text Source Attribute) |
| COUNT_DISTINCT | How many different values the Source Attribute holds among the matching records. | number |
| ANY | True when at least one record matches, false when none does. | checkbox |
| NONE | True when no record matches, false when at least one does. | checkbox |
| TEXT_LIST | The Source Attribute of every matching record, joined by the Delimiter. | text, long text |
| TEXT_LIST_DISTINCT | The same, with each value listed once. | text, long text |

- **Blanks.** A blank Source Attribute is never counted by COUNT_DISTINCT and never listed by
  a text list. FIRST and LAST take the first record's value even when it is blank; a filter
  condition "is not null" on the Source Attribute skips such records. ANY and NONE read no
  Source Attribute: the filter says which records count, so "any gift over 1,000" is ANY with
  the filter `Amount__c greater than 1000`.
- **Ties.** When two records have the same Order By Attribute, FIRST and LAST take the one
  with the lower record Id, so the answer is the same on every run (R-R9).
- **Order of a text list.** By the Order By Attribute when there is one, in the Order
  Direction (ascending when blank), records with a blank one last in either direction;
  otherwise alphabetically by value, ignoring case, A to Z or, descending, Z to A. Ties go to
  the lower record Id. TEXT_LIST_DISTINCT keeps the first occurrence of each value, compared
  exactly (letter case counts), and so does COUNT_DISTINCT.
- **Order Direction and FIRST and LAST.** FIRST is always the record with the lowest Order By
  Attribute and LAST the one with the highest; the direction does not apply to them, so a
  saved definition means what it always meant. "Largest first" is LAST, or a row limited
  aggregate in Descending order.
- **Row Limit (ADR-0136).** SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, TEXT_LIST and TEXT_LIST_DISTINCT may take a
  Row Limit N: only the first N matching records that have a value, in the order of the Order
  By Attribute and the Order Direction, are calculated, for example the sum of the 5 largest
  gifts (Amount, Descending) or the last 3 gift amounts as a text list (Gift Date,
  Descending). TEXT_LIST_DISTINCT lists the first N different values. A Row Limit needs an
  Order By Attribute and is at least 1. COUNT, COUNT_DISTINCT, ANY, NONE, FIRST and LAST take
  none: a limit would only cap a count, or FIRST and LAST already take one record. A grouped
  query cannot limit rows per target, so a row limited aggregate reads the matching rows, as
  a text list does, and keeps the first N per target record.
- **Delimiter.** Comma joins with a comma and a space, Semicolon with a semicolon and a space,
  New line with a line break, Pipe with a space, a vertical bar and a space (` | `), and Custom
  with the Custom Delimiter exactly as stored (up to 10 characters; a Custom Delimiter found
  empty at run time joins with Comma). A value that contains the delimiter is written as it
  is, not escaped, so a list of names that contain commas reads best with Semicolon, New line
  or Pipe.
- **Include Deleted (ADR-0136).** When true, every source query of the definition reads with
  ALL ROWS, so records in the Recycle Bin and archived tasks and events count as if they were
  not deleted or archived. It stays exact under recompute (R-R9): every calculation reads the
  same rows. Two limits: a deleted record counts only until it is purged from the Recycle Bin
  (emptied, or removed after the platform's retention period), and a purge fires no trigger,
  so the total keeps it until the next full recalculation; and a delete marks the target as
  usual (R-R11), but the recalculation still finds the deleted record, so the total does not
  drop. A target whose source rows are read in chunks by the large parent route (R-RQ6) cannot
  read deleted rows that way: the definition is left out of that record's write and the Error
  Log says why, so the total is never written without them.
- **Values into text.** A number, date or checkbox copied into text by FIRST, LAST or a text
  list is written as its plain value (`1250.00`, `2026-03-01`, `true`; a datetime in UTC as
  `2026-03-01 14:05`), not converted between currencies.
- **Picklist targets.** FIRST and LAST may fill a picklist from a picklist or text Source
  Attribute (ADR-0136). The value written is one of the target's active values, matched
  without regard to letter case and written as the target spells it. The save refuses a
  source picklist with an active value the target does not have (R-R10). A text value, or a
  value added to the source picklist later, that the target does not have is left out of the
  write: the record keeps what it holds and the Error Log records the value, the record and
  the attribute, so one value never fails the save of the record's other totals.
- **Cut at the field length.** A text result longer than the target attribute holds is cut at
  the attribute's length, so the save never fails on it and the same value is written on every
  run.
- **Exact under recompute.** Every aggregate here is recomputed from all the source records of
  each marked target (R-R11), so an instant, queued, nightly or on-demand calculation gives the
  same answer; none of them needs a fallback to a full recalculation. COUNT_DISTINCT and the
  text lists read the matching rows rather than a grouped answer, so a value found on the
  records of two household members, or of two path alternatives, is counted once.

**R-R16 Other rollup tools in the org (plan D-124 item 6).** BarnCRM detects DLRS (managed
namespace `dlrs`) and Rollup Helper (managed namespace `rh2`) by the namespace prefix of their
objects in the org's describe, as text, never as a compile-time reference, so an org without
either compiles and runs unchanged (ADR-0013). When one is found, the Rollup Builder, the
Setup Assistant's coexistence step and, when Rollup Builder or Giving is installed, the
Modules page say that it is a separate rollup tool whose rollups BarnCRM does not manage.
BarnCRM never creates, edits, switches off or deletes the other tool's definitions or
triggers. Rollup Helper's definitions are not read; its rollups are moved by hand.

*No shared target with DLRS.* BarnCRM reads DLRS's definitions (its custom metadata type and,
where present, its older custom object, by names built at run time) in system mode, reading
only the fields the installed DLRS version has. An active definition whose Target Entity and
Target Attribute an active DLRS definition also fills (its Parent Object and Aggregate Result
Field, matched through describe, ignoring case) is not saved switched on, and not switched on
in the rollup list, unless the administrator confirms she will switch the DLRS definition off.
The confirmation is a settings change history row (Section 12: Setting Name `Rollup Builder: `
and the definition's Name, Old Value naming the DLRS definition and the field, New Value saying
the switch off was confirmed); DLRS is not changed. The Builder asks only once every other
save check (R-R10, R-R8) has passed. Saving or switching a definition off never asks. Import
from a file cannot ask, so it refuses such an entry (R-R10 by way of `checkedRecord`). Health
Check warns about every active pair found later.

*Import from DLRS.* Each active DLRS definition is mapped to a definition, which is saved
switched off through the Builder's save checks (`checkedRecord`, as a file import is), with
Definition Key `DLRS_` and the DLRS definition's name (cut to 80 characters), so importing
again updates the same definition. Name is the DLRS label; Description says it was imported
from the DLRS definition. The mapping:

- Parent Object, Child Object and Relationship Field become Target Entity, Source Entity and
  Relationship Path, only when the Builder offers that source and path for the target.
- Aggregate Operation: Sum, Max, Min, Avg, Count, Count Distinct, Concatenate (TEXT_LIST),
  Concatenate Distinct (TEXT_LIST_DISTINCT), First and Last. Any other operation is refused.
- Field to Aggregate becomes Source Attribute; for Count, a field other than Id becomes an
  "is not null" condition instead, since DLRS counts only records with the field filled.
- Relationship Criteria becomes the Filter (R-R2) when it is fields compared with literals,
  `= null`, IN, NOT IN, `LIKE 'x%'`, `LIKE '%x%'`, THIS_YEAR, LAST_YEAR and LAST_N_DAYS:n,
  joined by AND, OR, NOT and brackets; anything else is refused naming the part.
- Field to Order By: one field, ASC or DESC, NULLS LAST. A descending First becomes Last and
  the other way round; a text list or row limit keeps the direction as Order Direction. More
  than one field, or NULLS FIRST, is refused. A First or Last with none orders by the field
  it reads.
- Row Limit: kept for the R-R15 aggregates, dropped from First, refused on Last and the counts.
- Concatenate Delimiter: BR(), SP() and TB() are read as a new line, a space and a tab first
  (DLRS writes them because Salesforce trims a text value's spaces on save). Then `, `, `; `,
  ` | ` and a new line become Comma, Semicolon, Pipe and New line; blank becomes Comma;
  anything else becomes Custom when it fits ten characters on one line (spaces and tabs at
  either end included: the Custom Delimiter is stored with them as tokens, below), otherwise
  it is refused.
- Aggregate All Rows becomes Include Deleted; Bypass Permission is kept.
- Calculation Mode: Realtime, Developer and Process Builder become Both; Scheduled stays
  Scheduled. Sharing mode User is not kept: definitions run in system mode.

A DLRS definition is also refused when an active definition already fills its field, or when
its copy is already switched on. Nothing is refused silently: each refusal and each change is
said in words. A compare step shows, for up to five target records, the value the record holds
(DLRS wrote it) beside the value the copy calculates, writing nothing. A copy is switched on
only with the confirmation above, recorded the same way. DLRS is read, never changed.

*NPSP customizable rollups (MIG-08, ADR-0197 migration-assistant decision 11).* NPSP's
customizable rollups (its custom metadata types Rollup and Filter Rule, `Rollup` and `Filter_Rule` with the `__mdt` suffix, in
namespace `npsp`, names built at run time, read by describe in system mode, only the fields the
installed version has) are read into the same definition shape and pass through the same import
steps, compare and confirmation as DLRS's, with Definition Key `NPSP_` and the NPSP rollup's
developer name. A rollup is active when Active is true and Is Deleted is not. Summary Object and
Field become Target Entity and Attribute; Detail Object becomes Source Entity, by the one lookup
from it to the summary object (a standard lookup first when there are several); Operation Sum,
Count, Average, Largest, Smallest, First and Last become SUM, COUNT, AVG, MAX, MIN, FIRST and LAST,
reading Amount Field (Detail Field, when set, for Largest, Smallest, First and Last) and ordering
First and Last by Date Field. Time Bound All Time adds nothing, Years Ago 0 and 1 add Date Field
this year and last year, Days Back n adds the last n days. Each filter rule on the detail object
becomes a condition, joined by AND (Equals, Not Equals, Greater, Less, Greater or Equal, Less or
Equal, In List, Not In List, Starts With, Contains; a record type named by developer name or name
becomes its Id). Refused with the reason, so the rollup stays in NPSP: Years Donated, Donor
Streak, Best Year and Best Year Total; Amount or Date read from another object; a filter rule on
another object or with another operator; fiscal years; Years Ago above 1; a contact summarized
from Opportunity (NPSP credits contacts through contact roles); no single lookup to the summary
object. The same-field guard applies to active NPSP customizable rollups as to DLRS's, with the
other tool named. NPSP is read, never changed.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Rollup_Definition__c`, listed and edited in the settings console.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Name | `Name` | Text (standard) |
| Description | `Description__c` | Long Text Area |
| Definition Key | `Definition_Key__c` | Text, External Id, unique |
| Source Entity | `Source_Object__c` | Text |
| Target Entity | `Target_Object__c` | Text |
| Relationship Path | `Relationship_Path__c` | Text |
| Aggregate | `Aggregate__c` | Picklist: SUM, COUNT, MIN, MAX, FIRST, LAST, AVG, COUNT_DISTINCT, ANY, NONE, TEXT_LIST, TEXT_LIST_DISTINCT (labels Sum, Count, Minimum, Maximum, First, Last, Average, Count distinct, Any, None, Text list, Text list, each value once) |
| Delimiter | `Delimiter__c` | Picklist: Comma, Semicolon, New line, Pipe, Custom (default Comma) |
| Custom Delimiter | `Custom_Delimiter__c` | Text (40). Up to 10 characters as typed; Salesforce trims a text value, so whitespace at either end is stored as tokens (SP() a space, TB() a tab, BR() a new line, as DLRS does), encoded on save and decoded wherever the delimiter is used or shown (`RollupPlanner.encodeDelimiter` and `decodeDelimiter`). A value saved without tokens reads as it is |
| Include Deleted | `Include_Deleted__c` | Checkbox (default false) |
| Source Attribute | `Source_Field__c` | Text |
| Order By Attribute | `Order_By_Field__c` | Text |
| Order Direction | `Order_Direction__c` | Picklist: Ascending, Descending (default Ascending) |
| Row Limit | `Row_Limit__c` | Number (4, 0 decimals) |
| Target Attribute | `Target_Field__c` | Text |
| Filter | `Filter_JSON__c` | Long Text Area |
| Target Filter | `Target_Filter_JSON__c` | Long Text Area |
| Fiscal Year Aware | `Fiscal_Year_Aware__c` | Checkbox |
| Fiscal Year Offset | `Fiscal_Year_Offset__c` | Number (0 decimals) |
| Fiscal Date Attribute | `Fiscal_Date_Field__c` | Text |
| Mode | `Mode__c` | Picklist: Real-time, Scheduled, Both (labels Instantly, Every night, Both (recommended); the same on `Rollup_Mode_Default__c`) |
| Last Calculated | `Last_Calculated__c` | DateTime |
| Is Package Default | `Is_Package_Default__c` | Checkbox |
| Active | `Active__c` | Checkbox |
| Bypass Permission | `Bypass_Permission__c` | Text(255) |

- **Shipped defaults:** `Rollup_Definition_Default__mdt` (Section 13).
- **Automation:** one registry row on `Rollup_Definition__c`, `Rollup_Definition_Validation`
  ("Check rollups before saving"), handler `RollupDefinitionValidationHandler`, execution order
  10, the save check of R-R10 and R-R15. It checks an insert and an edit of the aggregate, the
  target, the source attribute, the Order By Attribute, the Row Limit or the delimiters, so
  switching a definition on or off never re-checks it. It also refuses a Bypass Permission that names no custom permission in the org (R-R4a), on an
  insert and when the value changes, with one query for every name in the save. It
  pauses while the module is turned off (ADR-0125 `0125-rollup-builder-module.md`, decision
  9); a definition saved then that cannot be planned is refused by `RollupPlanner` and logged
  on every run, so no total is written wrong.
- **Settings keys:** `Rollup_Mode_Default__c` (Section 14B). The fiscal year is not a
  BarnCRM setting: it is the org's, read from Setup (R-R3).
- **Field history:** tracked on Source Entity, Target Entity, Relationship Path, Aggregate,
  Source Attribute, Target Attribute, Filter, Target Filter, Mode and Active, so "who changed
  how this total is calculated" has an answer (owner decision 2026-10-12; a platform feature,
  completed with the Rollup Builder, which set Filter and Target Filter). Long text attributes
  record that they changed, not the values.
- **Rollup Builder:** the `Rollup_Builder` tab and app page, `rollupBuilder` (which nests the
  Rollups list, `rollupDefinitions`, with New, Edit, Copy and Delete, the last through
  `RollupController.deleteRollup` in user mode, R-R6), `rollupWizard` (the five steps)
  and `rollupFilterBuilder` (R-R2 documents, built once and shared with Find, plan Section
  4.9). `RollupBuilderController` describes the org for the steps, in the running user's
  describe, and saves a definition in user mode after the checks of R-R10 and R-R8. A new
  definition gets the Definition Key `Custom_` followed by 16 random hexadecimal characters,
  and Is Package Default false; an edited one keeps its key. Its preview (S12) calculates the
  unsaved definition for one record through `RollupEngine.preview`, which writes nothing, and
  counts the target records it would maintain in user mode. `RollupController.estimateFullRun`
  counts the records Recalculate all goes through at a fixed rough rate (1,650 records a
  minute, to be measured on an org), and `runTonight` sets up one run at the nightly hour (Section 14B) through
  `RollupScheduler.scheduleTonight` only when the nightly run is not scheduled. Needs
  attention (S13), `rollupNeedsAttention` under the list, reads the Rollup Queue in user mode
  through `RollupAttentionController` (records waiting and the oldest's age, one row per record
  of each Failed entry named by describe, at most 200, whether the nightly run is scheduled and
  how the last full run ended); its Retry, for the selected records' entries or all, goes
  through `RollupQueue.retry`, which sets them Pending with Attempts 0 and no Next Attempt in
  system mode (R-RQ4, R-RQ5).
- **Moving rollups between orgs (ADR-0136; lifts ADR-0082's deferral):**
  `RollupDefinitionTransfer`, from the Builder's list. Export writes a JSON file
  `{"format": "BarnCRM rollups", "version": 1, "rollups": [...]}` of the ticked rollups, or
  every one with Is Package Default false; each entry is the definition as the Builder edits it
  (its `Draft`) with its Definition Key and without its record Id, Last Calculated or Is
  Package Default. Shipped definitions are never exported or imported: each org has them from
  the package (R-R6). **Keying rule:** an import matches an entry to an existing definition by
  Definition Key, ignoring case; a match is updated in place, no match is created with the
  file's key, so importing the same file twice changes nothing more. Import first says what it
  would do to each entry, then saves each entry on its own through the Builder's save checks
  (`RollupBuilderController.checkedRecord`: R-R10, R-R8), in user mode, so each is checked
  against those saved before it. An entry keeps the file's Active value only by passing every
  check; one that fails is not saved, and the reason is reported. Also refused per entry: a key
  that is blank or appears twice, a shipped key, and an attribute this version's Builder does
  not know (a file from a newer version is never saved as a different rollup). A file with
  another format name or a higher version is refused whole. An import recalculates nothing;
  the next run does. It stops before the transaction's query or DML limit and reports the
  remaining entries as not imported yet, which a second import of the same file finishes.
- **Service:** `RollupService`, `RollupSelector`, `RollupFilterParser` and `RollupScheduler`,
  in front of BarnCRM's own aggregation core (`decisions/0082-barncrm-owns-its-rollup-engine.md`;
  the vendored apex-rollup tree, `RollupAdapter`, `Rollup__mdt` and `RollupCalcItem__c` were
  deleted in slice S9). That core is
  `RollupEngine` (one pass per target entity), `RollupPlanner` (definitions into source queries), `RollupAggregator` (the calculator), `RollupCurrency` (target record currency),
  `RollupWriter` (changed-only writes), `RollupChanges` (which targets a save marks, R-R11),
  `RollupQueue` (the queue processor, Section 14A), and `RollupFullRecalcBatch` (the full and
  nightly recalculation: one batch pass per target entity in turn, records with many source rows
  in smaller chunks, large parents to the batch route (R-RQ6), Last Calculated stamped when the last pass finishes, R-R13, one
  run at a time, R-R14) with `RollupRecalcErrorHandler` queueing a stopped chunk's records from
  `BatchApexErrorEvent` (R-R14).
- **Flow action and template (R-R12):** `RollupRecalcAction`, the invocable action "Recalculate
  rollups", takes the saved record and its prior values (generic, so it serves any entity) and
  marks targets exactly as a packaged trigger does (R-R11): in the same save when few, queued
  otherwise, and always queued for a record being deleted, since a Flow runs before the delete.
  It does nothing while all automation is paused. `Recalculate_Rollups_Template` is a
  record-triggered Flow template (on Contact, never active) an administrator saves as her own
  copy and points at her entity.
- **Recalculating named records (R-R12 note, ADR-0136):** `RollupRecalcRecordAction`, the
  invocable action "Recalculate totals on this record", takes a target record Id and, optionally,
  one rollup's Definition Key or name, and recalculates that record's totals: every active
  definition targeting its entity, whatever the mode, or the one named. A request naming no
  active definition on the record's entity recalculates nothing and is written to the Error
  Log. `RollupService.recalculateTargets` does the work: in the same transaction when it has
  room (R-R4's limits, whatever `Rollup_Processing__c` says, since the caller asked for the
  totals now), queued otherwise, and nothing while the module is turned off.
- **Global Apex (R-R12 note, ADR-0136):** `RollupApi`, for developers who called
  `dlrs.RollupService`: `recalculate(Set<Id>)` is the action above for every active definition,
  and `recalculateChanges(List<SObject>, Map<Id, SObject>, Boolean)` is the Recalculate rollups
  Flow action (`RollupService.runForFlow`) for changed source records of any entities, with
  their prior values and whether they are being deleted. Global is permanent once a managed
  version is released, so the module makes nothing global without an ADR recording it
  (ADR-0136 lists these two classes and the Flow actions).

## 14A. Rollup Queue

### Definition

The list of target records waiting for their totals to be recalculated, and of the ones that
could not be. A bulk change (R-R4) writes the records it affected here instead of
recalculating them in the same save, and one background processor works through the list
(`decisions/0082-barncrm-owns-its-rollup-engine.md`). It is also what the Rollup Builder's
"Needs attention" list reads and what its Retry acts on, so one entity serves as queue,
failure list and retry.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | computed | The entry's identifier, assigned automatically. |
| Target Entity | text | yes | The entity whose records are listed, for example Account or Fund. |
| Record Ids | long text | yes | The identifiers of the target records to recalculate, at most 200, held as text (R-RQ2). |
| Record Count | integer | yes | How many identifiers Record Ids holds, so "records waiting" is a sum rather than a parse. |
| Definition Ids | long text | no | The identifiers of the Rollup Definitions whose change queued the entry, held as text. Empty means every active definition on the target entity (R-R11). |
| Status | picklist(Pending, Failed) | yes (defaults Pending) | Pending: waiting for the processor. Failed: tried five times without success; waits for Retry. |
| Attempts | integer | yes (defaults 0) | How many times the processor has tried these records. |
| Next Attempt | datetime | no | The earliest time the processor tries these records again after a failure; empty means now. |
| Last Error | long text | no | What went wrong on the last attempt, in plain language first, for the Needs attention list. |

### Relationships

- None. Record Ids, Definition Ids and Target Entity are text, never references (R-RQ2). An
  entry names the definitions that queued it, and only those active ones are recalculated for
  its records; an entry with no Definition Ids (a full run's hand-off, an entry written before
  the attribute existed) recalculates every active definition on its target entity (R-R11).

### Rules

**R-RQ1 Append-only for writers.** A transaction that changes source records inserts entries
(one per target entity, split at 200 identifiers) and never updates or deletes one. Only the
processor updates or deletes entries. Two writers therefore never contend for the same entry.

**R-RQ2 Identifiers as text.** A reference to the target would lock the target record when the
entry is inserted, so a large import touching one household would queue behind itself.
Identifiers held as text lock nothing. The cost is that an entry is not reportable by target;
the Needs attention list resolves the names.

**R-RQ3 How the processor works.** It reads Pending entries whose Next Attempt has passed,
merges and sorts their identifiers, recalculates a slice for the union of the entries'
definitions (R-R11), and deletes the entries it
finished. Target records that failed are written back as a new entry with Attempts increased
and Next Attempt set later each time; after the fifth attempt the entry is Failed. The
processor runs again while Pending entries remain. A second processor started by accident is
harmless, because recalculation recomputes (R-R11). A writer starts a processor only when none
is queued. A waiting processor may start and finish before the writer commits, so a transaction
that inserted entries and queued no processor (one was waiting, it asked earlier with nothing
pending, or its job allowance was used) publishes one `Rollup_Queue_Ready__e`, whose subscriber
asks again after commit; the subscriber, which inserts none, never publishes (ADR-0117,
`0117-rollup-queue-asks-again-after-commit.md`). When automation is paused, or the event cannot
be published, the nightly run, the
end of a pause, Retry and Start now on the Needs attention list start one for the Pending
entries. A save inside a Queueable job never starts
the processor: the platform lets a Queueable queue one job, and that job belongs to the running
job's own next step (the household soft credit recompute, a subscriber's integration). Instead
the transaction publishes one `Rollup_Queue_Ready__e` (publish after commit, however many
entries it wrote), and its subscriber calls `RollupService.startQueuedRecalculation`, which
starts the processor unless one is already waiting (ADR-0100). A job that rolls back publishes
nothing. If the event cannot be published, the entries wait for the next processor a later save
starts, the one a BarnCRM job starts itself when its chain ends, or the nightly run. A partial
save (allOrNone false, as the Bulk API, Data Loader and `Database.delete(records, false)` save)
whose records partly fail is rolled back, entries, queued processor and event with it, and its
triggers run again for the records that passed with static variables kept. The retry is told
apart by a DML count lower than the last insert left (the platform resets governor limits for
it) and that insert's entry gone, and goes back to what it had asked for before the attempt's
first insert, so it asks for a processor again unless one queued earlier in the transaction
survived; the trigger framework clears all its per record claims the same way, so the retry's
records are marked again (a claim never stops a re-fire across a partial save). Before this the
retry left its entries Pending with no processor until the nightly run. The
processor's own chain respects the platform's chain depth limit: a run as deep as its chain may
go (the chain's own maximum when one is set, otherwise five, the Developer Edition, trial and
scratch org limit) publishes the same event instead of queuing the next run, so a fresh chain
starts after it commits. It logs nothing: on a busy org it happens every few runs. Before this the refused
link stopped the chain and left Pending entries until the nightly run. A run that stops on
something it cannot catch, such as a governor limit, is handled by its finalizer, which logs it
to the Error Log. Only the records the run was recalculating are charged: they move to a new
entry with one more attempt and the reason in Last Error (Failed after the fifth), and the rest
of each entry it held stays as it was. An entry charged by a stopped run merges only with others
charged the same way, for the same entity and attempts, and a run takes a quarter as many records
per attempt (50, 12, 3, then 1 of a 200 slice), so a record that stops every run holding it ends
Failed alone while the records it shared runs with are recalculated. Entries whose save was
refused (R-RQ4) are already one record each, so their retries merge and run at the full slice. A single record that stopped its run on the query row limit goes to the large
parent route instead (R-RQ6). The finalizer then publishes the same event rather than queuing
the next run itself, because the platform queues at most five jobs in a row from the finalizers
of failed jobs. Before this a stopped run halved the next run's slice and queued it, and a record
too large for any slice left every entry Pending with nothing to process it. A run also takes
records only up to a row budget (60 percent of the rows a transaction may read), estimated as in
R-RQ6, and returns the rest to the queue for the next run uncharged. Rows its recalculation of
one target entity actually read count against the budget in place of their estimate, so an
entity that read more than its estimate leaves less for the entities after it. This protects only
the later entities: an entity's records are recalculated in one call, so its own records are
taken on their estimates alone.

**R-RQ4 Failures are visible.** A Failed entry stays until someone presses Retry (which sets it
back to Pending with Attempts 0) or the nightly full run recalculates its records successfully
(which deletes it). Each processor and nightly run writes one summary entry to the Error Log
(Section 9) when anything failed, so the Hub's error tile sees it. Health Check reports Failed
entries, and Pending entries older than an hour.

**R-RQ5 Written in system mode.** Entries are the engine's own bookkeeping and are written
under ADR-0021, so a gift saved by a user who cannot see the queue still queues its totals.
The engine's automation switch and the global pause (Section 10) stop entries being written
and processed; the nightly run puts the totals right afterwards in Both mode.

**R-RQ6 Large parents are recalculated by a batch.** An aggregate query counts every row it
aggregates towards the rows one transaction may read (50,000), so a record with tens of
thousands of source rows (a General Fund, a large organization donor) cannot be recalculated by
the processor at any slice size (ADR-0116,
`0116-rollup-large-parents-recalculated-by-a-batch.md`). A record's source rows are estimated
as its largest stored COUNT total times the queries its definitions plan; a filtered or fiscal
year COUNT is a floor, and a record with no COUNT to go by is taken as ten rows per query. The
stored totals of every active COUNT definition on the entity count, not only those of the
definitions the run calculates: an entry that names only a SUM or MAX (ADR-0099) otherwise took
a fund with 25,000 allocations as unknown, and its queries stopped the run.
Before a run recalculates its slice, a record estimated at two fifths of that limit or more
(below the run's row budget of three fifths, R-RQ3, leaving room for the run's other queries and
the target records' automation, and for a low estimate) is moved to a new entry and handed to
the large parent batch; a record below it stays in the queue, alone in a run if it must be. A
stored count goes stale while a load adds children faster than the queue recalculates (a fund
stored 3,200 of its 26,102 allocations), so the run also measures what each query of an entity's
recalculation read: before a further query would take the transaction past four fifths of the
limit, taken to read as much as the largest query before it, the recalculation stops with
nothing written and that entity's records in the run go to the batch as an estimated one does. A
single record that stopped its run on the query row limit (R-RQ3) goes to the batch too. No other failure goes there.
The full run (R-R14) applies the same protection: it estimates each record as above, queues a
record at the threshold or more, naming the run's definitions, instead of calculating it in a
chunk (the tier 1 scale test's fund of 30,000 allocations, calculated alone, stopped its chunk on
the query row limit every run), and recalculates each chunk under the same ceiling; a chunk the
ceiling stops is held back for smaller chunks, and a lone record it stops is queued the same way.
The queue then hands such records to the batch. The batch reads each
planned query's source rows in chunks, runs the query over each chunk's rows only and folds the
partial answers together, which merge exactly as path alternatives do (R-R1; a distinct count or
distinct list keeps one entry per value), then writes each record once, with partial success,
through the same target filters, currency handling and write as any other recalculation (R-R8,
R-R13). It owns the entries it was given: it charges each one attempt as it takes them (Failed
after the fifth), holds them with Next Attempt an hour ahead, renewed with every chunk, deletes
them when the totals are written and releases them with the reason when a chunk stops, so a run
that dies leaves them due again rather than lost. One batch runs at a time: a run starts only
under a lock on the org-level `Rollup_Run_Lock__c` record (created the first time), so two
processors routing records at the same moment cannot both find none running and both start one.
Entries routed while one runs, or when the lock cannot be taken in time, wait two minutes,
uncharged, and are routed again.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Rollup_Queue__c`, auto-number Name with format `RQ-{0000000}`, private sharing,
  readable by the BarnCRM Admin permission set and written only by the engine.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Target Entity | `Target_Object__c` | Text (80) |
| Record Ids | `Record_Ids__c` | Long Text Area |
| Record Count | `Record_Count__c` | Number (0 decimals) |
| Definition Ids | `Definition_Ids__c` | Long Text Area |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist: Pending, Failed |
| Attempts | `Attempts__c` | Number (0 decimals) |
| Next Attempt | `Next_Attempt__c` | DateTime |
| Last Error | `Last_Error__c` | Long Text Area |

- **Service:** `RollupQueue`, which writes entries and is the one processor (a Queueable with a
  finalizer); the Rollup Builder's Needs attention list reads and retries entries.
- **Batch:** `RollupLargeParentBatch`, the large parent route (R-RQ6): a batch over the source
  rows of each planned query, Ids only, chained query by query and entity by entity.
- **Custom setting:** `Rollup_Run_Lock__c`, hierarchy, protected, one field,
  `Last_Run_Started__c` (DateTime). Its one org-level record is the row a large parent run locks
  before it starts (R-RQ6); the code creates it the first time and nothing else reads or writes
  it. **Throttle (D-200 P2):** under the lock, a run starts only when `Large_Parent_Hours__c`
  (Section 14B, default 1) has passed since `Last_Run_Started__c`, which the run stamps as it
  starts; otherwise the entries routed to it wait, uncharged, until then (Next Attempt), and
  the saves queued in between merge into that one run. The Rollup Builder page says how often.
- **Event:** `Rollup_Queue_Ready__e`, a platform event with no fields, publish behavior Publish
  After Commit, published at most once per transaction by a save inside a Queueable job, or by
  one that queued entries and no processor (R-RQ3).
  `RollupQueueReadyTrigger` subscribes and starts the processor.
- **Processor request stamp (D-200 P13):** a save that queues entries runs no query to find a
  processor. It reads `Processor_Requested_At__c` on `Rollup_Settings__c` (from the platform's
  cache):
  within the last ten minutes it publishes the Ready event, whose subscriber checks the job list
  exactly after commit; otherwise it queues a processor and stamps the time (for a chained
  processor queued with a delay, the time it is due). A processor that died is still found
  missing: by the subscriber's exact check while the stamp is recent, and by the next save once
  it is not. The subscriber, background jobs and the nightly run keep the exact check.
- **Nightly scope (D-200 P1, R-R4b):** `RollupNightlyBatch` plans each night from
  `Full_Recalc_Day__c` and `Nightly_Covered_From__c` on `Rollup_Settings__c` (Section 14B):
  the full run, or one batch pass per source entity that queues the targets of what changed.
  Each night it first releases held Pending entries (Next Attempt cleared) and retries Failed
  ones.

## 14B. Rollup Settings

### Definition

The BarnCRM Rollup Builder module's own org-wide settings (ADR-0125,
`0125-rollup-builder-module.md`, decision 6). ADR-0017 gives every module package its own
protected hierarchy custom setting, so the two rollup keys Core held on `BarnCRM_Settings__c`
(Section 12) moved here with the engine, with their API names and definitions unchanged. The
values an org stored on the Core object are not carried over: an org that changed either one
sets it again. Their Setting Definition rows name this object in `Settings_Object__c`, so the
settings console shows them in its Rollups section as before.

- **Custom setting:** `Rollup_Settings__c`, hierarchy, protected.
- **Defaults (ADR-0035):** the field default only fills a record the platform creates; the
  readers in `RollupService` and `RollupScheduler` treat blank, and anything outside the
  allowed values, as the shipped value.
- **Nightly run hour (ADR-0136):** the settings console shows `Nightly_Run_Hour__c` as a
  picklist of the 24 hours (values 0 to 23, labels 12:00 AM (midnight) to 11:00 PM) from its Setting Definition
  row, since a custom setting cannot hold a picklist. The nightly job, Run tonight and the
  Rollup Builder page's schedule line all use it. A save that changes it moves the scheduled
  nightly run at once: Core's settings service hands every changed key to the engine through
  the third engine seam (`RollupEngineExtension.afterSettingsSaved`, ADR-0125 decision 4),
  and `RollupScheduler.reschedule` replaces the job when one is scheduled and starts nothing
  when none is.

| Key | Type | Default | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Rollup_Mode_Default__c` | picklist(Real-time, Scheduled, Both) | Both | The mode a new rollup definition takes unless the admin changes it. Shown as Instantly, Every night and Both (recommended), as on the definition (R-R4). |
| `Rollup_Processing__c` | picklist(Background, In_Save) | Background | When Real-time and Both totals are recalculated (R-R4): Background (shown as After the save (recommended)) queues them in the save and the Rollup Queue recalculates them just after it; In_Save (shown as During the save) recalculates a normal save's totals in it. Blank means Background. |
| `Nightly_Run_Hour__c` | integer(0 to 23) | 2 | The hour the nightly run starts (R-R4), in the time zone of the person who scheduled it, shown as a time (2:00 AM). Blank or out of range means 2. |
| `Large_Parent_Hours__c` | integer(0 to 24) | 1 | The fewest hours between two large parent runs (R-RQ6, D-200 P2); 0 runs as soon as possible. Blank or out of range means 1. |
| `Processor_Requested_At__c` | datetime | blank | Not a setting and not in the console: when the Rollup Queue last asked for a processor (D-200 P13, Section 14A). Written by the engine only. |
| `Full_Recalc_Day__c` | picklist(Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Every_Night) | Sunday | The night the nightly run recalculates every Scheduled and Both total over every record (R-R4b, D-200 P1); Every_Night (shown as Every night) does so every night. Stored as text, the values declared on Setting Definition `Rollup_Full_Recalc_Day`. Blank or unknown means Sunday. |
| `Nightly_Covered_From__c` | datetime | blank | Not a setting and not in the console: the start of the last nightly run that covered every change before it (R-R4b). Blank means the next night recalculates everything. Written by the engine only. |
