## 25O. Donor Segments

### Definition

A donor segment is a named, reusable list of people or organizations chosen by their giving
(feature G-28): lapsed donors, new donors, upgraders and the like, kept so they can be counted,
listed and exported for an email tool again next month. A segment is a Saved Query (Section 29D)
whose object is Contact (people) or Account (organizations). Giving adds no object for it: the
query document (R-SQ1) is the segment's criteria, Find edits and shares it, and Giving adds
starter templates, a count, a list and an export laid out for Mailchimp or Constant Contact.
Nothing is sent: BarnCRM writes a file and the person imports it.

### Attributes

One attribute is added to Contact and Account, so an upgrader can be found by a filter (a
query cannot compare two fields):

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Change From Last Year | currency, formula | no | Giving This Year minus Giving Last Year, a blank read as zero. Positive when the donor has already given more this year than all of last year. |

### Rules

**R-DS1 A segment is a saved query.** Every Saved Query of Contact or Account the person can
read (their own and those shared with them, as Find lists them) is shown as a segment. A
segment made from a template is saved as the person's own unshared Saved Query under the name
they give, replacing the query of their own saved query of that name if there is one (as R-SQ6
does) and keeping that one's sharing. Only the person's own saved query of that name whose
object is Contact or Account (a segment) is replaced: a Find saved query of the same name on
another object (for example a gift search) is left alone and the segment is saved beside it. Its criteria, columns and sharing are changed in Find; no
other copy exists.

**R-DS2 Starter templates are documented JSON.** The templates are one JSON document held in
`DonorSegmentTemplates`, in this format:

```
{
  "version": 1,
  "templates": [
    { "key": "lapsed", "objects": ["Contact", "Account"],
      "fields": ["Name", "Last_Gift_Date__c", "Giving_Last_Year__c", "Total_Giving__c"],
      "orderBy": { "field": "Giving_Last_Year__c", "direction": "DESC" },
      "filter": { "version": 1, "logic": "1 AND (2 OR 3)", "conditions": [ ... ] } }
  ]
}
```

`objects` says which of people and organizations a template applies to, `fields`, `orderBy`
and `filter` are the R-SQ1 and R-R2 parts, and names carry no namespace prefix: building a
segment qualifies each custom name for the org. The built document adds `Email` after `Name`
for people, a limit of 200 rows, and one more condition joined by AND to the template's logic:
`Deceased__c` equals false for people, `Is_Organization__c` equals true for organizations
(households are accounts too). A template's name is a custom label and its description is help
text in the Giving help catalog (`BarnHelp_Giving`, ADR-0164 help-text-json). The five
templates:

| Key | Name | Filter |
|---|---|---|
| `lapsed` | Lapsed Donors | Gave last year, nothing yet this year: `Giving_Last_Year__c` greater than 0 and `Giving_This_Year__c` equals 0 or is blank. |
| `new` | New Donors | First gift in the last 365 days (`First_Gift_Date__c`). |
| `upgraders` | Upgraders | Gave last year and has already given more this year: `Giving_Last_Year__c` greater than 0 and `Change_From_Last_Year__c` greater than 0. |
| `levelMovers` | Level Movers | Donor level changed in the last 90 days (`Donor_Level_Changed_Date__c`) from an earlier level (`Previous_Donor_Level__c` is not blank). |
| `majorProspects` | Major Gift Prospects | A largest gift of 1,000 or more or total giving of 5,000 or more (`Largest_Gift__c`, `Total_Giving__c`), and a gift in the last 730 days. |

The amounts and days are starting points, changed in Find once saved.

**R-DS3 Count.** `SELECT COUNT()` over the segment's filter as the person, through Find's
compiler (R-SQ2), counting at most 10,000; more is shown as "more than 10,000".

**R-DS4 List.** The segment's own columns, order and row count (at most 2,000), compiled and
run as Find's results grid runs them.

**R-DS5 Export.** Three layouts, each a CSV file built in the browser by Find's CSV writer
(R-SQ3 cell rules, UTF-8 with a byte-order mark), read in pages of 2,000 in Id order and
stopped at Export Row Limit (`Find_Export_Row_Limit__c`):

- **Mailchimp** (people only): Email Address, First Name, Last Name, Tags (the segment's
  name, so the import can tag the contacts).
- **Constant Contact** (people only): Email address, First name, Last name, Street address
  line 1, City, State/Province, Zip/Postal code, Country, from the mailing address.
- **All Columns**: the segment's own columns with their labels, for people or organizations.

The two email layouts read the segment's filter with three more conditions: `Email` is not
blank, `HasOptedOutOfEmail` equals false and `Deceased__c` equals false, so nobody who opted out
or has died is exported. A row whose email (compared without case or surrounding spaces)
already appeared is left out, since both tools refuse a repeated address in one import, and the
page says how many were. The header names follow each tool's own field names; both tools still
ask the person to confirm the columns when they import.

**R-DS6 Access.** Every action requires the `Find_And_Export_Records` custom permission
(R-SQ5): a segment is a Find query and an export is the sensitive act. Every read runs in user
mode, so a segment shows only the records, and the columns, the person can see. No settings
key: there is nothing to configure beyond the saved queries themselves.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Fields on Contact and Account** (shipped by Giving, read only):

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Change From Last Year | `Change_From_Last_Year__c` | Currency formula |

- **Apex:** `DonorSegmentTemplates` (the R-DS2 document and the build of a template into an
  R-SQ1 document), `DonorSegmentService` (count, list and export pages over Find's
  `QueryCompiler`), `DonorSegmentController` (the Donor Segments page).
- **Page:** the Donor Segments tab in the BarnCRM Fundraising app (`donorSegments`), with the
  browser-side layouts and duplicate check in the framework-free module `donorSegmentExport`.
- **Permission:** the page's controller is granted by Giving Admin, Giving Staff and Giving
  Read Only; the Find permission above is what opens it.

---

## 25P. Pledge Reminder Step

### Definition

One rung of the pledge reminder ladder (feature G-30): how many days before or after an
installment's due date it fires, and the email template or letter it sends. An organization
writes a few of them, for example an email a week ahead, a second email two weeks after, and a
letter a month after, and every open installment on an Active pledge walks the ladder.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | The step's name, shown on the page and kept on each reminder it makes. |
| Days From Due Date | integer | yes | Negative fires before the due date, zero on it, positive after it. |
| Channel | picklist(Email, Letter) | yes (defaults Email) | Email sends a templated email. Letter adds the installment to a merge file. |
| Email Template | text | conditional | The developer name of a standard `EmailTemplate`, required for an email step (the same by-name reference an Acknowledgment Rule uses, ADR-0032). The template merges the installment (`WhatId`) and the contact. |
| Active | boolean | yes (defaults true) | Whether the step fires. |

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Pledge_Reminder_Step__c`, Giving package. Name is text. Sharing ReadWrite.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Days From Due Date | `Days_From_Due__c` | Number(4, 0) |
| Channel | `Channel__c` | Picklist (Email, Letter) |
| Email Template | `Email_Template__c` | Text(80) |
| Active | `Active__c` | Checkbox |

### Rules

**R-PR1 One step per installment per run.** For each open installment (Scheduled, Overdue or
Partially paid, on an Active pledge) the run considers the active steps whose day, the due date
plus Days From Due Date, is today or within the previous 14 days. Only the one with the latest
day is made. An installment 20 days overdue with steps at 7 and 14 days gets the 14 day step.

**R-PR2 Only recent steps fire.** A step whose day passed more than 14 days ago is never made,
so a run that missed a night still sends, and turning the feature on does not send a final
notice about an installment that went overdue months ago. A step with Days From Due below zero
(a before-due heads-up) applies only while today is before the installment's Due Date: once the
due date arrives it no longer fires, even within its catch-up days.

**R-PR3 Nothing sends unless an administrator turned it on.** `Pledge_Reminders_Enabled__c` is
off by default (Section 25Q). With it off no reminder is made by hand or by the nightly run.

---

## 25Q. Pledge Reminder

### Definition

One pledge reminder, recorded (feature G-30): which installment, by which step, by email or
letter, to whom, and whether it went. It is the log the organization reads to answer "did we
remind them", and the claim that stops the same step reminding the same installment twice.

It reuses the acknowledgment feature's seams (Sections 25F to 25H): the Core `EmailSender`
interface, the template picked by developer name, the organization wide from address
(`Acknowledgment_From_Address__c`), the Send Acknowledgments permission, and the letter merge
file.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | computed | The record's identifier, assigned automatically. |
| Installment | reference(Installment) | yes | The installment being reminded about. Deleting it deletes its reminders. |
| Pledge | reference(Commitment) | no | The pledge the installment belongs to. |
| Step | reference(Pledge Reminder Step) | no | The step that fired; empty if the step was deleted since. |
| Step Name | text | no | The step's name when it fired. |
| Channel | picklist(Email, Letter) | yes | How it goes. An email step becomes a letter for a recipient with Email Opt Out set. |
| Status | picklist(Queued, Sent, Failed) | yes (defaults Queued) | A letter stays Queued until a person says the letters went. |
| Template | text | no | The email template used, by developer name. |
| Recipient Contact | reference(Contact) | no | The person it was addressed to: the pledge's donor, or the organization's primary contact. |
| Recipient Email | email | no | The address it went to. |
| Failure Reason | text | conditional | Why it did not go. |
| Sent On | datetime | conditional | When it went. |
| Days Overdue | integer | no | The installment's age past due when the reminder was made; negative before the due date. |
| Reminder Key | text | no | Installment and step identifiers, unique, held while the reminder stands and cleared when a send fails so the next run retries it. |
| Letter File Document Id | text | no | The merge file the letter is in. |

### Relationships

- **Pledge Reminder to Installment**, many to one (cascade).
- **Pledge Reminder to Pledge Reminder Step**, many to one (set null).
- **Pledge Reminder to Pledge** and **to Contact**, many to one (set null).

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Pledge_Reminder__c`, Giving package. Name is an auto number, `PR-{000000}`.
  Sharing Private.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Installment | `Installment__c` | Lookup to `Installment__c` |
| Pledge | `Commitment__c` | Lookup to `Commitment__c` |
| Step | `Step__c` | Lookup to `Pledge_Reminder_Step__c` |
| Step Name | `Step_Name__c` | Text(80) |
| Channel | `Channel__c` | Picklist (Email, Letter) |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist (Queued, Sent, Failed) |
| Template | `Template__c` | Text(80) |
| Recipient Contact | `Recipient_Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact |
| Recipient Email | `Recipient_Email__c` | Email |
| Failure Reason | `Failure_Reason__c` | Text(255) |
| Sent On | `Sent_On__c` | Date/Time |
| Days Overdue | `Days_Overdue__c` | Number(4, 0) |
| Reminder Key | `Reminder_Key__c` | Text(40), unique, external id |
| Letter File Document Id | `Letter_File_Document_Id__c` | Text(18) |

- **Settings keys** (on `Giving_Settings__c`, Section 21A): `Pledge_Reminders_Enabled__c`
  (boolean, false, whether reminders go out at all), `Pledge_Reminders_Last_Run__c` (datetime)
  and `Pledge_Reminders_Last_Run_Summary__c` (text, one sentence).

### Rules

**R-PR4 A reminder is claimed before it is sent.** The row, with its unique Reminder Key, is
written before anything goes, so a retried chunk or two people pressing Send produce one
reminder per installment and step. A failure before the send rolls the claims back. If the
platform refuses the whole send call, every claimed email row is marked Failed with the
platform's reason and its key cleared, and the next run tries again while the step is still
recent (R-PR2). If marking the rows Sent or Failed itself fails, each row is settled again on
its own with a fixed reason; no email row is left Queued holding its key.

**R-PR5 An email reaches only a person with an address who has not opted out or bounced.** The
recipient is the pledge's donor contact, or the organization's primary contact. A pledge with
nobody to email gets no row and is counted and named in one Error Log entry per chunk. A
recipient with Email Opt Out set, no email address, or an email address that bounced
(Salesforce's Email Bounced flag) is reminded by letter instead (R-AK13).

**R-PR6 A letter waits for a person.** The package writes a merge file of the queued letters
(pledge, installment, due date, amount still owed, days overdue, step, donor name, greeting,
address) and leaves the rows Queued until a person marks them sent, because Salesforce cannot
know whether anything was printed (R-AK11).

## 25R. Ask

Added by the solicitation pipeline (G-26, release 0.13, ADR-0153).

### Definition

One request for a gift that a fundraiser is working toward: who is being asked, for how much,
by when, who is responsible, where it stands, and how it ended. It is the Giving module's own
pipeline record, so a small development team can track its asks and moves without the standard
Opportunity object, which only the Mirror package may touch (ADR-0013). A gift is money that
arrived; an ask is the work that comes before it, and a won ask points at the gift or commitment
it produced.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | computed | The ask's identifier, assigned automatically. |
| Donor Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person being asked, where people are Contacts. |
| Donor Account | reference(Organization) | conditional | The organization or household being asked, or the person where people are person Accounts. |
| Stage | text | yes (defaults to the first stage) | Where the ask stands in the organization's own stage list (R-SO2). |
| Outcome | picklist(Open, Won, Declined, Withdrawn) | yes (defaults Open) | Whether the ask is still being worked, and how it ended (R-SO3). |
| Ask Amount | decimal | no | How much the donor is being, or was, asked for. |
| Target Date | date | no | When the fundraiser expects an answer. |
| Assigned To | reference(User) | yes | The staff member responsible for the ask: the record owner. |
| Next Step | text | no | The next thing to do, in a few words. |
| Next Ask Date | date | no | When to ask this donor again, usually set as the ask closes (R-SO7). |
| Fund | reference(Fund) | no | The fund the ask is for, carried onto the gift or commitment a win creates. |
| Appeal | reference(Appeal) | no | The appeal the ask belongs to, carried onto the gift or commitment a win creates. |
| Resulting Gift | reference(Gift) | no | The gift a won ask produced (R-SO5). |
| Resulting Commitment | reference(Commitment) | no | The pledge a won ask produced (R-SO5). |
| Stage Changed Date | date | computed | The day the ask reached its current stage (R-SO4). |
| Closed Date | date | computed | The day the outcome left Open; empty while the ask is open (R-SO3). |
| Sample Data | boolean | yes (defaults false) | True when the record was created by the sample data loader so it can be removed in one action. |

### Relationships

- **Ask to Contact or Organization**, many to one. Exactly one of the two is set, following the
  person reference convention in Section 4 (R-SO1).
- **Ask to Gift**, many to one, and **Ask to Commitment**, many to one. Usually one ask to one
  result; nothing stops two asks (a spouse's and a foundation's, say) pointing at the same gift.
- **Ask to Fund** and **Ask to Appeal**, many to one.

### Rules

**R-SO1 Exactly one donor.** An ask names a person or an organization, never both and never
neither. The rule is checked when an ask is created and whenever its donor changes, not on every
edit: deleting a donor clears the lookup (the ask is kept as a record of the work), and an ask
left with no donor can still be moved, closed or edited. In an org that stores people as accounts,
an ask saved with the contact behind a person account as its Donor Contact names the account as
Donor Account instead, before the rule is checked, so one person is one donor on the board and
their Next Ask Date is carried to one record (Section 4; QA-F3). An ask saved before this keeps
its donor.

**R-SO2 Stages are the organization's own list.** The stages are one org-wide setting, Ask Stages
(`Ask_Stages__c` on Giving Settings), an ordered list of names separated by semicolons; an empty
setting means the shipped list: Identified, Qualified, Cultivating, Ask Planned, Asked. An ask
saved with no stage gets the first one. A stage that is not in the list is refused when an ask is
created or its stage changes, and accepted on any other edit, so taking a stage out of the list
never blocks work on the asks still in it; the board shows those asks in a column of their own
until someone moves them. Stages describe progress only: how an ask ended is its outcome.

**R-SO3 Outcome is separate from stage.** An ask is Open while it is being worked, and Won,
Declined or Withdrawn once it ends (Withdrawn: the organization decided not to ask after all).
A closed ask keeps the stage it reached, so "declined at Cultivating" stays reportable. Closed
Date is filled with today when the outcome leaves Open and has no date, and cleared when the
outcome goes back to Open.

**R-SO4 Stage history.** Stage Changed Date is today when an ask is created and whenever its stage
changes, so the board can show how long an ask has sat where it is. The full history of Stage,
Outcome, Ask Amount and Target Date is kept by the platform's field history on the ask, not by a
package object.

**R-SO5 A win records what it produced.** Marking an ask Won from the board offers to record the
gift now, record a pledge, link a gift or commitment already entered for the same donor, or leave
the result for later. A gift is created through the same save as Quick Gift Entry, so every gift
rule applies (default allocation, posting lock, payment matching); a pledge is a Commitment of type
Pledge whose payments are generated as for any other. The donor, fund and appeal are carried from
the ask. The new record, the link and the outcome are saved together or not at all. A gift or
commitment linked later by editing the ask is accepted as it is.

**R-SO6 Pipeline totals.** The board totals the open asks of each stage (count and the sum of Ask
Amount) and, for the current fiscal year by Closed Date, the asks won (count and the sum of Ask
Amount) and declined (count). Totals are counted by the database, not from the cards on screen, so
they stay right when the board shows only the first cards of a long column.

**R-SO7 Next Ask Date is a hook, not a reminder.** It records when the organization means to ask
the donor again. The pipeline itself does nothing with it; when the ask closes, R-SO9 can carry it
onto the donor's Next Ask Date, which ask cadence (G-29) reads. Keeping it on the ask, set as the
ask closes, means the cadence work needs no change to this object.

**R-SO8 Erasing a person.** Erasing a person (Section 29H) clears Next Step on every ask for them
and sets each open one to Withdrawn, so no more work is planned about them. The asks are kept, like
their gifts, still pointing at the anonymized person.

**R-SO9 Open asks set the donor's Next Ask Date.** After an ask is created, deleted, restored from the Recycle Bin (it counts again, its Target
Date setting the donor's Next Ask Date as an insert does), or changes its Target Date, Outcome or donor, each donor it names (before and after the change) gets the
earliest Target Date among their open asks written into the donor's Next Ask Date (Section 25S),
so the ask cadence reminder and the Who Is Due list follow the pipeline with no second job. Open
asks without a Target Date are ignored. While a donor has an open ask with a Target Date, the
donor's Next Ask Date follows the earliest one, overwriting a date entered by hand. When the
change leaves a donor with no open ask with a Target Date, a donor Next Ask Date that is blank or
still holds the date the asks had set (the earliest open Target Date before the change) is
replaced: by the ask's own Next Ask Date (R-SO7) when this change closed the ask (Outcome left
Open) and that date is after today (the earliest, if several asks closed), otherwise by blank. A
date somebody entered or changed by hand is kept. Reads and the donor write run in system mode (ADR-0021: a package-owned
date computed from every open ask, whoever can see them); a donor that cannot be saved is
logged, and the ask's save is never refused for it.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Ask__c`, Giving package. Name is an auto number, `ASK-{000000}` (six digits, as Gift, Enrollment and most record
  numbers; eight until QA-F6, so asks created before keep their eight digit numbers). Sharing is
  Public Read/Write (`ReadWrite`): a small development team works one shared pipeline, and an
  organization that wants each fundraiser to see only their own asks sets it to Private in Setup
  (ADR-0153). Field history is on for Stage, Outcome, Ask Amount and Target Date (R-SO4).

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Donor Contact | `Donor_Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact, clears on delete |
| Donor Account | `Donor_Account__c` | Lookup to Account, clears on delete |
| Stage | `Stage__c` | Text(80) |
| Outcome | `Outcome__c` | Picklist, restricted: Open, Won, Declined, Withdrawn |
| Ask Amount | `Amount__c` | Currency(16, 2) |
| Target Date | `Target_Date__c` | Date |
| Assigned To | `OwnerId` | Owner (standard) |
| Next Step | `Next_Step__c` | Text(255) |
| Next Ask Date | `Next_Ask_Date__c` | Date |
| Fund | `Fund__c` | Lookup to `Fund__c`, clears on delete |
| Appeal | `Appeal__c` | Lookup to `Appeal__c`, clears on delete |
| Resulting Gift | `Gift__c` | Lookup to `Gift__c`, clears on delete |
| Resulting Commitment | `Commitment__c` | Lookup to `Commitment__c`, clears on delete |
| Stage Changed Date | `Stage_Changed_Date__c` | Date |
| Closed Date | `Closed_Date__c` | Date |
| Sample Data | `Sample_Data__c` | Checkbox |

- **Validation rule:** `Exactly_One_Donor` (R-SO1), on create and on a change of either donor
  field.
- **Automation:** one `Automation_Registry__mdt` row, `Ask_Stage_And_Dates`, handler
  `AskTriggerHandler`, order 10, always running: it fills the first stage, refuses a stage not in
  the list (R-SO2), and keeps Stage Changed Date and Closed Date in step (R-SO3, R-SO4). A
  second row, `Ask_Donor_Next_Ask_Date`, handler `AskNextAskDateHandler`, order 20, on by
  default and switchable in the automation console, runs after insert, update and delete and
  calls `AskDonorDateSync` (R-SO9).
- **Settings key** (on `Giving_Settings__c`, Section 21A): `Ask_Stages__c`.
- **Service:** `AskRules` (the stage list and R-SO2 to R-SO4), `AskSelector` (the board's
  queries, as the person), `AskPipelineController` (the board: totals, moving a stage, closing an
  ask, R-SO5 and R-SO6), `GivingPersonErasureExtension` (R-SO8), and the framework-free
  JavaScript module `askPipelineModel` (cards into columns, days in stage), which a WordPress block
  could reuse (plan Section 9.9).

## 25S. Ask cadence

### Definition

Two dates a fundraiser keeps on a donor, and the reminder the package makes from one of them.
Next Ask Date is when the donor should next be asked; Last Touch Date is when somebody last
spoke to them. Both are plain fields the staff edit, on Contact where people are Contacts and
on Account where the donor is an organization or a household. No new object: the reminder is
a Salesforce Task, so it appears in the owner's own task list.

### Attributes (on Contact and Account)

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Next Ask Date | date | no | The day the donor should next be asked. Entered by staff, or set from the donor's earliest open ask (R-SO9). |
| Last Touch Date | date | no | The day somebody last contacted the donor. Entered by staff; the package does not infer it. |
| Ask Reminder For Date | date | no | The Next Ask Date a reminder Task was last created for. Written only by the daily pass; it is how the pass knows not to create the same reminder twice (R-AC3). Read only to staff. |

### Rules

**R-AC1 Donor level dates only.** The reminder reads the two dates on the donor, never a date on
an ask. The solicitation pipeline (G-26) reaches it by writing the earliest open ask's Target
Date into the donor's Next Ask Date (R-SO9), so an open ask gets its reminder from this same
pass, with no second job.

**R-AC2 One switch, on by default.** `Ask_Reminders_Enabled__c` switches the daily pass on and
off for the whole organization. Off means the pass creates nothing; the Next Ask Date and Last
Touch Date fields and the Who Is Due list keep working. Only one ask reminder run goes at a
time: Run Now (Giving nightly jobs) and the nightly schedule start nothing while a run is
already queued or running. The setting is read again as a queued run processes, so turning Ask
Reminders off stops a run already queued (it makes no tasks and does not go on to the contacts
pass).

**R-AC3 One reminder per donor per date.** The pass creates a Task for a donor whose Next Ask
Date is today or earlier (within the catch up window of R-AC4) and whose Ask Reminder For Date
is not already that date, then stamps Ask Reminder For Date. Running the pass twice in a day,
or on every day after the date, creates nothing more. Changing the Next Ask Date to a new date
is a new ask and gets a new reminder.

**R-AC4 Catch up window.** A date more than 30 days in the past gets no Task: the first night
the setting is on must not bury staff under every stale date an old import left. Those donors
still appear in the Who Is Due list. A date inside the window that the pass missed (a job that
was stopped for a week) is caught up.

**R-AC5 The Task belongs to the donor's owner.** The Task is assigned to the owner of the
Contact or Account, related to the donor (Contact on Who and its Account on What, or the
Account on What for an account donor), dated the Next Ask Date, subject from a custom label. A donor whose
owner cannot take a Task is logged to Error Log, counted in the run summary, and left
unstamped so the next night tries again. The pass never deletes, closes or edits a Task.

**R-AC6 Who Is Due.** A list view named Who Is Due on Contact and one on Account list donors
whose Next Ask Date is today or earlier, whatever the setting says. A list view cannot carry a
sort in package metadata, so the list opens unsorted and a click on the Next Ask Date column sorts it.

### Salesforce implementation

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Next Ask Date | `Next_Ask_Date__c` | Date |
| Last Touch Date | `Last_Touch_Date__c` | Date |
| Ask Reminder For Date | `Ask_Reminder_For_Date__c` | Date |

- **Objects:** the three fields ship on both `Contact` and `Account`, Giving package.
- **Settings keys** (on `Giving_Settings__c`, Section 12): `Ask_Reminders_Enabled__c`,
  `Ask_Reminders_Last_Run__c`, `Ask_Reminders_Last_Run_Summary__c`.
- **Nightly job:** `AskReminderSchedulable` and `AskReminderBatch`, scheduled by
  `GivingScheduler` as the module's fourth job (`BarnCRM Giving Ask Reminders`, 03:30) and
  listed by `GivingNightlyJobProvider` for Health Check.
- **Service:** `AskReminderService`, `AskReminderSelector`, `AskReminderWriter`.

---

## 25T. Donor scoring

### Definition

Donor scoring (feature G-19) rates every donor on recency, frequency and monetary value (RFM)
and names a segment from the three scores. It adds no object. The inputs are rollups the
engine already runs (Section 26), the scores are plain attributes on Contact and Account, and
the cutoffs are org-wide settings with visible defaults, so a score is explainable from three
numbers printed beside it and an organization can change what "recent" means without code.

### Rules

- **R-DT1 Inputs are rollups.** Days since the last gift is a formula on `Last_Gift_Date__c`
  (Section 26). Gifts in the recent window and giving in the recent window are two new
  shipped rollups on each of Account, Contact and Household (Section 26): a COUNT and a SUM of
  gifts whose `Gift_Date__c` is in the last 730 days, with the ADR-0022 status filter and
  `Amount__c` greater than 0 for the count. The window is a `last n days` condition on the
  definition: an administrator changes 730 to any other day count in Rollup Builder, and the
  nightly rollup run keeps the totals right as the date moves.
- **R-DT2 Scores are 1 to 5.** Recency is 5 when the days since the last gift are at or under the
  first cutoff, 4 at or under the second, 3, 2, and 1 beyond the fourth. Frequency and Monetary
  are 5 when the value reaches the first cutoff, then 4, 3, 2 for the next three, and 1 below
  the fourth. A donor with no gift (empty `Last_Gift_Date__c`) has no scores and no segment,
  and any score or segment held is cleared. `RFM_Score__c` is the three scores added
  (3 to 15).
- **R-DT3 Cutoffs are settings.** `Donor_Score_Recency_Days__c` default `90,180,365,730`,
  `Donor_Score_Frequency_Gifts__c` default `6,4,2,1` and `Donor_Score_Monetary_Amount__c`
  default `5000,1000,250,50`, each four comma-separated numbers (days rise, gifts and amounts
  fall). A value that is not four numbers in order is ignored in favour of the default, so a
  typo never stops scoring. Settings are org-wide (Principle 3).
- **R-DT4 Segment.** The first rule that fits, with R, F and M the three scores: Champion
  (R 4 or 5, F 4 or 5, M 4 or 5); Loyal (R 3 or more, F 3 or more); Promising (R 4 or 5, F 1 or
  2); At Risk (R 1 or 2, and F 3 or more or M 4 or 5); Lapsed (R 1 or 2); Occasional (anything
  else). The segment is stored as its English name in `RFM_Segment__c` (text, ADR-0019).
- **R-DT5 When it runs.** In the before insert and before update of Account and Contact, in the
  same save that changes a rollup, as donor levels do (ADR-0028, R-DL6), and again in the
  nightly donor levels pass, because days since the last gift change with no record saved.
  Only a record whose five scoring values change is written by the pass. Two Automation
  Registry rows (`Donor_Score_Assignment_Account`, `Donor_Score_Assignment_Contact`) let the
  Automation page switch it off; they are on by default.
- **R-DT6 Find and segments.** Every attribute below is a normal field, so Find can filter,
  sort and show it, and two donor segment starter templates (Section 25O) use it: Champions
  and Slipping Donors (the At Risk segment).

## 25U. Wealth screening data

### Definition

What an outside wealth screening said about a person (G-32, D-156, release 1.5). BarnCRM buys
nothing and calls no screening service: the organization screens its list with a vendor of its
choice and loads the vendor's export with the packaged import template. Ratings vary by vendor,
so the two ratings are free text; the score is a number so it sorts and filters in Find.

- **R-WS1 Stored as received.** Nothing in BarnCRM reads, recalculates or rolls up these
  attributes; Find, reports and segments may filter on them.
- **R-WS2 Restricted to fundraisers.** Giving Admin and Giving Staff read and edit them; Giving
  Read Only does not see them, because screening data is a judgment about a person's means.
- **R-WS3 Import.** The shipped import template `wealth_screening` (one object, Update by a
  matching field: Contact by `Email`, or a person account by `PersonEmail` where people are
  accounts) fills the five attributes; a row whose email matches nobody is rejected, so screening
  data never creates a person.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Fields on Contact** (shipped by Giving, in the Giving Details section of the person page):

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Capacity Rating | `Capacity_Rating__c` | Text(80) |
| Affinity Rating | `Affinity_Rating__c` | Text(80) |
| Screening Score | `Screening_Score__c` | Number(8, 2) |
| Screening Date | `Screening_Date__c` | Date |
| Screening Source | `Screening_Source__c` | Text(80) |

- **Import templates:** `Import_Template_Default.Wealth_Screening_Contacts` (Person Mode
  Contacts, target `Contact`, Load Match Field `Email`) and
  `Import_Template_Default.Wealth_Screening_Person_Accounts` (Person Mode Person Accounts, target
  `Account`, Load Match Field `PersonEmail`, the `__pc` fields), both key `wealth_screening`, Load
  Operation Update by a matching field.

## 25V. Recurring donor health

### Definition

Recurring donor health (G-27, D-156, release 1.5) watches open-ended recurring gifts
(Commitments of Type Recurring) for the signs a sustainer is about to be lost: a failed charge, a
card about to expire, a cancellation at the payment processor, or a payment gone Overdue. The
processor's news arrives as Recurring Gift Event records, written by a Zapier recipe from the
organization's own processor account (the MIG-06 approach: Zapier's Salesforce Create Record or
Upsert action, no BarnCRM-held key) or by hand. BarnCRM calls no processor and stores no card
data: a card is known only by its expiry month.

### Attributes (Recurring Gift Event)

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event Number | auto number | yes | RGE-000001. |
| Commitment | reference to Commitment | no | The recurring gift. Found by R-RH1 when blank. Cleared when deleted. |
| Event Type | picklist | yes | Charge Failed (default), Charge Succeeded, Card Expiring, Card Updated or Cancelled. |
| Event Date | date | no | When it happened. Default today. |
| Subscription Id | text | no | The processor's id for the recurring gift. |
| Donor Email | email | no | The donor's email at the processor. |
| Card Expires | date | no | Last day of the card's expiry month. |
| Amount | currency | no | The charge's amount. |
| Detail | text | no | The processor's reason. |
| External Id | text | no | The processor's event id, so a repeated recipe records it once. |
| Match Status | picklist | no | Matched or Unmatched, set on save. |

### Rules

- **R-RH1 Matching.** Before an event is saved without a Commitment, the commitment whose
  Processor Subscription Id equals its Subscription Id (ignoring case) is taken; failing that,
  the one Active or Paused recurring gift whose donor Contact's Email equals its Donor Email. Two
  or more such gifts for one email match none. Match Status is Matched when a Commitment is set,
  else Unmatched; a person can choose the Commitment later (the Unmatched Events list view).
- **R-RH2 Applying.** When an event gains its Commitment (on insert, or when one is chosen
  later), it changes that commitment, oldest event first: Charge Failed adds 1 to Failed Charges
  (at most 999) and moves Last Failed Charge to its date if later; Charge Succeeded sets Failed
  Charges to 0 and clears Cancelled at Processor; Card Expiring sets Card Expires (its own date,
  or the end of the event's month); Card Updated sets Card Expires to its date or clears it;
  Cancelled sets Cancelled at Processor. The commitment's Status never changes: staff decide.
  The work runs in system mode (`RecurringGiftUpkeep`, Upkeep, ADR-0021) because the recipe's
  integration user cannot see private commitments. Registry row `Recurring_Gift_Event_Health`.
- **R-RH3 Save the Sustainer list.** Active recurring gifts with Failed Charges over 0, Card
  Expires on or before today plus `Recurring_Card_Expiry_Days__c` (default 60, 0 to 365), a
  Cancelled at Processor date, or an Overdue installment; at most 200, largest first; each with
  its reasons and a Create Follow-Up Task action (a Task for the person, about the gift and its
  donor). Read as the person (user mode).
- **R-RH4 Monthly recurring revenue.** Active recurring gifts' amounts by Frequency, turned into
  monthly values (Weekly x 52 / 12, Every two weeks x 26 / 12, Monthly x 1, Quarterly / 3, Twice a
  year / 6, Yearly / 12) in the page's framework-free model; at-risk revenue is the same sum over
  the R-RH3 list; and the Received gifts on recurring gifts for this month and the eleven before,
  by calendar month. Read as the person.
- **R-RH5 Payments subscriptions** (PAY-04, D-196; ADR-0218 `0218-payments-subscriptions.md`).
  When Payments tells Giving's listener of a subscription change on a commitment
  (`subscriptionsChanged`), the commitment's Processor Subscription Id and Processor Customer Id
  are filled when blank, and one Recurring Gift Event per change is upserted by External Id (the
  processor event's key): chargeSucceeded is Charge Succeeded, chargeFailed Charge Failed,
  cardUpdated Card Updated (with Card Expires), cancelled Cancelled. R-RH1 and R-RH2 then apply
  it. User mode, as the Payments processing administrator.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Recurring_Gift_Event__c`, name field Auto Number (RGE-{000000}), sharing Private
  (Giving Admin views all), tab Recurring Gift Events with All, My and Unmatched Events views.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Commitment | `Commitment__c` | Lookup(Commitment), Clear on delete |
| Event Type | `Event_Type__c` | Picklist (values above), restricted, required |
| Event Date | `Event_Date__c` | Date, default `TODAY()` |
| Subscription Id | `Subscription_Id__c` | Text(100) |
| Donor Email | `Donor_Email__c` | Email |
| Card Expires | `Card_Expires__c` | Date |
| Amount | `Amount__c` | Currency(16, 2) |
| Detail | `Detail__c` | Text(255) |
| External Id | `External_Id__c` | Text(100), unique, external ID |
| Match Status | `Match_Status__c` | Picklist (Unmatched, Matched), restricted |

- **Fields on `Commitment__c`** (Giving Admin edits them; Staff edit only the subscription id
  and read the customer id):

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Processor Subscription Id | `Processor_Subscription_Id__c` | Text(100), unique, external ID |
| Processor Customer Id | `Processor_Customer_Id__c` | Text(100), external ID: the processor's customer (Stripe `cus_...`), filled by R-RH5 or by an admin; Update Card needs it for Stripe |
| Failed Charges | `Failed_Charges__c` | Number(3, 0) |
| Last Failed Charge | `Last_Failed_Charge__c` | Date |
| Card Expires | `Card_Expires__c` | Date |
| Cancelled at Processor | `Processor_Cancelled__c` | Date |

- **Field on `Giving_Settings__c`:** Recurring Card Expiry Days, `Recurring_Card_Expiry_Days__c`,
  Number, default 60 (Setting Definition `Recurring_Card_Expiry_Days`, section Giving).
- **Code:** trigger `RecurringGiftEventTrigger`, handler `RecurringGiftEventHandler`, upkeep
  `RecurringGiftUpkeep`, page controller `RecurringHealthController`, components
  `recurringDonorHealth` and `recurringHealthModel`, tab and app page `Recurring_Donor_Health`.

## 26. Packaged default rollups

### Definition

The Rollup Definitions the Giving package ships and the attributes they write (plan
Sections 4.6 and 4.10, features G-02 and G-11). They are shipped as
`Rollup_Definition_Default__mdt` rows and materialized as `Rollup_Definition__c` records
on install (Section 13, R-R6). Every one of them is editable and deactivatable by the
admin.

The Giving package owns these target attributes, including the ones that sit on the
standard Account and Contact objects. An org without Giving installed has none of them,
which is Principle 3.

### Target scopes

Account carries households, organizations, and, in Person Account orgs, people. One
target attribute therefore serves three kinds of record, filled by three definitions whose
target record sets are disjoint (R-R8).

| Scope | Target entity | Target filter | Relationship path from Gift |
|---|---|---|---|
| Household | Account, record type Household | record type is Household | `Household__c` |
| Account (organization or person) | Account, any other record type | record type is not Household | `Donor_Account__c` |
| Contact | Contact | none | `Donor_Contact__c` |

Definition keys follow the scope: `Household_Total_Giving`, `Account_Total_Giving`,
`Contact_Total_Giving`, and so on, so a shipped default can be found by name.

### Giving totals on Account and Contact

Every definition here uses source entity Gift with the base filter `Status` in
`Received`, `Refunded`, `Written off`, and mode Both. The set, rather than `Status equals
Received`, is what makes R-R9 true: a refund is a negative gift whose own status is
Received while the original it reverses is moved to Refunded, so a filter that admitted
only Received would keep the negative rows and drop the positive one, and a fully refunded
gift would subtract itself twice (ADR-0022). Pending, Cancelled, Failed, and any other status that
does not represent money the organization holds stay outside the filter.

The rows that count, rather than add, carry `Amount__c` greater than 0 on top of that
status set, so that a gift given once and refunded in full reads as one gift and a total
of zero. A count and a sum here answer different questions on purpose: how many gifts this
donor gave, and what the organization is left holding.

| Target attribute | Aggregate | Source attribute | Extra filter | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Total_Giving__c` | SUM | `Amount__c` | none | The total of all gifts ever received from this donor, net of anything given back. |
| `Gift_Count__c` | COUNT | none | `Amount__c` greater than 0 | How many gifts this donor has given, counting a gift once whether or not it was later refunded. |
| `First_Gift_Date__c` | MIN | `Gift_Date__c` | `Amount__c` greater than 0 | The date of this donor's first gift, which is what "new donor" reporting counts from. |
| `Last_Gift_Date__c` | MAX | `Gift_Date__c` | `Amount__c` greater than 0 | The date of this donor's most recent gift, which is what lapsed-donor reporting counts from. |
| `Largest_Gift__c` | MAX | `Amount__c` | `Amount__c` greater than 0 | The largest single gift this donor has given. Without the amount condition a donor whose whole history was refunded would have a negative gift as their largest. |
| `Giving_This_Year__c` | SUM | `Amount__c` | fiscal year offset 0 | Total given in the current fiscal year. |
| `Giving_Last_Year__c` | SUM | `Amount__c` | fiscal year offset -1 | Total given in the previous fiscal year, which is the "LY" in LYBUNT. |
| `Giving_Two_Years_Ago__c` | SUM | `Amount__c` | fiscal year offset -2 | Total given two fiscal years ago, used by SYBUNT and retention reporting. |
| `Gifts_Last_Year__c` | COUNT | none | `Amount__c` greater than 0, fiscal year offset -1 | How many gifts this donor gave in the previous fiscal year, counting a gift once whether or not it was later refunded. A sum cannot answer this: a donor whose only gift last year was refunded inside that same year sums to zero while having given, and a donor whose sole activity last year was a refund of an older gift sums to less than zero while having given nothing. The retention reports read this attribute to tell a retained donor from a reactivated one (G-16, ADR-0026). |

### In-kind giving on Account and Contact

An in-kind gift is a Gift with Type In-kind whose Amount is zero (R-G12, ADR-0030), so it
adds nothing to any row in the table above and is excluded from every row that counts, which
is what keeps a donated vehicle out of Total Giving, out of Largest Gift, out of a donor level
(ADR-0028) and out of the retention reports (ADR-0026). These two rows are where it does
appear. They take the same status set and add `Type__c` equals `In-kind`.

| Target attribute | Aggregate | Source attribute | Extra filter | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `In_Kind_Value__c` | SUM | `Fair_Market_Value__c` | `Type__c` equals `In-kind` | What this donor's gifts of goods and services were worth, as the organization recorded them. Reported beside Total Giving and never added to it. |
| `In_Kind_Gift_Count__c` | COUNT | none | `Type__c` equals `In-kind` | How many gifts of goods and services this donor has given. There is no amount condition here, because a donor can give goods whose value they never told the organization and that gift still happened. |

Two further definitions on the same targets use different sources:

| Target attribute | Source | Aggregate | Source attribute | Filter | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Pledge_Balance__c` | Commitment | SUM | `Balance__c` | Type is Pledge and Status is Active or Paused | What this donor has promised and not yet paid. |
| `Total_Soft_Credits__c` | Soft Credit | SUM | `Amount__c` | gift status in the set above | The total this donor is recognized for without being hard credited. |
| `Soft_Credit_Count__c` | Soft Credit | COUNT | none | gift status in the set above, `Amount__c` greater than 0 | How many gifts this donor is recognized on. |

Relationship paths for the two non-Gift sources follow the same scope table, reading
`Household__c`, `Donor_Account__c`, or `Donor_Contact__c` on Commitment and `Account__c`
or `Contact__c` on Soft Credit.

### Totals on Giving objects

| Target entity | Target attribute | Source | Aggregate | Source attribute | Filter | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fund | `Total_Raised__c` | Gift Allocation | SUM | `Amount__c` | gift status in the set above | Everything ever designated to this fund. |
| Fund | `Total_Raised_This_Year__c` | Gift Allocation | SUM | `Amount__c` | gift status in the set above, fiscal year offset 0 | Designated to this fund in the current fiscal year. |
| Fund | `Gift_Count__c` | Gift Allocation | COUNT | none | gift status in the set above, `Amount__c` greater than 0 | How many gifts have been designated to this fund. |
| Fund | `Last_Gift_Date__c` | Gift Allocation | MAX | `Gift__r.Gift_Date__c` | gift status in the set above, `Amount__c` greater than 0 | The most recent gift to this fund. |
| Appeal | `Total_Raised__c` | Gift | SUM | `Amount__c` | status in the set above | What this appeal brought in. |
| Appeal | `Gift_Count__c` | Gift | COUNT | none | status in the set above, `Amount__c` greater than 0 | How many gifts responded to this appeal. |
| Commitment | `Paid_To_Date__c` | Gift | SUM | `Amount__c` | status in the set above | What has been paid against this commitment. |
| Installment | `Paid_Amount__c` | Gift | SUM | `Amount__c` | status in the set above | What has been paid against this scheduled installment. |

The fund definitions aggregate Gift Allocation but filter and read attributes on the
parent gift, written with a relationship-qualified name such as `Gift__r.Status__c`. That
is a requirement on the aggregation engine, recorded here so that it is part of the
vendoring evaluation in ADR-0011 rather than a surprise during the build. It has a second
half that R-R11 states: a change to the gift (its status, or its delete, which removes its
allocations without firing their trigger) has to mark the gift's funds for recalculation,
because the allocation row the fund total counts was not itself saved.

Appeal donor count is deliberately absent: counting distinct donors is not one of the
seven aggregates the engine offers (plan Section 4.10), and a grouped report answers it
without a new engine capability.

### Freshness: one last-calculated attribute per target entity

Every target entity carries a single `Rollups_Last_Calculated__c` datetime, written when
a rollup pass over that entity completes. There is not one per target attribute.

*Why.* The requirement is that a rollup shows when it was last calculated (Principle 2,
plan Section 4.10). Two questions are actually asked, and one attribute each answers
them: "when was this record's giving last recalculated", answered on the record page by
the entity-level attribute, and "when did this particular rollup last run", answered in
the settings console by Last Calculated on the Rollup Definition (R-R5). A per-attribute
sibling would add eleven datetime attributes to Account and eleven to Contact, all
carrying the same value whenever the pass that writes them is the same pass, which it is:
the engine recalculates a target record's definitions together. The cost of the choice is
that a single definition recalculated on its own moves the whole entity's stamp, which is
why the definition keeps its own Last Calculated as well.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Fields on Account** (shipped by Giving, shown read only in the Giving section of
  Giving's own Account and Contact record pages, ADR-0064 on the donor record pages):

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Total Giving | `Total_Giving__c` | Currency |
| Gift Count | `Gift_Count__c` | Number |
| First Gift Date | `First_Gift_Date__c` | Date |
| Last Gift Date | `Last_Gift_Date__c` | Date |
| Largest Gift | `Largest_Gift__c` | Currency |
| Giving This Year | `Giving_This_Year__c` | Currency |
| Giving Last Year | `Giving_Last_Year__c` | Currency |
| Giving Two Years Ago | `Giving_Two_Years_Ago__c` | Currency |
| Gifts Last Year | `Gifts_Last_Year__c` | Number |
| Pledge Balance | `Pledge_Balance__c` | Currency |
| Total Soft Credits | `Total_Soft_Credits__c` | Currency |
| Soft Credit Count | `Soft_Credit_Count__c` | Number |
| In-kind Value | `In_Kind_Value__c` | Currency |
| In-kind Gift Count | `In_Kind_Gift_Count__c` | Number |
| Totals Last Updated | `Rollups_Last_Calculated__c` | DateTime |

- **Fields on Contact** (shipped by Giving): the same fifteen API names, with the same
  types and the same definitions.

- **Fields on `Fund__c`:**

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Total Raised | `Total_Raised__c` | Currency |
| Total Raised This Year | `Total_Raised_This_Year__c` | Currency |
| Gift Count | `Gift_Count__c` | Number |
| Last Gift Date | `Last_Gift_Date__c` | Date |
| Totals Last Updated | `Rollups_Last_Calculated__c` | DateTime |

- **Fields on `Appeal__c`:**

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Total Raised | `Total_Raised__c` | Currency |
| Gift Count | `Gift_Count__c` | Number |
| Totals Last Updated | `Rollups_Last_Calculated__c` | DateTime |

- **Fields on `Commitment__c`:**

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Paid To Date | `Paid_To_Date__c` | Currency |
| Totals Last Updated | `Rollups_Last_Calculated__c` | DateTime |

- **Fields on `Installment__c`:**

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Paid Amount | `Paid_Amount__c` | Currency |
| Totals Last Updated | `Rollups_Last_Calculated__c` | DateTime |

- **Shipped defaults:** one `Rollup_Definition_Default__mdt` row per line in the tables
  above, per scope.
- **Service:** the Core engine (Section 14); Giving ships definitions, not engine code.

# Part E: Core additions for v0.3

These three entities are built by the v0.3 iteration in the Core package (features C-15,
C-16, C-17). They are constituent data: they describe how the people and organizations in
Part A are connected and where they live.

## 27. Relationship

### Definition

A connection between two people: spouses, a parent and a child, two colleagues, a friend
who introduced a donor (feature C-15, v0.3). This is the successor to NPSP's relationship
object, and its defining behavior is that the package maintains the other side of the
connection so that staff never enter it twice.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | computed | The relationship's identifier, assigned automatically. |
| Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person this relationship is described from, where people are Contacts. |
| Person Account | reference(Organization) | conditional | The person this relationship is described from, where people are person Accounts. |
| Related Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The other person, where people are Contacts. |
| Related Person Account | reference(Organization) | conditional | The other person, where people are person Accounts. |
| Type | picklist(Spouse, Partner, Parent, Child, Sibling, Grandparent, Grandchild, Friend, Colleague, Employer contact, Other) | yes | What the other person is to this person, read from this person's side. |
| Reciprocal Type | picklist(same values as Type) | computed | What this person is to the other one, filled from the shipped type mapping. |
| Status | picklist(Current, Former) | yes (defaults Current) | Whether the relationship still holds. |
| Start Date | date | no | When the relationship began. |
| End Date | date | no | When the relationship ended; empty means current. |
| Description | long text | no | Anything staff need to remember about the connection. |
| Reciprocal Relationship | reference(Relationship) | computed | The record that describes the same connection from the other person's side. |
| Is Reciprocal Managed | boolean | yes (defaults true) | Whether the package keeps the other side in step with this one. |

### Relationships

- **Relationship to each person**, many to one, to exactly one of Contact or Person
  Account on each side (Section 4 "Person references").
- **Relationship to Relationship**, one to one, pairing the two sides of one connection.

### Rules

**R-RL1 The package owns the other side.** Saving a relationship creates the mirrored
record from the other person's side, with the two sides pointing at each other and the
mirrored record's Type set from the reciprocal mapping. Editing Status, Start Date, End
Date, or Description on either side updates the other. Deleting either side deletes both.
This is controlled by the org's automatic reciprocal setting, which is on by default. On by
default means on before the org has saved anything: a checkbox on a hierarchy custom setting
reads back false, not its declared default, until Apex puts the shipped value on the record
(ADR-0035).

**R-RL2 Is Reciprocal Managed is the opt-out.** An org that needs the two sides to differ
(a relationship described asymmetrically, or one imported from a system that already holds
both sides) clears Is Reciprocal Managed on a record, and the package stops synchronizing
it while leaving the pairing reference intact.

**R-RL3 Reciprocal types come from shipped metadata.** The mapping from a type to its
reciprocal is `Relationship_Type__mdt` (Section 13). It ships gender-neutral: Parent maps
to Child, Child maps to Parent, Spouse and Partner and Sibling and Friend and Colleague
map to themselves, Grandparent maps to Grandchild, Employer contact maps to Colleague, and
anything unmapped maps to Other. No shipped row is gendered, so no reciprocal ever asserts
a person's gender from a relationship.

**R-RL4 A person is not related to themselves.** The two sides must be different people,
and a duplicate relationship of the same type between the same two people is rejected with
a message naming the existing record. A duplicate is counted in one direction: the same
person on this side, the same person on the other side, and the same type. A to B as
Parent and B to A as Parent are two different relationships and both are allowed, which is
what makes the mirrored record of A to B as Parent (B to A as Child) legal rather than a
duplicate of anything.

**R-RL4a Pairing prefers a record that is already there.** Before the package creates the
other side it looks for a relationship that is already the other side and is not paired
with anything: the two people the other way round, of exactly the reciprocal type, with no
Reciprocal Relationship set. Finding one, it pairs the two records instead of creating a
third. This is what makes an import that already carried both sides, and a restore from
the recycle bin that brought both sides back, settle into one pair rather than into
duplicates. A restore that brings back only one side first looks in the recycle bin for the
other side deleted with it and restores that record, so restoring one side, then the other,
or both at once, always ends with the original pair.

**R-RL5 Status follows the dates.** Setting End Date sets Status to Former on both sides.
Clearing it returns both to Current. Status is never left disagreeing with the dates.

**R-RL6 Relationships are not household membership.** A relationship never changes who is
in a household. Spouses in one household have both a household membership and, optionally,
a Spouse relationship, and the two mechanisms do not read each other.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Relationship__c`, auto-number Name with format `RL-{000000}`.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Contact | `Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact |
| Person Account | `Person_Account__c` | Lookup to Account |
| Related Contact | `Related_Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact |
| Related Person Account | `Related_Person_Account__c` | Lookup to Account |
| Type | `Type__c` | Picklist: Spouse, Partner, Parent, Child, Sibling, Grandparent, Grandchild, Friend, Colleague, Employer contact, Other |
| Reciprocal Type | `Reciprocal_Type__c` | Picklist, same values as `Type__c`, not restricted: BarnCRM always writes it from the relationship type mapping, whose values the custom metadata page checks against `Type__c`, so a custom type added to `Type__c` alone saves |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist: Current, Former |
| Start Date | `Start_Date__c` | Date |
| End Date | `End_Date__c` | Date |
| Description | `Description__c` | Long Text Area |
| Reciprocal Relationship | `Reciprocal_Relationship__c` | Lookup to `Relationship__c` |
| Is Reciprocal Managed | `Is_Reciprocal_Managed__c` | Checkbox |
| Sample Data | `Sample_Data__c` | Checkbox (v0.4) |

- **Shipped defaults:** `Relationship_Type__mdt` (Section 13).
- **Settings key:** `Relationship_Auto_Reciprocal__c` (Section 12), registered in
  `SettingsService.SHIPPED_DEFAULTS` so a fresh org gets it switched on (ADR-0035).
- **Service:** `RelationshipService`, `RelationshipDomain`, `RelationshipSelector`.
- **Automation:** two registry rows on `Relationship__c`. `Relationship_Validation`, handler
  `RelationshipValidationHandler`, execution order 10, holds the defaults and the rules
  (R-RL3, R-RL4, R-RL5). `Relationship_Reciprocal`, handler
  `RelationshipMaintenanceHandler`, execution order 30, writes and removes the other side.
  Two rows so that switching the upkeep off from the Automation page leaves every rule
  running. The service stands both automations down by name while it writes the other side,
  which is how a mirrored write does not re-enter the trigger that made it and is not
  checked a second time against the record it mirrors.

## 28. Affiliation

### Definition

A person's connection to an organization: an employee, a board member, a congregant, a
staff contact at a funder (feature C-16, v0.3). This is the successor to NPSP's
affiliation object, and it is what lets a person be related to an organization without
leaving their household.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | computed | The affiliation's identifier, assigned automatically. |
| Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person, where people are Contacts. |
| Person Account | reference(Organization) | conditional | The person, where people are person Accounts. |
| Organization | reference(Organization) | yes | The organization the person is connected to. |
| Role | text | no | What the person does there, in the org's own words, for example "Board chair". |
| Status | picklist(Current, Former) | yes (defaults Current) | Whether the person is still connected to the organization. |
| Is Primary | boolean | yes (defaults false) | Marks the organization this person is chiefly associated with. |
| Start Date | date | no | When the connection began. |
| End Date | date | no | When the connection ended; empty means current. |
| Description | long text | no | Anything staff need to remember about the connection. |

### Relationships

- **Affiliation to the person**, many to one, to exactly one of Contact or Person Account
  (Section 4 "Person references").
- **Affiliation to Organization**, many to one.
- **Contact to Primary Affiliation**, many to one: the person's primary organization,
  maintained by the package (R-AF2).

### Rules

**R-AF1 One person, one organization, dated.** A person may have many affiliations at
once, and the same person and organization may be affiliated more than once over time, so
long as the date ranges do not overlap for the same role.

**R-AF2 One primary per person.** At most one current affiliation per person has Is
Primary true. Setting it on a second clears the first, and the package mirrors the
primary organization to the person's Primary Affiliation reference so that a list view or
a mail merge can show an employer without a subquery.

**R-AF3 Affiliation is not household membership.** Setting an affiliation never changes
the person's household or their Account reference in contact mode. This is the mistake the
entity exists to prevent: a donor who works at a foundation is still a member of their
household.

**R-AF4 Status follows the dates.** As R-RL5: setting End Date sets Status to Former, and
a former affiliation is never the primary one.

**R-AF5 Created by the importer.** A spreadsheet row that names an employer creates or
matches an affiliation (R-IR1), which is how most affiliations in a converted org arrive. A
people import links the row's first person to the row's organization once both are resolved,
after the people are saved: a current affiliation of that person with that organization is
matched and nothing is written; otherwise one is created with the row's `Affiliation`
attributes, through the ordinary rules (R-AF1 to R-AF4, so it is primary only when R-AF2 makes
it so). Two rows of a chunk naming the same pair make one. The dry run counts the row as
creating something and writes nothing, unless an earlier row of the file, in its chunk or an
earlier one, would link the same pair, which the commit then finds (R-IB12): a person or an
organization the run would create is told apart by the key a later row finds it by. A created affiliation carries no batch tag: it is
journaled as Created (R-IJ3) and an undo deletes it before the people and organizations. The
second person is not linked, as NPSP's import links only its first contact with its first
account.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Affiliation__c`, auto-number Name with format `AF-{000000}`.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Contact | `Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact |
| Person Account | `Person_Account__c` | Lookup to Account |
| Organization | `Organization__c` | Lookup to Account |
| Role | `Role__c` | Text |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist: Current, Former |
| Is Primary | `Is_Primary__c` | Checkbox |
| Start Date | `Start_Date__c` | Date |
| End Date | `End_Date__c` | Date |
| Description | `Description__c` | Long Text Area |
| Sample Data | `Sample_Data__c` | Checkbox (v0.4) |

- **Field on Contact:** `Primary_Affiliation__c`, a Lookup to Account, maintained by the
  package (R-AF2). In Person Account orgs the same attribute exists on Account as
  `Primary_Affiliation__c`, added there with the other person attributes (Section 4
  "Person references"). It holds the **organization**, not the Affiliation record: the
  point of the field is that a list view or a mail merge can show an employer without a
  subquery, and an Affiliation id would not do that. The label an admin sees is Primary
  Affiliation because that is the nonprofit's word for it.
- **Automation:** two registry rows on `Affiliation__c`. `Affiliation_Validation`, handler
  `AffiliationValidationHandler`, execution order 10, holds the defaults and the rules
  (R-AF1, R-AF4). `Affiliation_Primary`, handler `AffiliationMaintenanceHandler`, execution
  order 30, settles who is primary. Two rows so that switching the upkeep off from the
  Automation page leaves every rule running. The service stands both automations down by
  name while it clears the primary flag from a person's other affiliations.
- **Service:** `AffiliationService`, `AffiliationDomain`.
