## 29. Address

### Definition

A place a household, an organization, or a person receives mail (plan Section 4.7,
feature C-17). Addresses exist as records rather than as fields so that a household can
have more than one, so that a seasonal address can take over automatically, and so that
history is not lost when someone moves.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | computed | The address's identifier, assigned automatically. |
| Account | reference(Household) | conditional | The household or organization this address belongs to. |
| Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person this address belongs to, for an address that is theirs rather than their household's. |
| Person Account | reference(Organization) | conditional | The person this address belongs to, where people are person Accounts. |
| Type | picklist(Home, Work, Mailing, Seasonal, Other) | yes | What kind of address this is. |
| Street | long text | no | The street address, including any second line. |
| City | text | no | The city or town. |
| State | text | no | The state, province, or region. |
| Postal Code | text | no | The postal or ZIP code. |
| Country | text | no | The country. |
| Seasonal Start Month | integer | conditional | The month a seasonal address takes over; required when Type is Seasonal. |
| Seasonal Start Day | integer | conditional | The day of that month; required when Type is Seasonal. |
| Seasonal End Month | integer | conditional | The month a seasonal address stops being used; required when Type is Seasonal. |
| Seasonal End Day | integer | conditional | The day of that month; required when Type is Seasonal. |
| Primary | boolean | yes (defaults false) | Marks the address currently written to the standard address fields (API name `Is_Default__c`). |
| Verification Status | picklist(Unverified, Verified, Failed) | yes (defaults Unverified) | Whether an address verification service has confirmed this address. |
| Latest Verified Date | date | no | When verification last succeeded. |
| Replaced By Seasonal | boolean | yes (defaults false) | Marks the address the seasonal swap displaced, so the job knows which address to put back when the season ends. |
| Status | picklist(Current, Former, Undeliverable) | no (a new address is saved Current) | Whether the address is in use now, was used before, or has mail coming back (R-AD10). A blank reads as Current. |
| Start Date | date | no | The day this address came into use, set on a move (R-AD10). |
| End Date | date | no | The day this address stopped being used, set on a move (R-AD10). |
| Deleted With | text (40) | no | The owner this address was deleted with, as its lookup field's name and the owner's Id (`Contact__c:003...`), so restoring the owner restores the address (R-AD11). Written by BarnCRM only, never shown on a page. |

### Relationships

- **Address to its owner**, many to one, to exactly one of Account, Contact, or Person
  Account (R-AD1).
- Addresses have no relationship to gifts or receipts: a receipt reads the owner's primary
  address at the time it is issued and stores the text it printed (v0.4, G-13).

### Rules

**R-AD1 One owner.** Exactly one of Account, Contact, or Person Account is set. An address
owned by an account is the household's or the organization's; an address owned by a person
is theirs alone and does not affect their household.

**R-AD2 One primary per owner.** At most one address per owner has Primary true.
Setting it on a second clears the first. Within one save that marks several addresses of
one owner as primary, the last of them keeps the flag. Clearing the flag on an owner's only
primary, with no other put in use in the same save, is refused (label
`Core_Address_CannotUntickOnlyDefault`). When the primary is deleted, the newest remaining
address that is not Seasonal is promoted, and a Seasonal one only when nothing else is left.
The first address added from the address card to an owner with none is saved as primary.

**R-AD3 Primary propagation.** The primary address is copied to the standard address
fields, so every standard feature, report, and third-party app keeps working: to the
Account's billing address for a household or an organization, and to the Contact's mailing
address for a person. The copy happens on save and on the seasonal swap. A household's or
an organization's primary is also copied to the mailing address of each current member of
the household, except two, who keep the address they have, on save and on the seasonal swap
alike:

- a member stored as a Contact who has a primary address of their own (one owned through
  Contact, R-AD1), such as the one R-AD5's personal address behavior gives them. This is how
  one person lives apart from their household, with no field to say so. A member held as a
  Person Account is not asked this, because every person account carries an address of its
  own captured from its mailing fields (R-AD5).
- in junction mode, a member for whom this household is not their household (R-M3: their
  primary membership, else their earliest current one).

Where the org's Address Updates setting is "Nobody moves until you choose" (R-AD5), a
household's or an organization's new primary is written to its own billing fields only, on
save, on a billing edit and when a primary is deleted alike: it reaches the members above
only on a move someone chose on the address card (R-AD9) or on the seasonal swap (R-AD4),
which moves members in every setting (ADR-0140).

The standard fields are not where a change is kept, but a change made there is captured
rather than lost: a person's mailing address under R-AD5, and a household's or an
organization's billing address, on insert and when it changes afterwards, as a new primary
address of type Home (Work for an organization), the old one kept as history (R-AD7). An
emptied billing address, one the primary already holds, and BarnCRM's own copy are not
captured, and neither is a household that carries a native Nonprofit Cloud household group,
whose standard fields this rule never writes (product-plan Section 11.2 item 9).

Where people are person accounts, the person's mailing fields are written instead of a
contact's. An account is written that way only when its record type is a person type. In a
person accounts org those mailing fields exist on every account record, but only a person
account will accept a value in one, so the org's shape is not the question: the record's
is. A household member, or an owner named in Person Account, that turns out to be a
household or an organization is left out of the copy rather than written and refused, which
would refuse the address the user was saving along with it.

**R-AD4 Seasonal swap.** A daily scheduled job makes the seasonal address the primary
while today falls inside its range, and restores the previous primary when the range ends.
Ranges may wrap the end of the year, so a November to March range is one range and not two.
A range is inclusive at both ends: an address used from November 1 to March 31 is in use on
November 1 and on March 31, and out of use on April 1.

The job works one owner at a time and does exactly one of four things for each:

1. A seasonal address is in season and is not the primary: the current primary is marked
   Replaced By Seasonal, its primary flag is cleared, and the seasonal address becomes the
   primary.
2. The primary is a seasonal address whose season has ended: the address marked Replaced By
   Seasonal becomes the primary again and that mark is cleared. If no address carries the
   mark, the most recently created address that is not seasonal is promoted instead, and if
   the owner has no other address the seasonal one stays in place rather than leaving the
   owner with no address at all.
3. Two seasonal addresses are in season on the same day, which is a data entry mistake: the
   oldest wins so the outcome does not change from night to night, and the run records the
   collision in the Error Log rather than choosing silently.
4. Nothing to do: the right address is already the primary.

Nothing else on the address is touched, and the propagation to the standard address fields
(R-AD3) is the address automation's work rather than the job's, so switching that automation
off stops the copy without stopping the swap.

**R-AD8 The run is visible.** Every run records when it finished and what it did (how many
addresses moved in, how many moved back, how many failed), and both are shown on the Hub
home page and on the Addresses page of the settings console, where the schedule is also
started and stopped. A failure on one owner is written to the Error Log and the run
continues: one household with an unreachable address never stops the rest of the org
swapping. The job reads and writes in system mode, because a nightly reconciliation of
package owned data must not depend on what the person who happened to schedule it can see
(ADR-0027).

**R-AD5 Address Updates.** When a person's address is edited, the org's Address Updates
setting (`Contact_Address_Change_Behavior__c`) decides what happens, and it also decides
whether a household's change reaches its members on its own (R-AD3). Three choices
(ADR-0140):

- **Everyone in the household moves together** (`Update household`, the shipped choice, and
  what a blank or unknown value means): the edit becomes the household's new primary
  address, so everyone in the household without an address of their own moves with it.
- **Only that person moves** (`Create personal address`): the edit becomes a primary address
  of that person's own. A household change still reaches every member with no address of
  their own.
- **Nobody moves until you choose** (`Manual`): the edit stays that person's own, as above,
  and a household change reaches its members only when someone chooses to move them (R-AD9),
  or through the seasonal swap, which still reaches every member with no address of their
  own (R-AD4).

The setting is explained in those words in the settings console, not in terms of objects,
and the console shows a blank as the shipped choice, never an empty box.

**R-AD6 Verification is a placeholder.** Verification Status and Latest Verified Date are
never written by Core's code. They exist so that a verification app can write them and so
that a report can find unverified addresses. The optional Address Verification module (C-46,
29AV1, R-AV1 to R-AV4) is such an app; without it, or with its handler switched off, any
third-party app can own them.

**R-AD7 History is kept.** Moving a household creates a new address and clears the old
one's primary flag. The old address is not deleted, so a mailing sent last year can still
be explained. R-AD10 records when it stopped being used.

**R-AD10 Status, start and end dates (AH1).** Every address is Current, Former or
Undeliverable (`Status__c`). An address saved with no status is saved Current.

- **A move ends the old address.** When a new address is added as an owner's primary and it
  is a different place (street, city and postal code) from the primary it replaces, the
  replaced primary gets End Date today and, if it was Current, Status Former; the new address
  gets Start Date today when it has none. This covers every way a new primary is added: the
  card with Primary ticked, a changed standard address captured under R-AD3 and R-AD5, Use for
  Whole Household, and an import. A person's own primary that Use for Whole Household or a
  tick in Update Everyone's Address releases (R-AD9) is ended the same way when it is a
  different place from the household's primary they now take.
- **Not a move:** choosing an address already on file as the primary (Set as Primary), the
  seasonal swap (R-AD4), the promotion after a primary is deleted (R-AD2), and a merge keeping
  one primary. None of them ends or starts anything. A Seasonal address is never ended by a
  move: when the primary a move replaces is Seasonal, the address waiting to come back (marked
  Replaced By Seasonal) is the one ended, and its mark is cleared.
- **Undeliverable is a person's call.** Only a person sets or clears it, from the card's status
  menu or the address record; BarnCRM never does. A move ending an Undeliverable address sets
  its End Date and leaves the status.
- **A Former address is not put back in use on its own.** The seasonal swap treats a Former
  seasonal address as out of season and never restores a Former address; a deleted primary's
  replacement is a Former address only when nothing else is left. An address made primary
  while Former becomes Current again and its End Date is cleared, so the primary is never
  Former.
- **Existing addresses are not rewritten.** An address saved before Status existed has a blank
  status, which every reader treats as Current; its next save fills in Current. No install or
  upgrade step backfills it, because nothing on file says which old address was left behind,
  and calling one Former would be a guess. Anyone can mark an old address Former from the card.
- **The card.** The Addresses card lists the Current and Undeliverable addresses first, the
  primary at the top, then a Former Addresses group, collapsed, holding every address that is
  Former or whose End Date has passed (never the primary), each with its date range. An
  Undeliverable address carries a badge, and an Undeliverable primary is flagged on the card.
  The admin-chosen Address Card Fields setting (`Address_Card_Fields__c`, Section 12) adds
  fields to every address on the card, each shown only to a user who can read it.
- **The check.** Data Hygiene, and Find through it, lists the primary addresses marked
  Undeliverable: the households, organizations and people whose mail is coming back.

**R-AD11 Addresses follow their owner to the Recycle Bin (D-184).** When a household,
organization, person or person account is deleted, the Addresses of Deleted Records setting
(`Address_Delete_Behavior__c`) decides what happens to its addresses. Delete (the default):
they are deleted with it. An address has one owner (R-AD1), so no other record's address is
ever touched. In an org where a household's people are its contacts, deleting the household
deletes those people too, and their own addresses go with them. Keep: they stay, with the
lookup the platform cleared, as before the setting. Rules that hold either way:

- **A merge is not a delete.** The platform moves the losing record's addresses to the
  survivor, and they stay there.
- **Restoring restores them.** Before the delete each address is marked with its owner
  (`Deleted_With__c`), because the platform clears the lookup and does not put it back.
  Restoring the owner from the Recycle Bin restores the addresses marked with it and links
  them again, whatever the setting says by then.
- **System mode, as package upkeep of dependent rows.** The person who deletes the owner need
  not be able to delete addresses themselves (ADR-0021); a failure is logged and never blocks
  the delete.
- **BarnCRM's own deletes are unchanged.** The empty household tidy-up (R-H12a) and erasure
  (R-ER2) already delete the addresses themselves.
- **Part of Addresses.** Two automations, Addresses of a deleted person and Addresses of a
  deleted account, belong to the Addresses feature (ADR-0124) and can be switched off on the
  Automation page like any other.

**R-AD9 Moving a household on purpose.** The address card offers two moves, in every Address
Updates setting (ADR-0140). Each checks the user's own access as any address write does,
works for many records in one save, and keeps what it replaces as history (R-AD7):

- On a person's own address, **Use for Whole Household** gives the person's household a new
  primary address copied from it (in junction mode their household under R-M3; where they
  are a current member of more than one, the user picks which). A person stored as a Contact
  stops having a primary address of their own, so they follow the household again; their
  addresses stay on file. Every member who takes the household's address (R-AD3) moves.
- On a household's primary address, **Update Everyone's Address** copies it to every member
  who takes the household's address (R-AD3), after a confirmation that lists them and the
  members with a primary address of their own. Those are left alone unless ticked; a ticked
  member's own primary stops being primary, kept as history, and they take the household's
  address from then on. A member for whom this is not their household is not listed.
- Both chosen moves leave out a member marked deceased: they are not moved and not listed.
  The automatic copy of R-AD3 is unchanged. In the confirmation, members who share a name are
  told apart by their birthdate, or their email when there is no birthdate, where the user
  can read it.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Address__c`, auto-number Name with format `AD-{000000}`.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Account | `Account__c` | Lookup to Account |
| Contact | `Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact |
| Person Account | `Person_Account__c` | Lookup to Account |
| Type | `Type__c` | Picklist: Home, Work, Mailing, Seasonal, Other |
| Street | `Street__c` | Text Area |
| City | `City__c` | Text |
| State | `State__c` | Text |
| Postal Code | `Postal_Code__c` | Text |
| Country | `Country__c` | Text |
| Seasonal Start Month | `Seasonal_Start_Month__c` | Number (0 decimals) |
| Seasonal Start Day | `Seasonal_Start_Day__c` | Number (0 decimals) |
| Seasonal End Month | `Seasonal_End_Month__c` | Number (0 decimals) |
| Seasonal End Day | `Seasonal_End_Day__c` | Number (0 decimals) |
| Primary | `Is_Default__c` | Checkbox |
| Verification Status | `Verification_Status__c` | Picklist: Unverified, Verified, Failed |
| Latest Verified Date | `Latest_Verified_Date__c` | Date |
| Replaced By Seasonal | `Replaced_By_Seasonal__c` | Checkbox |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist: Current (default), Former, Undeliverable |
| Start Date | `Start_Date__c` | Date |
| End Date | `End_Date__c` | Date |
| Deleted With | `Deleted_With__c` | Text (40) |
| Match Key | `Match_Key__c` | Text (100), External ID (indexed), not unique |

- **Match key (D-200 P6):** `Match_Key__c` holds the normalized postal code, a bar, and the
  first street word that normalization leaves as written (usually the house number), for
  example `02139|77`. Set before every insert and update by `AddressMatchKeyHandler`, an
  automation that always runs (registry row `Address_Match_Key`), so no pause or bypass leaves
  it stale; never edited by a person. The duplicate scan and import matching read the Address
  match sources by `Match_Key__c IN :keys`, an index read, instead of a LIKE over every
  address, and compare the rows exactly as before. Only once `Match_Keys_Filled__c` is true:
  until then they fall back to the LIKE read. `AddressMatchKeyBatch` fills the keys of
  addresses saved before the field existed; Health Check's **Match Keys Not Filled** finding
  starts it.
- **Standard fields written:** `Account.BillingStreet`, `BillingCity`, `BillingState`,
  `BillingPostalCode`, `BillingCountry`; `Contact.MailingStreet`, `MailingCity`,
  `MailingState`, `MailingPostalCode`, `MailingCountry`.
- **Settings keys:** `Contact_Address_Change_Behavior__c`, `Address_Delete_Behavior__c`, `Seasonal_Address_Last_Run__c`,
  `Seasonal_Address_Last_Run_Summary__c`, `Address_Card_Fields__c` (Section 12).
- **Service:** `AddressService`, `AddressTriggerHandler`, `AddressSelector` (the
  Addresses card reads and saves through Lightning Data Service, ADR-0093 record reads
  through Lightning Data Service, and calls `AddressMoveController` only for the two
  household moves of R-AD9); and for the seasonal swap
  `SeasonalAddressService`,
  `SeasonalAddressSelector`, `SeasonalAddressWriter`, `SeasonalAddressBatch`,
  `SeasonalAddressScheduler`, `SeasonalAddressController`.

## 29A. Duplicate Dismissal

### Definition

A record of a person deciding that two records the duplicate scan proposed are not the same
household or the same person (plan Section 5.1, feature C-20). It exists so that a decision a
person already made is not asked again the next time the scan runs.

Nothing else about duplicates is stored here. The suggestions themselves are platform
records: the platform's duplicate rules write a Duplicate Record Set and its Duplicate Record
Items, and the BarnCRM scan writes the same two standard objects for duplicates that were
already in the org before anybody looked. BarnCRM adds no object for a suggestion and no
copy of what the platform found (R-DP1); its own matching is limited to related-record values
through match sources, and a Duplicate Dismissal row of Kind Match Reason says which source
found a pair (R-DP6).

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | computed | The dismissal's identifier, assigned automatically. |
| Pair Key | text | yes | The two record identifiers, sorted and joined, that a person said are not duplicates. Unique, so the same pair is dismissed once. |
| Reason | text | no | Why they are not duplicates, in the words of the person who decided: "twin sisters at the same address". |

### Relationships

- **Duplicate Dismissal to the two records it is about**, by identifier rather than by
  lookup. The pair is two Contacts or two Accounts, and one lookup field cannot point at
  either object, so the identifiers are held as text.

### Rules

**R-DP1 The platform detects, BarnCRM reviews.** What counts as the same person or the
same household is decided by the org's own active duplicate rules for Contact and Account,
and nothing else. BarnCRM ships no matching rule and no duplicate rule (ADR-0050): every
org starts with the platform's standard rules for both objects switched on, and an
administrator's own rules are used exactly as written. No packaged code compares two records
field by field to decide whether they are duplicates. There are two additions: R-DP6, values on
related records the rules cannot see, compared only through the configured match sources; and
R-DP7, people's names scored by the shared fuzzy scorer, household aware (ADR-0145,
`0145-advanced-duplicate-management.md`).

**R-DP2 Only pairs BarnCRM can act on are proposed.** A suggestion is two people, or two
households. A pair of accounts where either side is not a household (an organization, or a
person stored as an account) is passed over, because the household merge (R-H13) is the only
account merge BarnCRM performs and a suggestion nobody can act on here is noise. A household
that also carries a Nonprofit Cloud household group (`PartyRelationshipGroup`) is passed over
and refused by the merge (ADR-0036), and so is a pair naming a person account's contact half,
which the platform cannot merge with a contact. The panel applies the same rule to sets a
duplicate rule wrote on save, and hides a set whose every pair is dismissed (R-DP5).

**R-DP3 The scan finds what the rules would have found.** A duplicate rule runs when a record
is saved, so records already in the org, and records saved past an alert, are never compared
with each other. The scan asks the platform to evaluate its active duplicate rules against
the people and households that already exist, fifty records at a time, and writes a
Duplicate Record Set of exactly two items for each new pair it is given back. It never
proposes a pair that is already in a suggestion, and never one that has been dismissed. It is
started by a person from BarnCRM Settings and is not scheduled. It refuses to start when no
duplicate rule for Contact or Account is active, because a scan with nothing to evaluate would
report a clean org rather than an org nobody is checking.

**R-DP4 A merge is one pair at a time, previewed, and confirmed by a person.** No packaged
code merges or deletes records in bulk, and no automation merges anything, with one exception:
an administrator's previewed auto-merge of exact people matches, journaled and undoable
(R-DP9, R-DP10). Two households are
merged by the household merge (R-H13) and nothing else. Two people are merged with the
platform's own merge, reached from the Potential Duplicates card on the person's record page,
because the platform already carries related records across safely.

**R-DP5 A dismissal is remembered, a suggestion is not.** Dismissing a suggestion writes a
Duplicate Dismissal for each pair in it and then deletes its Duplicate Record Set, which
removes the grouping and never touches the records. An administrator can delete a dismissal,
which is how a pair is put back in front of a reviewer. A household merge from the review
page deletes the suggestion without a dismissal, because the pair no longer exists.

**R-DP6 Related records add pairs the rules cannot see** (ADR-0133,
`0133-related-record-matching.md`). In each chunk of the scan, after the rules are asked, the
active match sources (`Match_Source__mdt`, Section 13) that can point at the chunk's object are
read: each record's values on the source are normalized, the other records holding the same
value are found, and each pair is added with a reason naming the source ("Same email on
Contact Point Email"). A parent resolves to a Contact or an Account as itself, an Individual to
the contacts carrying it (and, for accounts, the person accounts carrying it); anything else is
skipped. A value held by more than ten records is not used. Two people in the same household
are not paired by a Phone or Address source (sharing a home phone or address is what a
household is); an Email source still pairs them. Phone and address candidates are read with at
most 100 patterns to a query, an address by its postal code with the street's first word
normalization leaves as written; a lookup that reaches its 5,000 row cap is logged as a
warning, once per source per transaction. A lookup leaves the transaction 20 queries and 5,000
rows, reads at most what is left above that, and with nothing left is skipped and logged the
same way, never failed. A value from a lookup that reached its cap or was skipped is not used,
since it may be held by more than ten records the lookup did not read. A pair a rule also found is written once, as the
rule's; R-DP2 to R-DP5 apply as to any pair. The set still names an active rule for the
object, as the platform requires (any active rule stands in, so Salesforce's own Duplicate
Record Sets tab shows the pair under that rule), and a pass with no active rule writes no
source pair either. The reason is kept in a Duplicate Dismissal row of Kind Match Reason, keyed
by the set (ADR-NEXT `NEXT-fewer-custom-objects.md`), and shown on the review list (the rule's
name is shown otherwise). It is written, read and deleted in system mode, since it holds only a
source's label and the dismissal object is creatable by administrators only; it is deleted with
its suggestion when dismissed or closed by a merge. A reason row whose set
is gone any other way is never read again and is harmless. A source that cannot be read is
logged and counted as a failure.

**R-DP7 Similar names pair people, household aware** (ADR-0145,
`0145-advanced-duplicate-management.md`). In each people chunk of the scan, the people who share
a last name or an email with someone in the chunk (at most 2,000, read in user mode) are scored
on their full names by `FuzzyMatch.score` (normalized case, spacing and punctuation, then
Jaro-Winkler). A pair scoring at or above `Fuzzy_Match_Threshold__c` percent is proposed when
they share an email (trimmed, lower case) or a phone number (digits), or are in different
households and share a mailing postal code. In one household, where an address is shared by
design and similar names are usually family (Daniel and Danielle), two people with nothing
else in common are proposed only when their names are the same once normalized. Two people
whose birthdates are both filled in and differ are never paired. The reason names the score and what they share. A
pair a rule or a source also found is written once, as theirs; R-DP2 to R-DP5 apply.

**R-DP8 Merge rules decide which value wins.** When two people are merged by auto-merge
(R-DP9), each field the person merging may edit takes the value its active `Merge_Rule__mdt`
row names, and a field with no row follows `Merge_Default_Rule__c`: Keep master (the
survivor's value), Not blank (the survivor's value, or the other's when the survivor's is
blank), Most recent (the value of the record changed last), Oldest record (the value of the
record created first) or Most complete (the longer of the two, the survivor's on a tie). A blank
never wins over a value except under Keep master. A rule on `MailingAddress` or `OtherAddress`
moves the street, city, state, postal code and country together, from one record. The household
(`AccountId`) and owner are never changed by a rule.

**R-DP9 Auto-merge takes only exact matches, after a preview.** Candidates are the open
suggestions in the review list that pair two people (R-DP2) and meet
`Auto_Merge_Exact_Match__c`: the normalized first and last names are equal and so are the email
(trimmed, lower case), the phone (digits), both, or the birthdate, each filled in on both. A
pair whose birthdates both are filled in and differ is never exact. The administrator sees the
pairs, each survivor and the values that will change before anything runs; the run re-checks
each pair, merges in user mode with the platform's merge, at most 1,000 pairs a run, in a batch,
and closes each suggestion. The survivor is the person whose household has more current
members, else the record created first. Households are never auto-merged.

**R-DP10 Every auto-merge is journaled and undone from the Recycle Bin.** Before each merge a
Merge Journal row records the run, both identifiers, the survivor's values the rules changed and
the related records the merge moves (every child whose link to the merged-away person can be
changed). Undo works on a whole run: it undeletes the merged-away person (never a recreated
copy), puts back each changed value still as the merge left it and moves each recorded related
record still on the survivor back. What it cannot restore (no longer in the Recycle Bin, a value
changed since, a related record deleted or refused) is written on the row as Partly Undone or
Undo Failed. Undo is offered while the run is no more than 15 days old.

**R-DP11 Generic Record Merge merges two records of one BarnCRM object** (C-62, extends R-DP8
to R-DP10). Offered while `Generic_Merge_Enabled__c` is on, to holders of Manage BarnCRM
Settings. The objects offered are BarnCRM's own custom objects (those carrying the package
prefix; every custom object where BarnCRM runs without a namespace) that the person may read,
edit, delete and undelete, never Contact or Account (people and households have their own
merge) and never BarnCRM's own logs, journals and configuration objects. The person picks the
record to keep and, field by field, which value it keeps; the starting choice is the one the
merge rules give (R-DP8: a `Merge_Rule__mdt` row named `Object.Field`, else
`Merge_Default_Rule__c`). The owner and record type stay the kept record's. The platform's
merge serves only people, households, leads and cases, so BarnCRM merges in user mode, in one
transaction: it writes the chosen values on the kept record, moves every related record whose
link can be changed onto it, then deletes the other record (to the Recycle Bin). It refuses,
changing nothing, when a related record could not be read (it would lose its link) or sits under
a master-detail link that cannot be changed (it would be deleted with the record).

**R-DP12 Every Generic Record Merge is journaled and can be undone.** The merge writes one
Merge Journal row as R-DP10 describes, with its own Run Id, so undo works on that one merge.
The Merge Records area lists the last 15 days of these merges with Undo, which works as R-DP10
does. Auto-merge's Recent Runs lists only people merges. Files and notes linked to the other
record are also linked to the kept record (a file already linked there is skipped), in the
same transaction; the journal's moved-records list keeps the new `ContentDocumentLink` Ids
under the key `ContentDocumentLink+`, and undo deletes those links. The file itself is never
copied or changed.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Merge Journal** (R-DP10): each merge is an Admin Journal row (`Merge_Journal__c`, Section
  10A) of Kind Merge, with `Run_Id__c`, `Survivor_Id__c`, `Merged_Id__c`, `Merged_Name__c`,
  `Status__c` (Merged, Undone, Partly Undone, Undo Failed), `Changed_Values__c`,
  `Moved_Records__c` and `Notes__c` as declared there. Private: each run's rows belong to the
  administrator who ran it, and BarnCRM Admin views and modifies all of them. Written and read in
  user mode, always of Kind Merge.

- **Object** `Duplicate_Dismissal__c`, with an auto number Name. Sharing is public read/write:
  a dismissal is the organization's decision, and a scan run by one administrator must pass
  over a pair another administrator dismissed. It also holds the match reasons of R-DP6 (Kind
  Match Reason), which until N-11 were the separate object `Duplicate_Reason__c` keyed by
  `Set_Id__c`. Dismissal queries, the dismissal count and the All Duplicate Dismissals list view
  leave Match Reason rows out.

| Attribute | API name | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kind | `Kind__c` | Picklist, restricted, default Dismissal | Dismissal or Match Reason. |
| Pair Key | `Pair_Key__c` | Text(40), unique, external id | A dismissal: the two 18 character identifiers in ascending order, joined with a hyphen. A match reason: the Duplicate Record Set's 18 character identifier. |
| Reason | `Reason__c` | Text(255) | A dismissal: optional, the person's words. A match reason: what the review list shows, naming the match source. |

- **Suggestions** are the standard objects `DuplicateRecordSet` and `DuplicateRecordItem`,
  read with `DuplicateRule`. They are read and written in user mode, so a reviewer is never
  shown a pair containing a record they cannot see. Salesforce licenses them only to Sales
  Cloud and Service Cloud users, so no Core role grants them: the optional permission set
  `BarnCRM_Duplicate_Review` does, and the panel says so to anyone without it (ADR-0050).
  That set also carries the custom permission `Review_Duplicate_Suggestions`, which grants
  no record access and only shows the Review area of the Duplicate Matching tab to a holder
  who is not an administrator; its holders are in that tab's audience (`TabAccessService`,
  `BarnCRM_Tab_Duplicate_Matching`, ADR-0139). Scanning, dismissing and merging still need
  Manage BarnCRM Settings.
- **People merges** are the platform's. When a contact, or a person stored as an account, is
  deleted by a merge (`MasterRecordId` filled in `after delete`), its memberships are
  recreated on the survivor in junction mode (all or none; only current rows count as already
  a member; a household whose primary member was merged away gets the survivor as its
  primary, R-M3), the households it was in are recounted but not tidied away, and the
  real-time rollups that target the merged entity are recalculated for the survivors only.
  For a person stored as an account that is the rollups on Account and on the survivor's
  person contact. An account merge of households (R-H13) recalculates the surviving
  household's real-time rollups the same way.
- **Merge settlement** (PEOPLE-15) runs just after any Salesforce merge, in a queued job
  (`MergeSettlement`): a person in both merged households keeps one membership, a household
  that took in members is recounted and renamed, a survivor keeps one primary address (the one
  matching its standard address fields: billing for a household or organization, mailing for a
  contact or a person account, read by name so Core runs without person accounts; otherwise
  the newest), and a person loses relationships with themselves and second copies and has
  their primary affiliation chosen again. A merge that cannot queue the job (inside a
  Queueable, or with no queueable job left) publishes `Merge_Settlement_Ready__e` instead, and
  its subscriber queues the job after the merge commits (ADR-0118). Only a publish the
  platform refuses leaves the survivors to an administrator, named in the Error Log as a
  warning.
- **Event:** `Merge_Settlement_Ready__e`, a platform event, publish behavior Publish After
  Commit. `Household_Ids__c`, `Owner_Ids__c` and `Person_Ids__c` (Long Text Area, 32,768) each
  carry up to 200 comma-separated survivor identifiers; more survivors make more events.
  `MergeSettlementReadyTrigger` subscribes, as the Automated Process user, in batches of 50
  (`PlatformEventSubscriberConfig` `MergeSettlementReadyTriggerConfig`, no running user), and
  queues one settlement job per event, resuming from a checkpoint when its transaction can
  queue no more and retrying a batch it could queue nothing for. Each event is settled only for
  the identifiers its publisher (`CreatedById`) may edit (`UserRecordAccess`); the rest are left
  alone and named in the Error Log as a warning. BarnCRM Admin and BarnCRM Staff (who merge
  households) grant Read and Create on it; BarnCRM Read Only, which merges nothing, grants
  neither.
- **Matching** is `Datacloud.FindDuplicatesByIds`, which evaluates the org's active duplicate
  rules. It is called for one object at a time, and for households only among accounts: a
  call that includes a person stored as an account is refused by the platform when no person
  account rule is active.
- **Merge** of households is `HouseholdMergeService` (R-H13). The Contact record page carries
  the platform's Potential Duplicates card (`runtime_sales_merge:mergeCandidatesPreviewCard`),
  which is where the platform's own person merge starts. The Account record page does not
  carry it, so a household is never merged past R-H13.
- **Service:** `DuplicateService`, `DuplicateSelector`, `DuplicateScanBatch`,
  `DuplicateController`. The review list is the `duplicateReview` component, the Review area
  of the Duplicate Matching tab (app page `Duplicate_Matching`, shell `duplicateMatching`,
  ADR-0139). BarnCRM Settings has a Duplicate Matching section whose row opens that tab.

---

# Part F: Mirror additions for v0.6

The Mirror package is the only place a standard Salesforce object such as Campaign or
Opportunity may be named (plan Section 4.2), and even there only through dynamic Apex, so
Mirror installs on an org where the object is absent and its feature says it is unavailable.
The inbound gift API and the accounting export add nothing to the model (Section 30). Campaign
sync (X-02) adds one attribute to Appeal and Mirror's own settings object. The Opportunity
mirror (X-01) adds one attribute to Gift and two keys to that settings object. The Gift
Transaction mirror (X-07, Section 29C1) adds one attribute to Gift, one to Fund and five keys to
that settings object, and is the only place a Nonprofit Cloud object is named, by string,
through describe.

Since release 1.27 (N-09, ADR-NEXT mirror independence) these are two packages, under the same
rule. **Mirror** (`packages/mirror`, depends on Core only) keeps the settings object
`Mirror_Settings__c` with every key, Provider Request (Section 29C2) and the Nonprofit Cloud
households and relationships kits. **Mirror for Giving** (`packages/mirrorgiving`, depends on
Core, Rollup Builder, Giving and Mirror) ships every attribute and list view this part adds to
Giving's Appeal, Gift and Fund, and the Campaign sync, Opportunity mirror, Gift Transaction
mirror, inbound gift API and accounting export code and permission sets. Where a section below
says "shipped by Mirror" for an attribute on a Giving object, read Mirror for Giving. No
attribute, key or object changed.

---

## 29B. Campaign Sync

### Definition

A one-way copy of each appeal to a standard Salesforce Campaign, so that Campaign Members,
email tools and other marketing apps that only know Campaign see the organization's appeals
(plan Section 4.12, feature X-02). The appeal is the record staff edit; the Campaign follows
it. Nothing on a Campaign is ever copied back to an appeal.

Campaign sync is not an entity of its own. It is one attribute on Appeal, held by Mirror
because Giving may not name Campaign, and a switch on Mirror Settings. There is no link
object: an appeal has at most one Campaign, so the link is the attribute (ADR-0056, Campaign
sync keeps its link on the appeal).

### Attributes added to Appeal

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Campaign ID | text (18) | no | The record identifier of the Campaign this appeal is copied to. Written by Campaign sync when it creates the Campaign; an administrator may type an existing Campaign's identifier to link to it, or clear it to have a new Campaign made. Unique, so two appeals never share one Campaign. |

It is held as text rather than as a lookup because a lookup to Campaign is a compile-time
reference: Mirror would then refuse to install on an org without Campaign, which ADR-0013
and plan Section 4.2 forbid.

### Mirror Settings keys (v0.6)

| Key | Type | Default | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Campaign_Sync_Enabled__c` | boolean | false | Whether saving an appeal creates or updates its Campaign. Off at install, because an org that has Campaigns of its own must decide before BarnCRM adds more (R-CS1). |

### Rules

**R-CS1 Off until switched on.** Campaign sync does nothing until an administrator turns it
on in BarnCRM Settings. It also does nothing where the org has no Campaign object (a
Platform-only org), and the Campaign sync page says so rather than offering a switch that
cannot work. It is a registered automation on Appeal (`Campaign_Sync`), so it can also be
paused or switched off like any other (ADR-0040). The setting is authoritative: it says
whether the feature is wanted, and Sync all appeals follows it alone. The automation switch
only pauses the copy made on save, and has no effect while the setting is off.

**R-CS2 What is copied.** Name to Name, Description to Description, Start Date to Start
Date, End Date to End Date, Goal to Expected Revenue, Cost to Actual Cost, Active to Active,
and Parent Appeal to Parent Campaign (the parent appeal's Campaign, or none while the parent
has none). Nothing else is written: a new Campaign takes the org's defaults for Type and
Status, and the Campaign's own totals (from Opportunities) are the platform's. A Campaign
field changed by hand is overwritten the next time its appeal changes in one of these
attributes.

**R-CS3 When it is copied.** When an appeal is created, and when it is saved with a change to
one of the attributes in R-CS2, to its Campaign ID, or while it has no Campaign yet. The
Campaign is created or updated in the same save, before the appeal is written, so the new
Campaign ID is stored with the appeal and never in a second save. A Campaign whose values
already match is not updated.

**R-CS4 In the saver's own access.** The Campaign is written in user mode, with the access
of the person saving the appeal. Campaign is a standard object BarnCRM does not own, so
an elevated write (ADR-0021) is not available for it. Someone who cannot create or edit
Campaigns (in Salesforce that needs the Marketing User box on their user record as well as
Campaign permissions) still saves the appeal; the appeal simply stays without a Campaign.
One Warning is written to the Error Log when such a person creates appeals, at most once per
transaction; their later edits are skipped without one, so the log is not flooded.

**R-CS5 A failure never refuses the appeal.** A Campaign the platform refuses (a validation
rule on Campaign, a required field the org added, sharing) is written to the Error Log at
Warning with the appeal and the platform's message. The appeal saves, and keeps no Campaign
ID when none was created. However many appeals are refused, their Warnings are written in one
statement. A save too large to copy within the transaction's query and DML limits (thousands
of appeals in one Apex transaction) saves its appeals uncopied, logs one Warning, and leaves
them to Sync all appeals.

**R-CS6 Catching up.** The Campaign sync page shows how many appeals have a Campaign and how
many do not, and offers **Sync all appeals**, which runs R-CS2 over every appeal the person
can see, in the background, as that person. It is how the appeals that existed before the
feature was turned on get their Campaigns, and how appeals saved by someone without Campaign
access (R-CS4) are caught up. It needs the Manage BarnCRM Settings permission, and only one
runs at a time.

**R-CS7 Never deleted.** Deleting an appeal leaves its Campaign in place, with its members
and history; restoring the appeal restores the link. BarnCRM never deletes a Campaign it
did not just create. The one deletion is Sync all appeals undoing its own work: a Campaign it
created for an appeal whose Campaign ID it then could not store is deleted in the same run, so
the next run does not make a second one. A Campaign it cannot delete is named in a Warning.
A linked Campaign that has been deleted, or that the person saving cannot see, is reported
as R-CS5 describes and is not replaced: clearing the appeal's Campaign ID makes a new one.

**R-CS8 One appeal, one Campaign.** Campaign ID is unique, so a Campaign mirrors at most one
appeal, and a typed value that is not a Campaign's identifier is refused on save. It is also
the key the Opportunity mirror (X-01) will read to put a mirrored gift's Opportunity in the
Campaign of the gift's appeal, which is why it is an indexed external identifier.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Attribute on `Appeal__c`, shipped by Mirror for Giving** (in `packages/mirrorgiving`, not Giving):

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Campaign ID | `Campaign_Id__c` | Text(18), unique, external ID, case sensitive |

- **Custom setting:** `Mirror_Settings__c`, hierarchy, protected, Mirror's own under
  ADR-0017.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Campaign Sync Enabled | `Campaign_Sync_Enabled__c` | Checkbox |

- **Automation:** `Automation_Registry__mdt` row `Campaign_Sync` on `Appeal__c`, order 50,
  enabled by default, handler `CampaignSyncTriggerHandler`, running before insert and before
  update. Its switch row is created by `MirrorPostInstall`, which Mirror gains for this.
- **Service:** `CampaignSyncService` (the copy), `CampaignSyncSelector` (appeal and Campaign
  reads, Campaign by dynamic query only), `CampaignSyncBatch` (R-CS6),
  `CampaignSyncController` and the `campaignSync` page reached from the Giving section of
  BarnCRM Settings. Permission set: `Salesforce_Records_Sync` (retired `Campaign_Sync` until the
  next release, ADR-0194 D4).

## 29C. Opportunity Mirror

### Definition

A copy between gifts and standard Salesforce Opportunities, in one direction per org (plan
Section 4.12, feature X-01). **Gifts to Opportunities** copies each gift to an Opportunity, so
NPSP rollups, NPSP soft credits, Campaign totals and other apps that only know Opportunity see
the organization's giving. **Opportunities to Gifts** is for an org whose online giving tool
writes Opportunities: each won Opportunity becomes a gift. The org chooses one direction or
neither, never both, and a reconciliation page shows where the two sides disagree.

The Opportunity mirror is not an entity of its own. It is one attribute on Gift, held by
Mirror because Giving may not name Opportunity, two keys on Mirror Settings, and one
automation. There is no link object: a gift has at most one Opportunity, so the link is the
attribute, as it is for Campaign sync (Section 29B, ADR-0058).

### Attributes added to Gift

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opportunity ID | text (18) | no | The record identifier of the Opportunity this gift is mirrored to or was made from. Written by the mirror; an administrator may type an existing Opportunity's identifier to link to it, or clear it. Unique, so two gifts never share one Opportunity. |

It is text rather than a lookup for the reason Section 29B gives: a lookup to Opportunity would
stop Mirror installing on an org without Opportunity (ADR-0013).

### Mirror Settings keys (v0.6)

| Key | Type | Default | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Opportunity_Mirror_Direction__c` | text | Off | `GiftsToOpportunities`, `OpportunitiesToGifts` or `Off`, shown as Gifts to Opportunities, Opportunities to Gifts and Off. Empty reads as Off (R-OM1). |
| `Opportunity_Mirror_Start__c` | datetime | empty | Opportunities to Gifts only: an Opportunity becomes a gift only when its Close Date is on or after this date, read as a date in the org's default time zone. Empty means no Opportunity becomes a gift (R-OM7). |
| `Opportunity_Mirror_Record_Types__c` | text | empty | Opportunities to Gifts only: the record types, by API name and separated by commas, whose won Opportunities become gifts. Empty means every record type (R-OM7). |
| `Opportunity_Mirror_Last_Run__c` | datetime | empty | Written by the runs, not by an administrator: when the last completed run started (R-OM8). |
| `Opportunity_Mirror_Last_Summary__c` | text | empty | Written by the runs: one sentence saying what the last completed run did (R-OM8). |

### Rules

**R-OM1 One direction, off until chosen.** The mirror does nothing until an administrator
chooses a direction in BarnCRM Settings, and one setting holds the choice, so two directions
can never be active at once. It also does nothing where the org has no Opportunity object, and
the Opportunity mirror page says so. The Gifts to Opportunities copy made on save is a
registered automation on Gift (`Opportunity_Mirror`), so it can be paused or switched off like
any other (ADR-0040); the setting is authoritative, and the runs of R-OM8 follow it alone.

**R-OM2 Which gifts are copied.** In Gifts to Opportunities, a gift gets an Opportunity when it
counts in the giving totals: Status Received, Refunded or Written off (ADR-0022). That includes
the negative gift recording a refund or a write-off, whose Opportunity has a negative Amount,
so an NPSP total nets exactly as the BarnCRM total does, and an in-kind gift, whose Amount
is zero (R-G12). A Pending or Cancelled gift gets no Opportunity. A copied gift that moves to
Cancelled keeps its Opportunity, moved to the lost stage; one that moves back to Pending keeps
its Opportunity at the stage it has (R-OM3). Neither is ever deleted.

**R-OM3 What is copied.** Amount to Amount; Gift Date to Close Date; Status to Stage, as the
won stage for a gift in the totals, the lost stage for a Cancelled gift, and the Opportunity's
own stage left as it is for a Pending gift, so linking an open Opportunity to a pledge never
closes it; Donor Account to Account, or Household when the donor is a person stored as a
contact (the BarnCRM household, which in an org running NPSP alongside is not the NPSP
household); the appeal's Campaign ID (Section 29B) to Campaign, when it names a Campaign and the
saver may read Campaigns and the appeal's Campaign ID (otherwise Campaign is left as it is,
never cleared); and the donor person as the primary Contact Role (Donor
Contact, or the person contact of a person account), with Role `Donor` when the org's role list
has it. The won stage is the org's active stage named `Closed Won` when it is a won stage, and
otherwise its first active won stage by order; the lost stage is found the same way from
`Closed Lost`. On creation only, the Opportunity is named from the donor and the gift date, and
takes the record type `Donation` when the org has one the saver may use; a Donation record type
whose sales process lacks the chosen stage makes the insert fail, which is logged as R-OM6
describes. Nothing else is written.
A copied field changed by hand on the Opportunity is overwritten the next time its gift changes
in one of these attributes.

**R-OM4 When it is copied.** In Gifts to Opportunities, when a gift is created, and when it is
saved with a change to an attribute in R-OM3 or to its Opportunity ID, or while it has no
Opportunity yet. The Opportunity is created or updated in the same save, before the gift is
written, so its identifier is stored with the gift and never in a second save. An Opportunity
whose values already match is not updated.

**R-OM5 In the saver's own access.** Opportunities and Contact Roles are written in user mode,
with the access of the person saving the gift. Opportunity is a standard object BarnCRM does
not own, so an elevated write (ADR-0021) is not available for it. The copy needs Opportunity
create and edit, and nothing else: the Opportunity ID is written onto the gift being saved by
the automation itself, so a person without the Opportunity Mirror permission set, who cannot
see that attribute, still has their gifts copied. Someone who cannot create and edit
Opportunities still saves the gift, which stays uncopied until a run of R-OM8 copies it. One
Warning says so, written when such a person creates or changes gifts in a save they made
themselves, at most once per transaction; none is written from a background job, since an import
of many chunks would repeat it for every chunk.

**R-OM6 A failure never refuses the gift.** An Opportunity the platform refuses (a validation
rule on Opportunity, a required field the org added, a closed stage the org's rules forbid) is
logged and the gift saves. Refusals are grouped: one Warning per distinct platform message per
transaction, or per run, giving the count and naming up to ten gifts, so a rule that refuses
every gift of a large import writes a handful of entries rather than one per gift; at most 50
distinct messages are kept, and any further ones are counted together. A copy starts only while
half of the transaction's queries and DML statements, and 40 percent of its CPU time, are still
unspent, since the org's own Opportunity automation (NPSP's rollups, say) runs inside the same
save and its cost cannot be measured in advance. A save that does not leave that room saves its
gifts uncopied, logs one Warning, and leaves them to the next run.

**R-OM7 Opportunities to Gifts.** Each won Opportunity whose Close Date is on or after the start
date (a date in the org's default time zone), whose record type is one of those listed when any
are, and that no gift names, becomes a gift: the donor is the primary Contact Role's contact (a
person account's account where people are accounts, R-G1), or else the Opportunity's Account;
Amount is the Opportunity's Amount, which must be above zero; Gift Date is its Close Date; Type
Other; Status Received; Appeal is the appeal whose Campaign ID is the Opportunity's Campaign;
and Opportunity ID is set in the same insert, so the unique attribute stops a second gift even
when two runs overlap. Giving's own rules then derive the household and the default allocation,
as for any gift. A gift made this way is never edited by the mirror afterwards, so a receipted
or posted gift is never touched (R-G4, R-G14); a later change to its Opportunity shows on the
reconciliation page instead. An Opportunity that cannot become a gift (no donor, an amount not
above zero, a gift rule such as a closed period) is logged as R-OM6 describes and tried again
by the next run; an Opportunity another run has just made a gift of is counted as unchanged.
Gifts are created in user mode, as the person who started the run.

**R-OM8 Runs.** The Opportunity mirror page offers **Run now** and a nightly schedule
(Schedule and Stop, the shape of ADR-0038, at 01:30). A run follows the chosen direction: in
Gifts to Opportunities it copies every gift in the totals that has no Opportunity yet, which is
how the gifts that existed before the mirror was turned on, and those saved by someone without
Opportunity access, are caught up, and every linked gift changed since the last completed run
started, which puts right a change whose copy was skipped; in Opportunities to Gifts it applies
R-OM7. Starting a run or the schedule needs the Manage BarnCRM Settings permission, and only
one run is in progress at a time. A run executes as the person who started or scheduled it, in
user mode. While automation is paused (ADR-0055) or the `Opportunity_Mirror` switch is off, a
run does nothing and writes one Info entry saying so, checked when it starts and before each
chunk, because Giving's own rules are paused too and a gift made then would never get its
household or allocation. A run that completes writes a summary at Info to the Error Log and
records its start time and summary on Mirror Settings, which the page shows. Health Check
warns when the nightly run is scheduled, the direction is chosen, and no run has completed for
more than two days (ADR-0055 point 7).

**R-OM9 Never deleted.** Deleting a gift leaves its Opportunity in place, and one Warning per
delete names the gifts and their Opportunities; the reconciliation page then shows each as a
won Opportunity without a gift, for the administrator to decide. In Opportunities to Gifts the
next run makes a new gift from such an Opportunity while it is still won, and the Warning says
so. BarnCRM never deletes an Opportunity it did not just create. The one deletion is a run undoing
its own work: an Opportunity it created for a gift whose Opportunity ID it then could not store
is deleted in the same run, so the next run does not make a second one, and one it cannot delete
is named in a Warning. A linked Opportunity that has been deleted, or that the person saving
cannot see, is logged as "deleted or not visible to you" and is not replaced: clearing the
gift's Opportunity ID makes a new one.

**R-OM10 One gift, one Opportunity.** Opportunity ID is unique, so an Opportunity mirrors at
most one gift, and a typed value that is not an Opportunity's identifier is refused on save. A
15 character identifier is stored in its 18 character form. Typing an existing Opportunity's
identifier links to it, and the gift's values then overwrite that Opportunity's copied fields.

**R-OM11 Reconciliation.** For a date range, the reconciliation page compares the gifts in the
totals dated in the range with the won Opportunities closed in the range, both as the person
viewing can see them, and shows each side's count and total and the differences: a gift with no
Opportunity; a gift whose Opportunity is deleted or not visible; a linked gift and Opportunity
whose amount, date or won state disagree; and a won Opportunity with no gift visible to the
viewer. It reads in user mode and writes nothing, and a viewer who cannot read Opportunity, its
Name, Amount and Close Date, or the gift's Opportunity ID is refused in words. A range holding
more than 10,000 gifts or 10,000 won Opportunities, or more than the transaction can read in
one go, is refused rather than shown in part, as the accounting export is (ADR-0051); the
reads stop at 10,001 records a side, so a very large range is refused rather than failing. In Gifts to
Opportunities it offers **Copy these gifts again**, a run over every gift in the range, linked
or not, which puts right what R-OM3 copies. In Opportunities to Gifts the differences are shown
only, because a gift is never edited from its Opportunity.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Attribute on `Gift__c`, shipped by Mirror for Giving** (in `packages/mirrorgiving`, not Giving):

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Opportunity ID | `Opportunity_Id__c` | Text(18), unique, external ID, case sensitive |

- **Custom setting `Mirror_Settings__c`** (Section 29B) gains:

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Opportunity Mirror Direction | `Opportunity_Mirror_Direction__c` | Text(40) |
| Opportunity Mirror Start | `Opportunity_Mirror_Start__c` | Date/Time |
| Opportunity Mirror Record Types | `Opportunity_Mirror_Record_Types__c` | Text(255) |
| Opportunity Mirror Last Run | `Opportunity_Mirror_Last_Run__c` | Date/Time |
| Opportunity Mirror Last Summary | `Opportunity_Mirror_Last_Summary__c` | Text(255) |

- **Automation:** `Automation_Registry__mdt` row `Opportunity_Mirror` on `Gift__c`, order 50,
  after `Gift_Core_Rules` derives the household, enabled by default, handler
  `OpportunityMirrorTriggerHandler`, running before insert, before update and after delete. Its
  switch row is created by `MirrorPostInstall`.
- **Service:** `MirrorSync` (the comparisons, limit headroom, identifier checks and grouped
  Warnings shared with Campaign sync), `OpportunityMirrorService` (Gifts to Opportunities),
  `OpportunityGiftService` (Opportunities to Gifts), `OpportunityMirrorSelector` (gift and
  Opportunity reads, Opportunity by dynamic query only), `OpportunityMirrorBatch` and
  `OpportunityMirrorSchedulable` (R-OM8), `OpportunityMirrorReconciliation` (R-OM11),
  `OpportunityMirrorController` and the `opportunityMirror` page reached from the Giving section
  of BarnCRM Settings, `MirrorSettingsWriter` (the runs' record of their last completed run)
  and `MirrorHealthCheckExtension` (the stale run finding, through the ADR-0057 seam).
  Permission set: `Salesforce_Records_Sync` (retired `Opportunity_Mirror` until the next
  release, ADR-0194 D4), which also carries the custom permission
  `Use_Opportunity_Mirror`: the page's reads require it, and the console shows the page's row
  only to someone who has it (the Setting Definition's `Required_Permission__c`).
- **List view** `Gifts_And_Opportunities` on Gift, shipped by Mirror for Giving, where Opportunity ID is
  typed or cleared (R-OM10).

## 29C1. Gift Transaction Mirror

### Definition

A one-way copy of gifts to Nonprofit Cloud (Agentforce Nonprofit) Gift Transaction records, with
their designations (plan Sections 4.5 and 4.12, feature X-07, ADR-0157). Nonprofit Cloud's donor
gift summaries, donor pages, giving levels, actionable lists and Agentforce actions read Gift
Transactions only, so an organization that records its gifts in BarnCRM turns the mirror on to
keep those features seeing its giving. A reconciliation page shows where the two sides disagree.

The mirror is not an entity of its own. It is one attribute on Gift and one on Fund, held by
Mirror for Giving because no other package may name a Nonprofit Cloud object, and five keys on Mirror
Settings. There is no link object, for the reason Section 29C gives (ADR-0058). Every Nonprofit
Cloud object and field is reached through describe, by name, never at compile time; the names
used are those of `docs/architecture/reference/nonprofit-cloud-data-model.md` Sections 3.1 to
3.3, and the types it marks as inferred are checked at run time (R-GT1).

The reverse direction, Gift Transactions to Gifts, is not built: it is the open owner question
O-7 (plan Section 11.2 item 32). The direction setting is a list so that it can be added without
a model change.

### Attributes added to Gift

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gift Transaction ID | text (18) | no | The record identifier of the Gift Transaction this gift is mirrored to. Written by the mirror's runs; an administrator may type an existing Gift Transaction's identifier to link to it, or clear it. Unique, so two gifts never share one Gift Transaction. Independent of Opportunity ID (Section 29C): a gift may have both. |

### Attributes added to Fund

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gift Designation ID | text (18) | no | The record identifier of the Nonprofit Cloud Gift Designation this fund stands for, typed by an administrator. Not unique: two funds may share one designation. Empty means the fund's share of a gift is not designated (R-GT5). |

Both are text rather than lookups for the reason Section 29B gives: a lookup to a Nonprofit Cloud
object would stop Mirror installing on every org without Nonprofit Cloud (ADR-0009, ADR-0013).

### Mirror Settings keys (release 0.17)

| Key | Type | Default | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Gift_Transaction_Mirror_Direction__c` | text | Off | `GiftsToGiftTransactions` or `Off`, shown as Gifts to Gift Transactions and Off. Empty reads as Off (R-GT1). |
| `Gift_Transaction_Mirror_Status__c` | text | Paid | The API value of the Gift Transaction Status that means paid in this org, written on each Gift Transaction the mirror creates. Empty, or a value the org's Status list does not have active, means nothing is copied (R-GT2). |
| `Gift_Transaction_Mirror_Start__c` | datetime | empty | Only gifts dated on or after this date are copied, read as a date in the org's default time zone. Empty means nothing is copied (R-GT2). |
| `Gift_Transaction_Mirror_Last_Run__c` | datetime | empty | Written by the runs, not by an administrator: when the last completed run started (R-GT6). |
| `Gift_Transaction_Mirror_Last_Summary__c` | text | empty | Written by the runs: one sentence saying what the last completed run did (R-GT6). |

### Rules

**R-GT1 Off until chosen, and nothing at all without Nonprofit Cloud.** The mirror does nothing
until an administrator sets the direction to Gifts to Gift Transactions in BarnCRM Settings. It
is independent of the Opportunity mirror (Section 29C). The mirror is available only when the
running person's describe has the Gift Transaction object (Nonprofit Cloud fundraising, which
needs the Fundraising Access license and the Fundraising User permission) and its fields are the
shape this version expects: Donor a reference to Account, Transaction Date a date, Original
Amount an amount, Status a picklist. Otherwise the mirror is unavailable: the page says so, runs
do nothing, and no query names a Nonprofit Cloud object. Saving a gift never reads Nonprofit
Cloud records (R-GT6), so an org without Nonprofit Cloud pays nothing for the feature being
installed.

**R-GT2 Nothing moves until the paid status and the start date are right.** Gift Transaction
Status values are the org's configuration, so the paid status is a setting, shipped as `Paid`
and checked against the org's active Status values before a run does anything. The start date
has no default: a gift loaded from Nonprofit Cloud into the same org (the Nonprofit Cloud import
templates, C-14) already has its Gift Transaction, and copying it back would count every
historical gift twice in Nonprofit Cloud's summaries. Setting the start date to the day after the
last load is how an administrator says where the mirror begins.

**R-GT3 Which gifts are copied.** A gift is copied when its Status is Received, its Amount is
above zero, its Type is not In-kind, and its Gift Date is on or after the start date. A refund or
write-off, which is a negative gift (R-G3), is never copied: Nonprofit Cloud records money given
back on the Gift Transaction itself, so a negative Gift Transaction would count as one more gift
in its summaries. A refunded or written off original that has no Gift Transaction yet is not
copied; one that already has one keeps it unchanged, and the reconciliation lists it (R-GT10). An
in-kind gift carries no money (R-G12) and is not copied. Pending and Cancelled gifts are not
copied.

**R-GT4 What is copied.** Donor Account to Donor, or Household when the donor is a person stored
as a contact; Gift Date to Transaction Date; Amount to Original Amount. On creation only: Amount
to Current Amount, the paid status of R-GT2 to Status, and the gift's name to Name, each only
where the org has the field and the person running may write it. A later run updates Donor,
Transaction Date and Original Amount when the gift's differ, and never Status or Current Amount,
which Nonprofit Cloud maintains once the transaction exists (a refund recorded there lowers
Current Amount). Nothing else is written: no campaign, source code, payment or tax field, and
never a record Nonprofit Cloud calculates (Donor Gift Summary, the Gift Designation totals). A
gift with neither a Donor Account nor a Household cannot be copied and is logged as R-GT7
describes.

**R-GT5 Designations.** When a run creates a Gift Transaction, it gives it one Gift Transaction
Designation per allocation of the gift (R-G5) whose fund has a Gift Designation ID naming a Gift
Designation: Gift Transaction to the new record, Gift Designation to the fund's, and Amount to the
allocation's amount. A fund is matched only by that identifier, never by name, because a renamed
fund would otherwise move money between designations. Designations are written at creation only,
and only when the new Gift Transaction has none (Nonprofit Cloud may give it a default one): after
that they belong to Nonprofit Cloud, a later run never changes them, and the reconciliation does
not compare them. An allocation whose fund has no Gift Designation ID, or one that does not name a
Gift Designation, is left undesignated and counted in the run's summary; a designation the
platform refuses is logged as R-GT7 describes, and the Gift Transaction stays. Designations are
written only where the org's describe has Gift Transaction Designation with Gift Transaction and
Gift Designation references and an Amount, and the person running may create it with them;
otherwise the run copies gifts without designations and its summary says so.

**R-GT6 Runs, never on save.** The Gift Transaction mirror page offers **Run Now** and a nightly
schedule (Schedule and Stop, the shape of ADR-0038, at 01:35). Saving a gift copies nothing:
Nonprofit Cloud calculates its donor summaries in its own scheduled runs, so a copy on save would
be seen no sooner, and Gift Transactions are open only to people with the Fundraising User
permission, which not everyone who enters gifts has. A run copies every gift of R-GT3 that has no
Gift Transaction yet, and every linked gift of R-GT3 changed since the last completed run
started. Starting a run or the schedule needs the Manage BarnCRM Settings permission, and only
one run is in progress at a time. A run executes as the person who started or scheduled it, in
user mode. While automation is paused (ADR-0055) or the `Gift_Transaction_Mirror` switch is off,
a run does nothing and writes one Info entry saying so, checked when it starts and before each
chunk; a run whose paid status or start date is missing or unknown, or whose person can no longer
read or write what the copy needs, does nothing and writes one Warning. A chunk that starts
without half of the transaction's queries and DML statements, and 40 percent of its CPU time,
unspent is skipped and counted, with one Warning for the run. A run writes a summary at Info when
it ends; one that left no chunk also records its start time and summary on Mirror Settings, which
the page shows, so a run that left chunks is followed by one that rechecks from the last complete
run. Health Check warns when the nightly run is scheduled, the direction is chosen, and no run
has completed for more than two days, and lists the nightly run with the other nightly jobs while
the direction is chosen (ADR-0075).

**R-GT7 A refusal never stops the run.** Every write is in user mode with partial success. A
record the platform refuses is counted, and one Warning per distinct message is written when the
run ends, giving the count and naming up to ten records, with at most 50 distinct messages kept
(`MirrorSync.Warnings`, as R-OM6). A Gift Transaction created for a gift whose Gift Transaction
ID then could not be stored is deleted again in the same run, so the next run does not make a
second one; one it cannot delete is named in a Warning.

**R-GT8 Nothing the org had is deleted.** Deleting a gift leaves its Gift Transaction in place,
and one Warning per delete names the gifts and their Gift Transactions. A linked Gift Transaction
the person running cannot find is logged as "deleted or not visible to you" and is not replaced:
clearing the gift's Gift Transaction ID makes a new one.

**R-GT9 One gift, one Gift Transaction.** Gift Transaction ID is unique, so a Gift Transaction
mirrors at most one gift. A typed value that is not a Gift Transaction's identifier is refused on
save wherever the person saving can see Gift Transactions, and a 15 character identifier is stored
in its 18 character form. Typing an existing Gift Transaction's identifier links to it, and the
next run writes the gift's values of R-GT4 onto it.

**R-GT10 Reconciliation.** For a date range, the page compares the gifts of R-GT3 dated in the
range (without the start date) with the Gift Transactions of the paid status dated in the range,
both as the person viewing can see them, and shows each side's count and total and the
differences: a gift with no Gift Transaction; a gift whose Gift Transaction is deleted or not
visible; a linked pair whose amount, date or status disagree; and a Gift Transaction that no gift
of R-GT3 names. It reads in user mode and writes nothing; it refuses in words a viewer who cannot
read Gift Transactions, their Name, Original Amount, Transaction Date and Status, or the gift's
Gift Transaction ID, and a range over 10,000 records a side or more than the transaction can
read, as R-OM11 does. It offers **Copy These Gifts Again**, a run over the gifts of R-GT3 in the
range that are dated on or after the start date.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Attribute on `Gift__c`, shipped by Mirror for Giving** (in `packages/mirrorgiving`):

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Gift Transaction ID | `Gift_Transaction_Id__c` | Text(18), unique, external ID, case sensitive |

- **Attribute on `Fund__c`, shipped by Mirror for Giving**:

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Gift Designation ID | `Gift_Designation_Id__c` | Text(18) |

- **Custom setting `Mirror_Settings__c`** (Section 29B) gains:

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Gift Transaction Mirror Direction | `Gift_Transaction_Mirror_Direction__c` | Text(40), default `Off` |
| Gift Transaction Mirror Status | `Gift_Transaction_Mirror_Status__c` | Text(255), default `Paid` |
| Gift Transaction Mirror Start | `Gift_Transaction_Mirror_Start__c` | Date/Time |
| Gift Transaction Mirror Last Run | `Gift_Transaction_Mirror_Last_Run__c` | Date/Time |
| Gift Transaction Mirror Last Summary | `Gift_Transaction_Mirror_Last_Summary__c` | Text(255) |

- **Nonprofit Cloud names read, all through describe:** the object `GiftTransaction` and its
  fields `DonorId`, `TransactionDate`, `OriginalAmount`, `CurrentAmount`, `Status` and `Name`;
  the object `GiftTransactionDesignation` and its fields `GiftTransactionId`,
  `GiftDesignationId` and `Amount`; the object `GiftDesignation`, whose identifiers the funds
  hold. Their types, required flags and `Status` values are not verified by the reference, which
  is why R-GT1 and R-GT5 check the types and R-GT2 checks the status. `CurrentAmount` and `Name`
  are optional: without them, or without write access to them, a Gift Transaction is created
  without them. The names are held in one place, `GiftTransactionMirrorSchema`, which tests point
  at stand-in objects of the same shape (Gift, Gift Allocation and Fund), so the copy is tested
  in an org without Nonprofit Cloud.
- **Automation:** `Automation_Registry__mdt` row `Gift_Transaction_Mirror` on `Gift__c`, order
  51, enabled by default, handler `GiftTransactionMirrorTriggerHandler`, running before insert and
  before update (R-GT9, only when the link is typed or changed) and after delete (R-GT8). It
  copies nothing; its switch also stops the runs. Its switch row is created by
  `MirrorPostInstall`.
- **Service:** `GiftTransactionMirrorSchema` (the names, the describe and the shape checks of
  R-GT1 and R-GT5), `GiftTransactionMirrorService` (settings, the link check, the copy and the
  designations), `GiftTransactionMirrorSelector` (gift, allocation, fund and Gift Transaction
  reads, Nonprofit Cloud objects by dynamic query only), `GiftTransactionMirrorBatch` and
  `GiftTransactionMirrorSchedulable` (R-GT6), `GiftTransactionMirrorReconciliation` (R-GT10),
  `GiftTransactionMirrorController` and the `giftTransactionMirror` page reached from the Giving
  section of BarnCRM Settings. Shared with the Opportunity mirror: `MirrorSync`,
  `MirrorSettingsWriter` (the runs' record of their last completed run),
  `MirrorGivingHealthCheckExtension` (the stale run finding) and
  `MirrorGivingNightlyJobProvider` (the nightly jobs list), all in Mirror for Giving. Permission set: `Salesforce_Records_Sync` (retired `Gift_Transaction_Mirror`
  until the next release, ADR-0194 D4), which also carries the custom
  permission `Use_Gift_Transaction_Mirror`: the page's reads require it, and the console shows
  the page's row only to someone who has it. It is offered on the Access page through an
  `Access_Add_On__mdt` row.
- **List views** `Gifts_And_Gift_Transactions` on Gift, where Gift Transaction ID is typed or
  cleared (R-GT9), and `Funds_And_Gift_Designations` on Fund, where Gift Designation ID is typed
  (R-GT5), both shipped by Mirror for Giving.
