## 29J. Volunteer Job

### Definition

A piece of work the organization needs volunteers for: sorting the food pantry, driving the
van, staffing the front desk (V-01). It is the durable thing; a shift (29K) is one dated
occurrence of it.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | What the job is called, in the words the coordinator uses when asking for help. |
| Description | long text | no | What the volunteer will be doing, and anything to know before arriving. |
| Location | text | no | Where the work happens, when it is the same for every shift. |
| Coordinator | reference(User) | no | The staff member who runs this job. |
| Active | boolean | yes (defaults true) | Whether this job is offered when a new shift is scheduled. |
| Event ID | text | no | Set by Event Management (EV-08) when the job was made for an event: the event's record ID kept as text, never a lookup (ADR-0177 decision 12). Empty for every other job. |
| Total Hours | decimal | computed | Approved hours ever recorded against this job. |
| Last Volunteer Date | date | computed | The most recent day anybody worked this job. |
| Totals Last Updated | datetime | computed | When BarnCRM last worked out this job's totals. |
| Sample Data | boolean | yes (defaults false) | Set by the sample data loader so Remove Sample Data finds the job and everything hanging off it. |

### Relationships

- **Volunteer Job to Volunteer Shift**, one to many; the shift is a detail of the job.
- **Volunteer Job to Volunteer Hours**, one to many, so hours can be recorded against a job
  with no shift.
- Coordinator is a User, not a person pair: a coordinator is staff who logs in.

### Rules

**R-VJ1 A used job is deactivated, not deleted.** A job with shifts or hours is not deleted;
the message says to clear Active instead (as R-F2 for a fund). Hours of any status count,
Approved ones included: deleting the job would take its shifts and sign-ups with it and leave
hours that count in totals naming no job and no shift. The rule is enforced in Apex, before
the delete, by an automation that always runs (registry row `Volunteer_Job_Rules`, ADR-0024),
and it asks whether any shift or entry exists in the org (an existence check, never a count,
so a bulk delete of busy jobs stays inside the query row limit), including those the deleting
user cannot see.

**R-VJ2 An inactive job keeps its history.** Clearing Active stops it being offered on a new
shift and changes nothing already recorded, including its totals.

**R-VJ3 A job is public only by choice (V-09).** A job's Open shifts that start after now are
on the public sign-up page only while Show on Public Page and Active are both checked; its
Sign-Up Form (a published public form's record identifier) is the form those shifts offer.
What a guest is shown, and how a sign-up is booked, is ADR-0198 (volunteer self-service)
decisions 1 to 3: job name and description, shift start, end and location, and places left as
a count; never who is booked, the coordinator or notes. The form's answers `groupSize` (a whole
number from 1 to 50; anything else is 1) and `groupName` set the sign-up's Group Size and Group
Name. Without BarnCRM Forms there is no public page and both fields do nothing.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Volunteer_Job__c`, name field Text, label Job Name.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Description | `Description__c` | Long Text Area(32768) |
| Location | `Location__c` | Text(255) |
| Coordinator | `Coordinator__c` | Lookup to User |
| Active | `Active__c` | Checkbox, default true |
| Event ID | `Event_Key__c` | Text(18), external ID (EV-08) |
| Total Hours | `Total_Hours__c` | Number(10, 2) |
| Last Volunteer Date | `Last_Volunteer_Date__c` | Date |
| Totals Last Updated | `Rollups_Last_Calculated__c` | DateTime |
| Sample Data | `Sample_Data__c` | Checkbox, default false (v0.8) |
| Show on Public Page | `Public_Page__c` | Checkbox, default false (V-09, R-VJ3) |
| Sign-Up Form | `Signup_Form_Key__c` | Text(18) (V-09, R-VJ3) |

- **Public pages (V-09):** `VolunteerPublicPage` (`PublicPageExtension`, kind `volunteers`,
  without sharing, Without Sharing Register) and `VolunteerFormAttachment`
  (`FormAttachmentExtension`): shift pages and the list, the signed personal page (R-VU10).
- **Event extension:** `VolunteersEventExtension` (EV-08) lists and creates an event's jobs and
  shifts for Event Management through Core's `EventVolunteerExtension`.
- **Service:** `VolunteerJobTriggerHandler`, `VolunteerJobSelector`,
  `VolunteerIntegritySelector` (the R-VJ1 counts, without sharing).

---

## 29K. Volunteer Shift

### Definition

One dated occurrence of a job: the Saturday pantry sort on 14 March, nine until noon, four
volunteers wanted (V-01). It is what a volunteer signs up for and what a coordinator counts
heads on.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | What this shift is called. BarnCRM writes it from the job and the start when it is left empty. |
| Job | reference(Volunteer Job) | yes | The work being done. A shift is a detail of its job. |
| Start Time | datetime | yes | When the shift starts. |
| End Time | datetime | yes | When the shift ends. |
| Volunteers Needed | integer | yes (defaults 1) | How many people the coordinator wants on this shift. |
| Location | text | no | Where this shift happens, when it differs from the job's usual place. |
| Status | picklist(Open, Cancelled, Completed) | yes (defaults Open) | Where the shift stands. A cancelled shift is kept, so the people booked on it can still be found. |
| Shift Schedule | reference(Shift Schedule) | no | The recurring schedule that created this shift (V-07), empty for a shift created by hand. |
| Slots Filled | integer | computed | How many places are taken: the Places of sign-ups that are not Cancelled or Waitlisted (V-16). |
| Minimum Volunteers | integer | no | The fewest places the shift needs to go ahead (V-14, R-VS6). Empty means no minimum. |
| Below Minimum | boolean | computed | Whether Slots Filled is under Minimum Volunteers (R-VS6). |
| Slots Remaining | integer | computed | Volunteers Needed less Slots Filled. Negative when more came than were asked for, which is information, not an error. |
| Total Hours | decimal | computed | Approved hours recorded against this shift. |
| Totals Last Updated | datetime | computed | When BarnCRM last worked out this shift's totals. |
| Nudge Sent On | datetime | no | When the "still need you" email for this unfilled shift went out (V-10b, R-VU6a). Empty means none was sent. BarnCRM writes it; a coordinator clears it to send the nudge again. |

### Relationships

- **Volunteer Shift to Volunteer Job**, many to one, as a detail of the job.
- **Volunteer Shift to Volunteer Sign-up**, one to many; the sign-up is a detail of the shift.
- **Volunteer Shift to Volunteer Hours**, one to many, optional on the hours side.

### Rules

**R-VS1 A shift belongs to a job.** Master-detail, so who can see a shift is decided by who
can see its job: shifts are the schedule, not private data.

**R-VS2 A shift names itself.** A shift saved without a name gets one from its job and start,
for example "Food pantry sort: 14 Mar 2026, 9:00 AM". A typed name is never overwritten.

**R-VS3 A shift ends after it starts.** A validation rule, so it holds with automation off.

**R-VS4 Volunteers Needed is a target, not a limit.** A sign-up is never refused because a
shift is full; Slots Remaining goes negative and the coordinator sees it. With Waitlist When
Full on (29N, V-14), Volunteers Needed is the maximum: a new sign-up that does not fit is saved
as Waitlisted instead (R-VU8).

**R-VS6 A minimum only shows (V-14).** Minimum Volunteers, when set, is the fewest places the
shift needs to go ahead; Below Minimum is checked while Slots Filled is under it, and the
Shifts Below Minimum list view lists Open shifts still to come that are. Nothing is cancelled
or refused for it. A minimum above Volunteers Needed is refused (validation rule).

**R-VS5 Cancelling is not deleting.** Status Cancelled keeps the shift and its sign-ups.
Deleting a shift takes its sign-ups with it and leaves its hours, with the job, in place.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Volunteer_Shift__c`, name field Text, label Shift Name, sharing Controlled By
  Parent.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Job | `Volunteer_Job__c` | Master-Detail to `Volunteer_Job__c`, relationship name Shifts |
| Start Time | `Start_Time__c` | DateTime, required |
| End Time | `End_Time__c` | DateTime, required |
| Volunteers Needed | `Volunteers_Needed__c` | Number(4, 0), default 1 |
| Location | `Location__c` | Text(255) |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist: Open, Cancelled, Completed |
| Shift Schedule | `Shift_Schedule__c` | Lookup to `Shift_Schedule__c`, delete constraint SetNull (kept shifts survive a deleted schedule); ships with the Shift Schedule object (V-07) |
| Slots Filled | `Slots_Filled__c` | Number(4, 0) |
| Slots Remaining | `Slots_Remaining__c` | Formula (Number): `Volunteers_Needed__c` less `Slots_Filled__c` |
| Total Hours | `Total_Hours__c` | Number(10, 2) |
| Totals Last Updated | `Rollups_Last_Calculated__c` | DateTime |
| Nudge Sent On | `Nudge_Sent_On__c` | DateTime, read-only on the layout; editable (to clear) for Admin and Coordinator |
| Minimum Volunteers | `Minimum_Volunteers__c` | Number(4, 0) (V-14) |
| Below Minimum | `Below_Minimum__c` | Formula (Checkbox): Minimum Volunteers set and Slots Filled (blank as 0) below it (V-14) |

- **Validation rules:** `End_After_Start` (R-VS3), `Minimum_Within_Needed` (R-VS6).
- **List view:** `Shifts_Below_Minimum` (Open, Below Minimum, Start Time from today).
- **Slots Filled roll-up:** `Volunteer_Shift_Slots_Filled` sums `Places__c` of sign-ups whose
  Status is not Cancelled and not Waitlisted (V-16; was a count of sign-ups not Cancelled). An
  org that installed the earlier definition keeps it until an admin edits it in Rollup Builder.
- **Service:** `VolunteerShiftTriggerHandler`, `VolunteerShiftSelector`.

---

## 29L. Volunteer Sign-up

### Definition

A person, or a group with its leader, booked onto a shift (V-02, V-16). It is the intention;
Volunteer Hours (29M) is the record of what happened. Staff enter sign-ups; volunteers also sign
up on the portal (PB-03) and on the public sign-up page (V-09, R-VJ3).

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | An auto number: a sign-up is identified by its person and shift. |
| Volunteer Shift | reference(Volunteer Shift) | yes | The shift the person is booked onto. A sign-up is a detail of the shift. |
| Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person, where people are Contacts. |
| Account | reference(Account) | conditional | The person, where people are person Accounts. |
| Status | picklist(Signed up, Confirmed, Attended, No show, Cancelled, Waitlisted) | yes (defaults Signed up) | Where this booking stands, up to whether the person turned up. Waitlisted holds no place (V-14, R-VU8). |
| Notes | text | no | Anything the coordinator needs to remember about this booking. |
| Group Size | integer | no (defaults 1) | How many people this booking holds, the leader (the person named) included (V-16). |
| Group Name | text | no | The group's name, such as a company or a class (V-16). |
| Places | integer | computed | Group Size, or 1 when it is empty: the places this booking takes (V-16). |
| Standing | boolean | no (defaults false) | Whether the person holds this shift every time its recurring schedule repeats (V-16, R-VU9). |
| Consent Needed | boolean | computed | Set by BarnCRM when the person is a minor with no current guardian consent (V-15, R-VU11). |
| Reminder Sent On | datetime | no | When the shift reminder email for this booking went out (V-10, R-VU6). Empty means none was sent. BarnCRM writes it; a coordinator clears it to send the reminder again. |

### Relationships

- **Volunteer Sign-up to Volunteer Shift**, many to one, as a detail of the shift.
- **Volunteer Sign-up to a person**, through the Contact and Account pair (Section 4).
- **Volunteer Sign-up to Volunteer Hours**, one to at most one, when attendance created the
  hours (R-VU3).

### Rules

**R-VU1 Exactly one person.** Contact or Account, never both, never neither (validation rule).
In a Person Account org a person is named by the Account side (Section 4). A sign-up or an
hours entry that names a person account's person contact on the Contact side is not rewritten
to the Account side: Gift does not rewrite its donor pair either, and the entry points that create them (the sign-up and hours screens,
the hours import) are where the side is chosen. Such a record still saves, but its household
(R-VG2) and the one sign-up per person check (R-VU2) see the person contact as a different
person from the account. If the pairs are ever normalized, it is done for every pair at once,
in Core.

**R-VU2 One sign-up per person per shift.** A second one for the same person on the same
shift is refused, naming the shift: it is always a mistake and would double the filled count.
Every sign-up in the org counts, a cancelled one and one the user cannot see included. The
check runs on insert, when the shift or person changes, and on undelete: restoring a sign-up
for a person since booked onto the shift again is refused.

**R-VU3 Marking attendance can write the hours.** When Attendance Creates Hours is on (29N),
moving a sign-up to Attended creates one Volunteer Hours entry for that person, dated the
shift's start, for the shift's length, against the shift and its job, naming the sign-up.
Marking attendance again creates no second entry, and moving the sign-up away from Attended
deletes nothing: removing hours a coordinator may have approved is left to a person. Undeleting
an old entry for a sign-up another entry already records is refused, so one attendance stays
one entry. A sign-up whose shift has no end time, ends before it starts, or cannot be read gets
no entry; its attendance is still saved and a Warning in the Error Log names the sign-up, so
the hours are typed by hand. While automation is paused or the sign-up automation is switched
off, marking attendance writes no hours and nothing writes them later: the coordinator enters
them by hand (admin guide, volunteers page).

**R-VU4 A cancelled sign-up stops counting.** Slots Filled sums the Places of sign-ups whose
Status is not Cancelled or Waitlisted, so someone who drops out frees the place without the
booking being deleted.

**R-VU8 Waitlist and promotion (V-14).** With Waitlist When Full on (29N, off by default), a
sign-up saved as Signed up or Confirmed on a shift with Volunteers Needed set is checked against
the places free, counted now from the sign-ups (not Slots Filled, which a roll-up updates a
moment later), in the order given: one that does not fit is saved as Waitlisted, and one that
does fit takes its places (Core `WaitlistQueue`, ADR-0198 volunteer self-service decision 5).
When places free up (a sign-up Cancelled or deleted, a group made smaller, or Volunteers
Needed raised) on a shift still to come, Waitlisted sign-ups
are promoted to Signed up, oldest first by Created Date, each that fits taking its places; a
group too big for what is free is passed over for a smaller one behind it. Counting and
promotion run in system mode in the same transaction, so a portal or form sign-up and one the
user cannot see are handled alike, and send no email of their own (the shift reminder, R-VU6, goes
out as for any booking). With the setting off nothing is waitlisted or promoted, and a sign-up
a coordinator sets to Waitlisted by hand stays so until changed.

**R-VU9 A standing sign-up repeats (V-16).** A sign-up with Standing checked on a shift of a
recurring schedule (29T) books the same person, Group Size and Group Name on every later Open
shift of that schedule they have no sign-up on: when the schedule creates shifts (R-SSC2) and
when a sign-up becomes standing. The person's latest sign-up on the schedule (by shift start)
decides: the booking continues while that one is Standing and not Cancelled, so cancelling the
future ones from a given day ends it. Each copy goes through the sign-up rules (R-VU2, R-VU8,
R-VU11) and is itself Standing. A standing sign-up does not keep a future shift when the
schedule's pattern changes (R-SSC4): it is removed with the shift, and the person continues on
the new pattern's shifts.

**R-VU10 The personal page and profile (V-09).** A sign-up is the person's own record, so a
public link to it carries a signed claim (ADR-0188). With a Self-Service Profile Form set (29N)
and BarnCRM Forms on an active Site, the shift reminder adds the person's link; it opens a page
with their upcoming bookings, approved hours this year and in total with their value (R-VP5) and
their latest ten approved entries, and the profile form, whose answers `availabilityDays`,
`availabilityTimes`, `emergencyContactName` and `emergencyContactPhone` overwrite those
fields on the person the sign-up names (blank answers are left out), never on a person the
answers name. Read and written in system mode by `VolunteerPublicPage` and
`VolunteerFormAttachment`, for that person only, and only after the host checked the claim.

**R-VU11 Minors and guardian consent (V-15).** With Guardian Consent Required on (29N, off by
default), a sign-up that is new, or whose person changes, for a Contact whose Birthdate makes
them younger than Minor Age (default 18) on the shift's day, with no current Guardian consent
requirement (29S), is saved with Consent Needed checked, and a Guardian consent requirement Not
started is created for them unless one that is not current is already open (Not started or In
progress). A public sign-up whose form wrote a person under the record key `guardian` names that
person as the requirement's Guardian. The requirement is created in system mode (requirements are
kept to coordinators, R-VQ4). Consent Needed records the check at booking; the person's
onboarding card (R-VQ3) shows whether consent is current now. Nothing is refused: the coordinator decides (R-VQ3). A person with
no Birthdate, or named by an Account, is not checked. Done by `VolunteerMinors`, from the
`Volunteer_Signup_Rules` handler; R-VU8 by `VolunteerCapacity` and R-VU9 by `VolunteerStanding`.

**R-VU5 Erasing the person keeps their sign-ups.** Erasing a person (Section 29H) keeps every
sign-up naming them, so shift counts stand, and empties its Notes. A sign-up Signed up or
Confirmed on a shift that has not started is set to Cancelled, so the place is freed and nobody
expects the person. Done by `VolunteersErasureExtension`, as the user (R-ER5).

**R-VU6 One reminder per booking.** When Send Shift Reminders is on (29N), a morning job at
7:00 AM (`VolunteerReminderScheduler`, one of the two Volunteers nightly jobs Health Check
schedules) emails each booking that is Signed up or Confirmed, on an open shift that starts
after now and before the start of the day Days Before a Shift to Remind after today (org time
zone), once: each due booking is stamped Reminder Sent On first, and only bookings whose stamp saved
are emailed; a booking whose stamp could not be saved is not emailed (so it is never emailed
twice) and is listed in the Error Log as a Warning, and a booking whose email failed has its
stamp cleared so the next morning's run tries again. A stamped booking is never emailed again.
A booking made after that morning's run for a shift starting before the next morning's run gets
no reminder. Nobody is emailed whose Contact has Email Opt Out
checked or no email address. In an org that stores people as accounts, a booking named by a
person account with no Contact (as the Sign-ups panel books one) is reminded at the account's
own email, under the same opt out and blank address rules, read by name so no packaged metadata
names a person account field (QA-F3). The email goes through the platform's single email call to
the person's own address, so the org's daily email limit applies: a message the platform refuses is not stamped,
a Warning in the Error Log counts them, and the next morning's run tries them again while the
shift is still ahead. Reminders ship off.

**R-VU6a One nudge per unfilled shift (V-10b).** When Send Unfilled Shift Nudges is on (29N), a
nightly step at 7:15 AM (`VolunteerNudgeScheduler`, a third Volunteers nightly job, no switch of
its own) emails, for each Open shift that starts after now and before the start of the day Days
Before a Shift to Nudge after today (org time zone, default 3, 1 to 14), whose Slots Remaining is
above zero and whose Nudge Sent On is empty, the active volunteers (Volunteer Status Active) with
approved hours on the shift's job, an email address and Email Opt Out unchecked, who have no
sign-up of any status on the shift: the most hours first, at most three per open place and 25 per
shift. People are Contacts; a person account volunteer is reached through the contact behind the
account. Like R-VU6 the shift is stamped Nudge Sent On first and emailed only if the stamp saved
(a failed stamp is a Warning in the Error Log); a shift none of whose emails went out has the
stamp cleared so the next morning retries; a stamped shift is never nudged again; a shift with
no one to write to stays stamped. The email goes through the platform's single email call, so
the org's daily email limit applies. Nudges ship off.

**R-VU7 Suggestions are read only and rank on data already held.** The Suggested Volunteers
card on an Open shift (V-11) offers Contacts whose Volunteer Status is Active and who have no
sign-up of any status on the shift (R-VU2 would refuse a second), up to the 500 with the most
total hours. Per person it gathers the available days, the skills and interests that match the
job's required skills (Job Skill), approved hours on the job and in total, and onboarding
(`cleared` when the latest step of each Type is current, `open` when one is not, `none` when
the user sees no steps). It ranks them with the documented weights (admin guide, Suggested
Volunteers): skills up to 30 (share of required skills held), interests up to 10 (required
skills held only as interests), an available day +25 or minus 25 when days are listed and the
shift's is not one, hours on the job up to 20 (capped at 40), total hours up to 5 (capped at
200), onboarding cleared +10 or open minus 15. The ranking is the framework-free module
`rankSuggestions`; Apex only gathers facts, in user mode, so a user sees suggestions only from
what they may read. Nothing is written: booking uses `VolunteerShiftSignupsController.addSignup`,
so R-VU1 to R-VU4 apply. The card shows nothing to a user who cannot create sign-ups or for a
shift that is not Open. In an org that stores people as accounts the Contacts read include the
contact behind each person account; that person is suggested by the account, as the Sign-ups
panel books them, and one already booked on the shift by the account is left out (QA-F3).

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Volunteer_Signup__c`, name field AutoNumber `VS-{000000}`, sharing Controlled
  By Parent.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Volunteer Shift | `Volunteer_Shift__c` | Master-Detail to `Volunteer_Shift__c`, relationship name Signups |
| Contact | `Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact, delete constraint SetNull |
| Account | `Account__c` | Lookup to Account, delete constraint SetNull |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist: Signed up, Confirmed, Attended, No show, Cancelled, Waitlisted; required, default Signed up |
| Notes | `Notes__c` | Text Area(255) |
| Group Size | `Group_Size__c` | Number(4, 0), default 1 (V-16) |
| Group Name | `Group_Name__c` | Text(80) (V-16) |
| Places | `Places__c` | Formula (Number, 0): `IF(OR(ISBLANK(Group_Size__c), Group_Size__c < 1), 1, Group_Size__c)` (V-16) |
| Standing | `Standing__c` | Checkbox, default false (V-16) |
| Consent Needed | `Consent_Needed__c` | Checkbox, default false, read only in every set (V-15) |
| Reminder Sent On | `Reminder_Sent_On__c` | DateTime, read-only on the layout; editable (to clear) for Admin and Coordinator |

- **Reminders:** `VolunteerReminderScheduler` (7:00 AM) starts `VolunteerReminderBatch` (100
  bookings per transaction), which reads through `VolunteerReminderSelector` (system mode) and
  sends through `VolunteerReminderService`.
- **Validation rules:** `Exactly_One_Person` (R-VU1), checked only when the sign-up is new or
  its Contact or Account changes, so a sign-up whose person was deleted (the lookup cleared by
  SetNull) can still be edited.
- **Service:** `VolunteerSignupService`, `VolunteerSignupTriggerHandler`,
  `VolunteerIntegritySelector` (the R-VU2 and R-VU3 checks read every sign-up and entry in the
  org, without sharing, so a booking or an entry the user cannot see still counts).

## 29M. Volunteer Hours

### Definition

Time a person actually gave, entered by staff and approved by a coordinator (V-02). Every
volunteer number in the product is calculated from it, which is why approval is part of the
record.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | An auto number: an entry is identified by its person, date and job. |
| Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person who gave the time, where people are Contacts. |
| Account | reference(Account) | conditional | The person who gave the time, where people are person Accounts. |
| Household | reference(Household) | computed | The household credited with this time. BarnCRM fills it in from the person. |
| Job | reference(Volunteer Job) | conditional | The work that was done. Filled from the shift when a shift is named. |
| Volunteer Shift | reference(Volunteer Shift) | no | The shift the time was given on, when it was a scheduled shift. |
| Volunteer Sign-up | reference(Volunteer Sign-up) | no | The booking these hours were created from, when attendance created them. |
| Date Worked | date | yes | The day the time was given. |
| Hours | decimal | yes | How many hours, to two decimal places. |
| Status | picklist(Submitted, Approved, Rejected) | yes (defaults Submitted) | Where this entry stands with the coordinator. |
| Reviewed By | reference(User) | computed | Who approved or rejected the entry. |
| Reviewed Date | datetime | computed | When they did it. |
| Rejection Reason | text | conditional | Why the entry was rejected; required when rejecting. |
| Notes | text | no | What the person did, when it is worth recording. |

### Relationships

- **Volunteer Hours to a person**, through the Contact and Account pair (Section 4).
- **Volunteer Hours to Household**, many to one, written by the module, never typed (R-VG2),
  the same shape as Gift so a household total is a rollup over one reference.
- **Volunteer Hours to Volunteer Job, Volunteer Shift and Volunteer Sign-up**, many to one,
  plain lookups, so hours survive a shift or sign-up being deleted.

### Rules

**R-VG1 Exactly one person.** Contact or Account, never both, never neither (validation rule).

**R-VG2 The household is derived.** From the person's household through `HouseholdService`,
in both membership modes, as R-G2 does for a gift: set when the entry is saved, recomputed
only when its person changes, empty when the person has no household. Hours stay with the
household they were given in when the person later moves (ADR-0071), and that household is
kept by the empty household tidy-ups and an import undo while any entry names it, through
`VolunteersHouseholdDependentsExtension` (R-H12, R-H12a). A household merge moves the entries
to the household kept, by the platform's merge.

**R-VG3 An entry names a job.** A validation rule requires the job or the shift; the module
fills the job from the shift, so a shift deleted later leaves the hours with their job.

**R-VG4 Hours are greater than zero** (validation rule): zero hours is a mistake or an
attendance record, and attendance is a sign-up.

**R-VG5 Approval is a status moved by a service.** Status, Reviewed By and Reviewed Date (API
names `Approved_By__c` and `Approved_Date__c`, unchanged) are moved only by `VolunteerHoursService`, which refuses a user without the custom permission
`Manage_Volunteers`; a Status change made any other way is refused. It is not a Salesforce
approval process (ADR-0127, decision 4). The service has four verbs: submit (create entries,
which start Submitted, or Approved under R-VG6), approve (any entry not yet Approved: Reviewed
By and Reviewed Date are the coordinator and now, any Rejection Reason is cleared), reject
(R-VG8: Reviewed By and Reviewed Date record who rejected and when) and reopen (an Approved or
Rejected entry back to Submitted, those three fields cleared). Each verb saves entry by entry
and reports any it could not move (one the user may see but not edit) without stopping the
rest. Outside the service a new entry is saved Submitted, or Approved when Hours Require
Approval is off, and naming any other status is refused; on a saved entry a change to Status,
Reviewed By, Reviewed Date or Rejection Reason is refused. Two layers hold this. The hours
automation (`Volunteer_Hours_Rules`) refuses the change for everyone outside the service. The
validation rule `Status_Needs_Manage_Volunteers` refuses it for any user without
`Manage_Volunteers`, so it holds while automation is paused or switched off. New entries are
not covered by the validation rule: with automation paused, an import of past hours may load
them already Approved.

**R-VG6 Only approved hours count.** Every rollup in 29O filters on Status equals Approved.
With Hours Require Approval off (29N), entries are created Approved, by the saving user at the
save time, and count at once.

**R-VG7 An approved entry is locked.** While Status is Approved, its person, Date Worked and
Hours cannot change: the coordinator moves it back to Submitted, edits it and approves it
again. A validation rule, so it holds with automation off. Merging two people is not such a
change: the platform's merge moves the duplicate's entries, approved ones included, to the
surviving person without running the rule or the hours automation, so the entry keeps the
household it was given in (R-VG2) (`VolunteerHoursTriggerHandlerTest`,
`VolunteerHoursPermissionTest`).

**R-VG8 Rejecting says why.** A rejection without a Rejection Reason is refused by the
service.

**R-VG9 Approved hours are not deleted.** Deleting an Approved entry is refused for everyone,
a coordinator with Modify All included: it counts in totals, and deleting it would change them
with nothing on record. The message says to reopen it (back to Submitted, which needs
`Manage_Volunteers`) and then delete it. A validation rule cannot block a delete, so the rule
is Apex before the delete, in an automation that always runs (registry row
`Volunteer_Hours_Delete_Guard`, ADR-0024): no switch or pause suspends it.

**R-VG10 Erasing the person keeps their hours.** Erasing a person (Section 29H) keeps every
entry naming them, with its status, date and hours, still credited to the anonymized person, so
every total stands, as Giving keeps gifts (ADR-0110). Notes is emptied, as the user (R-ER5).
Nothing else changes, so an Approved entry, locked by R-VG7 against a change of person, date or
hours, is erased like any other. The five volunteer totals on the person (29O) are fields the
module keeps (`fieldsToKeep`, R-ER1), as Core already keeps the target of every rollup the
engine reports: naming them also covers a total whose definition the administrator deleted,
which is read only to every user and would otherwise refuse the erasure. They are anonymous
aggregates like a donor level, and emptying them would leave totals that disagree with the
hours kept.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Volunteer_Hours__c`, name field AutoNumber `VH-{000000}`, sharing Private.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Contact | `Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact |
| Account | `Account__c` | Lookup to Account |
| Household | `Household__c` | Lookup to Account |
| Job | `Volunteer_Job__c` | Lookup to `Volunteer_Job__c` |
| Volunteer Shift | `Volunteer_Shift__c` | Lookup to `Volunteer_Shift__c` (clears on delete) |
| Volunteer Sign-up | `Volunteer_Signup__c` | Lookup to `Volunteer_Signup__c` (clears on delete) |
| Date Worked | `Date_Worked__c` | Date, required |
| Hours | `Hours__c` | Number(6, 2), required |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist: Submitted, Approved, Rejected |
| Reviewed By | `Approved_By__c` | Lookup to User |
| Reviewed Date | `Approved_Date__c` | DateTime |
| Rejection Reason | `Rejection_Reason__c` | Text(255) |
| Notes | `Notes__c` | Text Area(255) |

- **Validation rules:** `Exactly_One_Person` (R-VG1), `Job_Or_Shift_Required` (R-VG3),
  `Hours_Must_Be_Positive` (R-VG4), `Approved_Hours_Are_Locked` (R-VG7),
  `Status_Needs_Manage_Volunteers` (R-VG5).
- **Custom permission:** `Manage_Volunteers`, in `Volunteers_Coordinator` and
  `Volunteers_Admin` (R-VG5).
- **Service:** `VolunteerHoursService`, `VolunteerHoursTriggerHandler`,
  `VolunteerHoursDeleteGuardHandler` (R-VG9),
  `VolunteerHoursSelector`, `VolunteerHoursWriter` (the status save, in system mode because
  Reviewed By and Reviewed Date are read only in every permission set; ADR-0021).

## 29N. Volunteer Settings

### Definition

The Volunteers module's own org-wide settings (ADR-0017: each module owns a protected
hierarchy custom setting), edited in the BarnCRM Settings console's Volunteers section (the
module has no settings page of its own), never in Setup. Defaults are applied in Apex
(ADR-0035, `VolunteerSettings`): a blank or out of range value reads as the shipped one.

| Key | Type | Default | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Hours_Require_Approval__c` | boolean | true | Whether hours are entered as Submitted and wait for a coordinator. Off means an entry is Approved as it is saved and counts at once (R-VG6). |
| `Attendance_Creates_Hours__c` | boolean | true | Whether marking a sign-up Attended writes the hours for that shift (R-VU3). |
| `Shift_Horizon_Weeks__c` | integer, 1 to 26 | 8 | How many weeks ahead recurring schedules keep their shifts created (V-07). |
| `Reminders_Enabled__c` | boolean | false | Whether bookings get one reminder email before their shift (V-10, R-VU6). Ships off, because turning it on emails real people. |
| `Reminder_Lead_Days__c` | integer, 1 to 14 | 1 | How many days before a shift its reminder goes out (V-10). |
| `Nudges_Enabled__c` | boolean | false | Whether an unfilled shift emails the job's regular volunteers once (V-10b, R-VU6a). Ships off, because turning it on emails real people. |
| `Nudge_Lead_Days__c` | integer, 1 to 14 | 3 | How many days before an unfilled shift its nudge goes out (V-10b). |
| `Hour_Value__c` | decimal, 0 to 9999.99 | 34.79 | The value of one volunteer hour in the org's currency (V-12, R-VP5). 0 hides every value. |
| `Recognition_Enabled__c` | boolean | false | Whether milestone and anniversary thank-you Tasks are created (V-13, R-VP4). Ships off. |
| `Hour_Milestones__c` | text | `25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000` | The total hours that earn a thank-you, separated by commas (V-13). A part that is not a whole number above 0 is ignored; with none left the shipped list applies. |
| `Waitlist_Enabled__c` | boolean | false | Whether a full shift waitlists new sign-ups and promotes them when places free up (V-14, R-VU8). Ships off, because it changes what a sign-up on a full shift does. |
| `Minor_Consent_Required__c` | boolean | false | Whether a minor's sign-up is flagged and gets a guardian consent step (V-15, R-VU11). Ships off. |
| `Minor_Age__c` | integer, 1 to 21 | 18 | The age below which a volunteer is a minor (V-15). |
| `Profile_Form_Key__c` | text | empty | The record identifier of the published public form a volunteer's personal page offers (V-09, R-VU10). Empty means no personal page; there is no form to default to. |

**R-VP5 The value of hours only displays (V-12).** Hour Value times approved hours is shown as
Value of Hours This Month on Volunteers Home, on the personal page (R-VU10) and in hour letters
through `{HoursValue}` (the person's hours in the period times the rate) and `{HourValue}` (the
rate), in the org's default currency. Nothing stores a value. At 0 the figure and the personal
page's value are left out, and both tokens merge as empty.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Custom setting:** `Volunteer_Settings__c`, hierarchy, protected.

| Key | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Hours Require Approval | `Hours_Require_Approval__c` | Checkbox, default true |
| Attendance Creates Hours | `Attendance_Creates_Hours__c` | Checkbox, default true |
| Weeks Ahead to Create Shifts | `Shift_Horizon_Weeks__c` | Number(2, 0) |
| Send Shift Reminders | `Reminders_Enabled__c` | Checkbox, default false |
| Days Before a Shift to Remind | `Reminder_Lead_Days__c` | Number(2, 0), default 1 |
| Send Unfilled Shift Nudges | `Nudges_Enabled__c` | Checkbox, default false |
| Days Before a Shift to Nudge | `Nudge_Lead_Days__c` | Number(2, 0), default 3 |
| Value of One Volunteer Hour | `Hour_Value__c` | Number(6, 2), default 34.79 |
| Send Thank-You Tasks | `Recognition_Enabled__c` | Checkbox, default false |
| Hour Milestones | `Hour_Milestones__c` | Text(255), default `25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000` |
| Waitlist When Full | `Waitlist_Enabled__c` | Checkbox, default false |
| Guardian Consent Required | `Minor_Consent_Required__c` | Checkbox, default false |
| Minor Age | `Minor_Age__c` | Number(2, 0), default 18 |
| Self-Service Profile Form | `Profile_Form_Key__c` | Text(18) |

- **Setting Definition rows:** `Settings_Object__c` `Volunteer_Settings__c`, `Module__c`
  Volunteers, `Section__c` Volunteers, one per key.

## 29O. Packaged default volunteer rollups

### Definition

The Rollup Definitions Volunteers ships for hours on a person, a household, a job and a shift,
and the filled count on a shift (V-03). They follow Section 26: shipped as
`Rollup_Definition_Default__mdt` rows with `Package__c` Volunteers, materialized by
`VolunteersPostInstall` into the Rollup Builder module's `Rollup_Definition__c` (Section 14),
each editable and deactivatable by the admin. Volunteers ships definitions, not aggregation
code, and requires BarnCRM Rollup Builder (ADR-0127, decision 1).

Target scopes are Section 26's three disjoint ones, with paths from Volunteer Hours:
Household (record type Household, `Household__c`), Account (record type not Household,
`Account__c`) and Contact (`Contact__c`). Definition keys follow the scope, for example
`Household_Volunteer_Hours_Total`.

### Volunteer totals on Account and Contact

Source Volunteer Hours, base filter Status equals Approved (R-VG6), mode Both, fiscal windows
on Date Worked. Five rows per scope, fifteen in all.

| Target attribute | Aggregate | Source attribute | Extra filter | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Volunteer_Hours_Total__c` | SUM | `Hours__c` | none | Every approved hour this person or household has given. |
| `Volunteer_Hours_This_Year__c` | SUM | `Hours__c` | fiscal year offset 0 | Approved hours in the current fiscal year. |
| `Volunteer_Hours_Last_Year__c` | SUM | `Hours__c` | fiscal year offset -1 | Approved hours in the previous fiscal year. |
| `First_Volunteer_Date__c` | MIN | `Date_Worked__c` | none | The first day this person gave time, which a service award counts from. |
| `Last_Volunteer_Date__c` | MAX | `Date_Worked__c` | none | The most recent day they gave time, which a lapsed volunteer report counts from. |

### Totals on Volunteers objects

Four rows, mode Both.

| Target entity | Target attribute | Source | Aggregate | Source attribute | Filter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Volunteer Job | `Total_Hours__c` | Volunteer Hours | SUM | `Hours__c` | Status equals Approved |
| Volunteer Job | `Last_Volunteer_Date__c` | Volunteer Hours | MAX | `Date_Worked__c` | Status equals Approved |
| Volunteer Shift | `Total_Hours__c` | Volunteer Hours | SUM | `Hours__c` | Status equals Approved |
| Volunteer Shift | `Slots_Filled__c` | Volunteer Sign-up | COUNT | none | Status not equal to Cancelled (R-VU4) |

### Rules

**R-VR1 Freshness without Giving.** `Rollups_Last_Calculated__c` on Account and Contact is
shipped by Giving (Section 26). In an org without Giving the engine finds no stamp there and
writes none: the totals are right, and the person page shows no "last calculated" line.
Volunteers ships no second stamp, because two packages cannot define one API name on Account
and a differently named twin would answer the same question twice. Jobs and shifts carry the
module's own stamp.

**R-VR2 Turned off, then on.** While Volunteers is turned off (ADR-0073) its registry rows do
not run, so its saves queue no recalculation. The nightly run still recalculates the totals
while the module is off; only turning Rollup Builder off stops it. After Turn on the totals
catch up at the next nightly run (mode Both), or at once with Recalculate all.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Fields on Contact, and on Account with the same API names** (shipped by Volunteers):

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Volunteer Hours Total | `Volunteer_Hours_Total__c` | Number(10, 2) |
| Volunteer Hours This Year | `Volunteer_Hours_This_Year__c` | Number(10, 2) |
| Volunteer Hours Last Year | `Volunteer_Hours_Last_Year__c` | Number(10, 2) |
| First Volunteer Date | `First_Volunteer_Date__c` | Date |
| Last Volunteer Date | `Last_Volunteer_Date__c` | Date |

- **Shipped defaults:** 19 `Rollup_Definition_Default__mdt` rows, `Package__c` Volunteers,
  `Mode__c` Both, `Default_Active__c` true.
- **Automation Registry:** `Volunteers_Rollups_Hours` (Volunteer Hours) and
  `Volunteers_Rollups_Signup` (Volunteer Sign-up), handler `RollupTriggerHandler`, order 90,
  `Module__c` Volunteers.

## 29P. Skill

Sections 29P to 29V cover V-04 to V-08, beside the volunteer profile, Job
(`Volunteer_Job__c`), Shift (`Volunteer_Shift__c`), Sign-up (`Volunteer_Signup__c`), Hours
(`Volunteer_Hours__c`) and Volunteer Settings (`Volunteer_Settings__c`) of Sections 29I to 29O
(ADR-0127). Nothing here is added to Core except the three Import Template Default fields in
Section 13. A person reference is the pair in Section 4: `Contact__c` and `Account__c`, exactly
one set.

### Definition

One entry in the organization's list of volunteer skills and interests, for example "Spanish",
"Forklift licence" or "Working with children" (feature V-04). The list is the admin's own; the
package ships no skills.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | The skill as staff see it in pickers and filters. |
| Description | long text | no | What the skill means here, for example which licence counts. |
| Active | boolean | yes (defaults true) | Whether the skill is offered when a skill is added to a person or a job. |
| Sample Data | boolean | yes (defaults false) | Set by the sample data loader so Remove Sample Data finds the skill. |

### Relationships

- **Skill to Volunteer Skill** and **Skill to Job Skill**, one to many.

### Rules

**R-SK1 Archive, do not delete.** A skill that a person or a job holds cannot be deleted; the
admin clears Active instead. An inactive skill stays on the people and jobs that hold it and is
refused for new ones: a Volunteer Skill or Job Skill that is created, or moved to another
skill, may not name an inactive skill. A row that already holds a skill keeps it when the skill
is retired, and a merge that moves a person's rows to the person kept is not refused.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Skill__c`, Text Name (80), sharing Read, tab in the Volunteers app.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Description | `Description__c` | Long Text Area (2000) |
| Active | `Active__c` | Checkbox, default true |
| Sample Data | `Sample_Data__c` | Checkbox, default false (v0.8) |

---

## 29Q. Volunteer Skill

### Definition

That a person has a skill or is interested in one (feature V-04). When a person can volunteer
is held on the person, in the multi-select attributes `Availability_Days__c` and
`Availability_Times__c` that the volunteer profile defines.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | computed | An identifier assigned automatically. |
| Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person, where people are Contacts. |
| Person Account | reference(Organization) | conditional | The person, where people are person Accounts. |
| Skill | reference(Skill) | yes | The skill or interest. |
| Type | picklist(Skill, Interest) | yes (defaults Skill) | Skill: the person can do it. Interest: the person would like to. |

### Relationships

- **Volunteer Skill to the person**, many to one, to exactly one of Contact or Person Account.
- **Volunteer Skill to Skill**, many to one.

### Rules

**R-VK1 One person.** Exactly one of Contact and Person Account is set (Section 4).

**R-VK2 Duplicates are harmless.** The skills editor on the person never adds a pair the person
already holds. A duplicate written another way (an import, the API) changes no answer, because
matching asks whether a person holds a skill, not how many times, so no automation guards it.

**R-VK3 Matching a shift.** "Find volunteers" for a shift lists people whose Volunteer Status is
Active, who hold every skill of Type Skill that the shift's job lists (Section 29R), and whose
`Availability_Days__c` includes the shift's weekday and whose `Availability_Times__c` includes
the part of the day the shift starts in (before 12:00, 12:00 to 17:00, from 17:00). A person
with no availability recorded is listed last rather than left out. Interests matching the job's
skills are shown beside each name; they never filter.

**R-VK4 Deleted with the person.** Deleting a person deletes their volunteer skills, as it
deletes their requirements (R-VQ5 says how).

**R-VK5 Erased with the person.** Erasing a person (Section 29H) deletes their volunteer skills
and empties them from the Recycle Bin, as it does their requirements (R-VQ4): a skill or an
interest is a fact about the person, like the availability the erasure empties on the person
itself.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Volunteer_Skill__c`, auto-number Name `VK-{000000}`, sharing Read.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Contact | `Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact (the platform empties it when the person is deleted, and the row is then deleted, R-VK4) |
| Person Account | `Account__c` | Lookup to Account (the same, R-VK4) |
| Skill | `Skill__c` | Required lookup to `Skill__c` (refuses deleting a skill in use, R-SK1) |
| Type | `Type__c` | Required picklist: Skill, Interest (default Skill) |

- **Validation rules:** `Volunteer_Skill_One_Person` (R-VK1), `Volunteer_Skill_Active_Skill`
  (R-SK1: a new row, or a row moved to another skill, names an active skill).
- **Related lists:** Volunteer Skills on the Skill page layout. On the person, the admin adds
  the list to the organization's person layout (the module cannot edit Core's layout).

## 29R. Job Skill

### Definition

A skill a job needs (feature V-04), used to find volunteers for its shifts (R-VK3).

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | computed | An identifier assigned automatically. |
| Job | reference(Job) | yes | The job. |
| Skill | reference(Skill) | yes | The skill the job needs. |

### Relationships

- **Job Skill to Job**, many to one; deleting the job deletes its job skills.
- **Job Skill to Skill**, many to one.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Job_Skill__c`, auto-number Name `JK-{000000}`, sharing controlled by the job.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Job | `Job__c` | Master-Detail to `Volunteer_Job__c` |
| Skill | `Skill__c` | Required lookup to `Skill__c` (refuses deleting a skill in use, R-SK1) |

- **Validation rule:** `Job_Skill_Active_Skill` (R-SK1: a new row, or a row moved to another
  skill, names an active skill).
- **Related lists:** Job Skills on the Volunteer Job page layout.

## 29S. Volunteer Requirement

### Definition

One onboarding step for one person: an application, a background check or an orientation,
with where it stands and when it lapses (feature V-05). A person has one requirement row per
step they have started, and a new row when a lapsed step is done again.

The result of a background check is kept here and nowhere else: no person field records it, so
it is seen only by those who may see requirements and it leaves with them (R-VQ4).

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | computed | An identifier assigned automatically. |
| Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person, where people are Contacts. |
| Person Account | reference(Organization) | conditional | The person, where people are person Accounts. |
| Type | picklist(Application, Background check, Orientation, Guardian consent) | yes | Which onboarding step this is. The admin may add values. Guardian consent is a minor's (V-15, R-VU11). |
| Status | picklist(Not started, In progress, Completed, Not approved) | yes (defaults Not started) | Where the step stands. |
| Completed Date | date | conditional | The day the step was completed; required when Status is Completed. |
| Expires | date | no | The day a completed step lapses, for example a background check valid for two years; empty means it does not lapse. |
| Notes | text | no | A short note for the coordinator, such as the reference of the check. Never the findings of a check. |
| Is Current | boolean | computed | True when Status is Completed and Expires is empty or not before today. |
| Guardian | reference(Contact) | no | The parent or guardian who gives consent, on a Guardian consent step (V-15). |
| Provider | text | no | Who ran the background check, such as the screening company (V-17). |
| Reference ID | text | no | The provider's reference for the check, to find it in the provider's own system (V-17). Never the findings. |
| Entry Source | picklist(Entered, Imported) | no (defaults Entered) | Whether the step was typed in or loaded from a provider's export (V-17). |

### Relationships

- **Volunteer Requirement to the person**, many to one, to exactly one of Contact or Person
  Account.
- **Volunteer Requirement to its guardian**, many to one, optional, to a Contact (V-15).

### Rules

**R-VQ1 One person.** Exactly one of Contact and Person Account is set (Section 4).

**R-VQ2 Dates.** Completed Date is required when Status is Completed and may not be in the
future; Expires may not be earlier than Completed Date.

**R-VQ6 Background check details, never a provider call (V-17).** Provider and Reference ID say
where the check is kept; BarnCRM calls no screening provider and stores no findings. A row loaded
through Load One Object with Entry Source Imported says it came from a provider's export; a row
typed in is Entered. Only Background check rows use them, by convention: nothing refuses them on
another Type.

**R-VQ3 Readiness is shown, not enforced.** The volunteer profile shows each Type's most recent
row (the one added last) and whether it is current; a Type with no row shows as not started.
It shows only what the viewer may read: nothing to a user without access to requirements, and
nothing on a household or organization. Nothing in v0.8 refuses a sign-up or hours for a person
whose steps are not current; the coordinator decides.

**R-VQ4 Kept to coordinators, erased with the person.** Requirements are private records: the
Volunteers Admin and Volunteers Coordinator permission sets read and edit all of them, and the
Volunteers Staff and Volunteers Read Only sets grant no access. Erasing a person (Section 29H)
deletes their requirement rows and empties them from the Recycle Bin, through the Volunteers
`PersonErasureExtension`, and the Erasure record lists them by Id only.

**R-VQ5 Deleted with the person.** Deleting a Contact or an Account deletes the requirement rows
and volunteer skills (R-VK4) that name it, in the same transaction, whoever deletes it. They are
deleted in system mode: a background check must not outlive its person, and the user deleting
the person may be a Team Member, who cannot see requirements at all. A record merged into
another is not a deletion here: the merge moves its rows to the record kept, background checks
included. Restoring a person from the Recycle Bin does not restore these rows; they stay in the
Recycle Bin, without a person, until it empties. The rule always runs: no switch, pause or
bypass stops it (R-A4).

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Volunteer_Requirement__c`, auto-number Name `VR-{000000}`, sharing Private.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Contact | `Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact (the platform empties it when the person is deleted, and the row is then deleted, R-VQ5) |
| Person Account | `Account__c` | Lookup to Account (the same, R-VQ5) |
| Type | `Type__c` | Required picklist, not restricted so the admin may add values: Application, Background check, Orientation, Guardian consent |
| Status | `Status__c` | Required restricted picklist: Not started (default), In progress, Completed, Not approved |
| Completed Date | `Completed_Date__c` | Date |
| Expires | `Expires__c` | Date |
| Notes | `Notes__c` | Text (255) |
| Is Current | `Is_Current__c` | Formula (Checkbox) |
| Guardian | `Guardian__c` | Lookup to Contact, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Guardian_Consents (V-15) |
| Provider | `Provider__c` | Text(80) (V-17) |
| Reference ID | `Reference_ID__c` | Text(80) (V-17) |
| Entry Source | `Entry_Source__c` | Picklist, restricted: Entered (default), Imported (V-17) |

- **Validation rules:** `Volunteer_Requirement_One_Person` (R-VQ1), `Volunteer_Requirement_Dates`
  (R-VQ2).
- **Erasure:** `VolunteersErasureExtension` implements `PersonErasureExtension` (R-ER8). It reads
  the person's requirements, volunteer skills, hours and sign-ups in system mode
  (`VolunteerErasureSelector`) and changes them as the user (a user without access to them is
  refused, R-ER5): requirements and volunteer skills deleted (R-VQ4, R-VK5), hours and sign-ups
  kept with their notes emptied (R-VG10, R-VU5), bookings on shifts still to come cancelled
  (R-VU5). It keeps the five volunteer totals on the person (R-VG10), and each entry's Rejection
  Reason, listed as one Kept row with the count of entries that have one. It reads everything
  first, and when the person has any Volunteers record or generated letter it refuses, before
  any change, a user lacking Manage Volunteers, edit on hours and sign-ups or delete on volunteer
  skills and requirements, with `PersonErasure.ErasureException` and the help text
  `Volunteers_Erase_NeedVolunteersAccess` in `BarnHelp_Volunteers` ("To erase a volunteer you also need Volunteers Admin
  or Volunteers Coordinator."); a person with none is erased by anyone Core allows. It deletes
  the hour letters and certificates BarnCRM generated for the person (R-VL4; amends D-108),
  listed as Deleted under "Hour letters and certificates": a file linked to the person, saved
  under the letter file name `volunteer-letter.pdf`, first published on the person, whose title
  starts as `Volunteers_Letter_FileTitle` starts for an existing letter template. Any other file
  is never taken and stays in Core's Kept files row. The letters are deleted in system mode,
  because a file belongs to whoever generated it and a coordinator cannot delete a colleague's
  file as themselves; only exact generated letters are taken, and only after the access check.
  Core adds the Ids of any records an extension reports as Deleted to those it empties from the
  Recycle Bin after the commit.
- **Person delete:** `VolunteerPersonDeleteHandler`, registered on Contact and on Account
  (`Automation_Registry.Volunteers_Person_Delete_Contact` and `..._Account`, order 20, Always
  Runs, `Module__c` Volunteers) and run by Core's own triggers. Before delete it notes the Ids
  of the requirement rows and volunteer skills that name each deleted record (on Account, also
  those naming any of its contacts, which the platform deletes with it, a person account's own
  contact among them, with no person account field read); after delete it deletes the
  ones noted for every record whose MasterRecordId is empty, so a merge loser's rows, which the
  merge has moved to the record kept, stay.
- **Readiness (R-VQ3):** the `volunteerReadiness` component, read from
  `VolunteerReadinessController` (cacheable, user mode), on `Volunteers_Contact_Record_Page` and
  `Volunteers_Account_Record_Page`: Core's person pages unchanged plus the component, as Giving
  ships its own (ADR-0064), assigned in the Volunteers app (Large and Small). Elsewhere the admin
  activates them or adds the component to a page of their own.
- **Access:** `Volunteers_Admin` and `Volunteers_Coordinator` create, read, edit and delete, with
  View All and Modify All (a Private object is edited by others only with Modify All, which the
  platform gives only with delete); Is Current is read only. `Volunteers_Staff` and
  `Volunteers_Read_Only` hold no object or field permission. The Volunteer Requirements tab, in
  the Volunteers app, is visible in the Admin and Coordinator sets only; its All and Not Current
  list views are shared with all users, who see rows only through the object permission.

## 29T. Shift Schedule

### Definition

A repeating pattern of shifts for one job, for example "every Saturday, 9:00 to 12:00, four
volunteers" or "Tuesdays and Thursdays every other week" (feature V-07). The schedule creates
ordinary shifts a set number of weeks ahead, and the shifts are then signed up for, cancelled
and counted like any other. ADR-0128 (`0128-volunteer-recurring-shifts.md`) records why.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | What the coordinator calls the schedule, for example "Saturday sorting". |
| Job | reference(Job) | yes | The job whose shifts the schedule creates. |
| Days of the Week | multi-select(Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday) | yes | The days of the week a shift falls on (labelled Weekdays before v1.0). |
| Repeat Every (Weeks) | integer | yes (defaults 1) | 1 for every week, 2 for every other week, and so on, counted from the week of Start Date. |
| Start Time | time | yes | When each shift starts. |
| End Time | time | yes | When each shift ends, later the same day. |
| Start Date | date | yes | The first day a shift may fall on. |
| End Date | date | no | The last day a shift may fall on; empty means the schedule runs until it is ended. |
| Volunteers Needed | integer | yes (defaults 1) | The places on each shift, copied to the shift's Volunteers Needed. |
| Location | text | no | Where the shifts happen, copied to each shift; empty means the job's location. |
| Active | boolean | yes (defaults true) | Whether the schedule still creates shifts. |
| Created Through | date | computed | The last day the schedule has created shifts for. Kept by the generator; never edited. |
| Shifts Kept | integer | computed | How many future shifts the last edit that removed shifts (R-SSC4, R-SSC5) kept as they were, because they have sign-ups or hours; Cancelled shifts are kept too but not counted. Cleared by a later save that changes neither the pattern nor the end. Kept by the automation; never edited. |
| Rebuild Pending | boolean | computed (defaults false) | Set when a save changed or ended more schedules than it could remove shifts for itself (R-SSC6): the next run removes this schedule's future shifts after Created Through, records Shifts Kept and clears it. Bookkeeping, not on the layout; never edited. |

### Relationships

- **Shift Schedule to Job**, many to one; deleting the job deletes its schedules.
- **Shift Schedule to Shift**, one to many, through the shift's `Shift_Schedule__c` lookup.

### Rules

**R-SSC1 Which days.** A day is a shift day when its weekday is in Weekdays, it is on or after
Start Date and on or before End Date (if any), and the number of whole weeks between the Monday
of Start Date's week and the Monday of its own week divides by Repeat Every (Weeks). Start Time and End
Time are read in the org's default time zone, so a 9:00 shift starts at 9:00 local time on both
sides of a daylight saving change, whoever's job created it.

**R-SSC2 A rolling horizon.** An active schedule keeps shifts created from today to
`Shift_Horizon_Weeks__c` weeks ahead (Volunteer Settings, default 8). Each run creates the
shift days after Created Through (or from today, if later), up to the horizon and End Date, then
moves Created Through forward. A day that already has a shift from this schedule is skipped, and
so is a shift today whose start has already passed. Each created shift is Open, linked to the
schedule, and takes the schedule's job, times, Volunteers Needed and Location; it is named as
R-VS2 names a shift, from its job and start, with the start written in the org's time zone.

**R-SSC3 When it runs.** Saving a schedule queues a run for it, so its shifts appear without
waiting for the night (the `Shift_Schedule_Rules` automation). An update queues one for a
schedule marked Rebuild Pending, and for an active schedule whose pattern changed, that was
turned back on, whose End Date moved, or whose Created Through is short of the horizon (or of
End Date when sooner, while that day has not passed), so opening and saving a schedule fills
it. The run's own bookkeeping save moves Created Through to that day, so it queues nothing. Every night the Volunteers
nightly job runs every active schedule in a batch (ADR-0128). A run takes a lock on the schedule's row first, so the
queued run and the nightly run never create the same day twice. Nothing runs while the module
is turned off; turning it back on catches up at the next nightly run.

**R-SSC4 Editing changes only future shifts with no sign-ups.** When Weekdays, Repeat Every (Weeks),
Start Time, End Time, Start Date, Volunteers Needed or Location changes, the schedule's shifts
that start after now, are not Cancelled and have no sign-up record of any status and no hours
record are deleted, Created Through is cleared, and a run recreates them from the new pattern.
Past shifts, shifts with sign-ups or hours and Cancelled shifts are never changed, and a day holding one of them is not given
a second shift. The save records on the schedule, in Shifts Kept, how many future shifts with a
sign-up or hours were kept as they were (Cancelled shifts are kept but not counted). A later save
that changes neither the pattern nor the end, a name-only edit for one, clears Shifts Kept; the
automation's own bookkeeping saves do not. Changing only Name changes no shift. A change to End Date with none of the
others is ending (R-SSC5): a later or empty End Date only lets the next run go further.

**R-SSC5 Ending a schedule.** Clearing Active, or setting End Date earlier, deletes the future
shifts it no longer covers that have no sign-ups or hours and are not Cancelled; the rest are
kept, and Shifts Kept counts those with a sign-up or hours that it no longer covers. Clearing Active also clears Created
Through, so setting it again fills the horizon from today; an earlier End Date moves Created
Through back to it, so a later End Date creates those days again.
Deleting a schedule does the same for all its future shifts, and the shifts kept lose their
link to it. A coordinator who wants one day off cancels that shift: a deleted shift is created
again by the next edit of its schedule, a Cancelled one is not.

**R-SSC6 Scale.** The nightly batch takes ten schedules per transaction, so one transaction
creates at most ten schedules' worth of shifts at the longest horizon the setting allows. A save
that changes the pattern of, or ends, many schedules removes shifts in the save only for as many
schedules as the transaction's DML rows allow (the rows still free, less a reserve of 2,000,
over seven shifts a week to the horizon: 43 at 26 weeks). The save marks the rest Rebuild
Pending, with Created Through cleared or moved back as R-SSC4 and R-SSC5 say, and queues a run
for them. Every run, queued or nightly, first removes the future shifts after Created Through of
each marked schedule it takes, active or not, as R-SSC4 and R-SSC5 say, records Shifts Kept and
clears the mark, then creates the new shifts; the nightly batch takes every marked schedule, so
a run that could not be queued is made up that night. Until then those schedules show no Shifts
Kept and still hold their old shifts. A delete of many schedules removes shifts in the save
within the same budget; for the rest it takes the Ids of the future shifts R-SSC5 removes before
the delete empties their link, and a queued job (`ShiftScheduleRemovalJob`, 5,000 a
transaction) deletes those that still have no sign-up or hours, have not started and are not
Cancelled.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Shift_Schedule__c`, Text Name (80), sharing controlled by the job.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Job | `Job__c` | Master-Detail to `Volunteer_Job__c` |
| Days of the Week | `Weekdays__c` | Multi-Select Picklist: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday |
| Repeat Every (Weeks) | `Every_N_Weeks__c` | Number (2, 0), default 1 |
| Start Time | `Start_Time__c` | Time |
| End Time | `End_Time__c` | Time |
| Start Date | `Start_Date__c` | Date |
| End Date | `End_Date__c` | Date |
| Volunteers Needed | `Volunteers_Needed__c` | Number (4, 0), default 1 |
| Location | `Location__c` | Text (255) |
| Active | `Active__c` | Checkbox, default true |
| Created Through | `Created_Through__c` | Date, read only in every permission set |
| Shifts Kept | `Shifts_Kept__c` | Number (5, 0), read only in every permission set |
| Rebuild Pending | `Rebuild_Pending__c` | Checkbox, default false, read only in every permission set, not on the layout |

- **Validation rule:** `Shift_Schedule_Valid`: Weekdays not empty, Repeat Every (Weeks) 1 to 52, End
  Time after Start Time, End Date not before Start Date, Volunteers Needed at least 1.
- **Automation:** registry row `Shift_Schedule_Rules` (`ShiftScheduleTriggerHandler`), which
  applies R-SSC4 and R-SSC5 and queues `ShiftScheduleGenerator`; nightly job `ShiftScheduleBatch`,
  started at 3:00 AM by `VolunteersScheduler` (job name `BarnCRM Volunteer Schedules`; Health
  Check and the Nightly Jobs list call it "Volunteer Schedules, 3:00 AM"), which
  `VolunteersNightlyJobProvider` (`NightlyStepProvider`) supplies as a step of the one nightly
  run (Section 29ZR). The shift deletes of R-SSC4 and R-SSC5 and the writes to Created
  Through, Shifts Kept and Rebuild Pending run in system mode: they are the schedule's own bookkeeping, which a
  Coordinator or Staff user who may edit the schedule cannot do with their own delete and field
  access. Shifts are created in user mode.
- **Health Check:** an active schedule whose Created Through is more than two days short of the
  horizon (or End Date) is reported as "schedule horizon not filled"
  (`volunteer_schedule_horizon`, Part G "Health Check").

## 29U. Volunteer Letter Template

### Definition

The wording of a volunteer hours letter or certificate: HTML with merge tokens for the
organization, the person, the hours and the period (feature V-08). Letters are produced by the
Volunteers package's own generator through the Visualforce PDF rendering service, not by
Giving's receipts (ADR-0129, `0129-volunteer-letters.md`). The HTML is restricted to what that
service renders, as for receipts (Section 25E).

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | What the administrator calls this template. |
| Type | picklist(Hours letter, Certificate) | yes | Which kind of document this template lays out. |
| Body | long text | yes | The HTML with merge tokens. |
| Active | boolean | yes (defaults false) | Whether this is the template used for its type. |
| Template Key | text | no | The shipped default it came from; empty for a template the administrator wrote. Unique. |

### Rules

**R-VL1 One active template per type.** Activating a template deactivates the others of its
type. Generating with no active template of the type asked for is refused with a readable
message, and so is generating with a template that is not active (an inactive template is never
merged, however it was chosen).

**R-VL2 Tokens are a closed set.** `{OrganizationName}` and `{OrganizationAddress}` (Core's
`Organization_Legal_Name__c` and the six address parts, `Organization_Street__c` to
`Organization_Country__c`, on one line), `{PersonName}`, `{FirstName}` (the
Preferred Name when set), `{Hours}`, `{FromDate}`, `{ToDate}`, `{JobList}` (each job with its
hours in the period), `{Today}`, and since V-12 `{HourValue}` (the value of one hour, R-VP5)
and `{HoursValue}` (Hours times it), both in the org's default currency and empty when Hour
Value is 0. Since C-47b also `{BrandName}`, `{BrandPhone}`, `{BrandWebsite}`, `{BrandSignature}`
(its line breaks as `<br/>`) and `{BrandLogo}` (an `img` of the brand's logo file, or empty);
with brands on, a person whose hours in the period are all for jobs of one brand (no brand
reads as the default brand) gets that brand's identity, and `{OrganizationName}` and
`{OrganizationAddress}` become its legal entity name and address (R-BR5). Otherwise
`{BrandName}` is the organization name and the other brand tokens are empty. Every merged value
is HTML escaped. An unknown token is left as typed, so a typo shows on the proof.

**R-VL3 What a letter counts.** Hours is the sum of the person's hours with Status Approved and
a Date Worked from From Date to To Date, read in the user's own access. A person with no
approved hours in the period gets no letter and is listed as skipped.

**R-VL4 What a letter is.** Each letter is one PDF file linked to the person's record and to
nothing else; the file is the record that it was sent. Generating needs the custom permission
`Manage_Volunteers`; a list of people is generated in a batch of ten people per transaction.

**R-VL5 The shipped templates arrive at install.** `Volunteer_Letter_Template_Default__mdt` is
materialized by `VolunteersPostInstall` at install and at every upgrade, creating only the
templates whose Template Key the org does not have and never changing an existing one
(Section 13). A materialized template is Active when its type has no active template. A Restore
the shipped templates action on the template list that does the same is a later item (an upgrade
already brings back a deleted shipped template).

**R-VL6 A list is started with a type and checked first.** The flow action Generate volunteer
letters takes a letter Type (a picklist value, not a template Id) and uses that type's one active
template. Before any job starts it checks the permission, the type, the template (it must be
active) and the period, and refuses with a readable message that reaches the flow's fault path.
All requests in one transaction run as one job, so a record-triggered flow on 200 records starts
one job, not 200.

**R-VL7 The person who started a list is told how it went.** A job counts the letters made, the
people skipped (grouped by reason, for example no approved hours in the period) and the people
whose chunk failed, across all chunks. When it ends it sends the person who started it one custom
notification (Core's job notification, `BarnCRM_Job_Finished`, which the BarnCRM Settings option
Job notifications turns off) giving the three counts and, when any failed, pointing to the Error
Log. A job started by a schedule sends none. The record action shows the same outcome on screen.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Volunteer_Letter_Template__c`, Text Name (80), sharing Read; edited only through
  the Volunteers Admin permission set.
- **Access:** `Volunteers_Admin` creates, edits and deletes templates, every field editable;
  `Volunteers_Coordinator` reads them, every field, to generate letters; `Volunteers_Staff` and
  `Volunteers_Read_Only` have no access.
- **Automation:** R-VL1 runs in `VolunteerLetterTemplateTriggerHandler`, registry row
  `Volunteer_Letter_Template_Rules`, which always runs (it keeps a rule, not a convenience).

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Type | `Type__c` | Picklist: Hours letter, Certificate |
| Body | `Body__c` | Long Text Area (32768) |
| Active | `Active__c` | Checkbox |
| Template Key | `Template_Key__c` | Text (80), External ID, Unique |

- **Shipped defaults:** `Volunteer_Letter_Template_Default__mdt`, one row per type
  (`Hours_Letter`, `Certificate`), with `Template_Name__c` (Text 80), `Letter_Type__c` (Text 40)
  and `Body__c` (Long Text Area 32768); DeveloperName is the Template Key.
- **Service:** `VolunteerLetterService`, `VolunteerLetterBatch`, `VolunteerLetterRenderer`
  (`Blob.toPdf`). On a person account the hours counted are those whose `Account__c` is the
  account; an account that is not a person gets no letter.
- **Where it is started:** the record action Volunteer letter (`volunteerLetter`) on Contact and
  on Account, for one person with a preview, and the flow action Generate volunteer letters
  (`VolunteerLetterBatch`, taking a letter Type) for a list of people (R-VL6, R-VL7).

## 29V. Volunteer hours import template

### Definition

The shipped import template that loads a spreadsheet of volunteer hours with the Core import,
one row per hours record (feature V-06). It adds no entity: it is an `Import_Template_Default__mdt`
row shipped by Volunteers. Since release 0.14 it is an upload of several objects (R-IT20,
ADR-0147; it loaded one object, R-IT12, before), as the program roster template is (29ZA).

### Rules

**R-VH1 The shipped rows.** Volunteers ships two rows with the Template Key `volunteer_hours`:
one with Person Mode Contacts, whose person column fills `Contact__c`, and one with Person Mode
Person Accounts, whose person column fills `Account__c`. Only the one matching the org's people
is materialized (R-D3). Target Object `Volunteer_Hours__c`, Load Operation Insert. Its mapping
lists the objects `Volunteer_Hours__c` (Insert) and `Volunteer_Job__c` (Update by a matching
field, key Name): the job is found, never created, and its name is not rewritten; each hours
record links to its row's job (ADR-0147 decision 4). Columns target `Volunteer_Hours__c.<field>`
and `Volunteer_Job__c.Name`, and the Status default `Volunteer_Hours__c.Status__c`.

**R-VH2 Columns.**

| Column | Loads | Found by |
|---|---|---|
| Email | The person (`Contact__c` or `Account__c`) | The person's email: `lookupField` `Email` on Contact, `PersonEmail` on Account |
| Job | The job | The job's name |
| Date | Date Worked | |
| Hours | Hours | |
| Notes | Notes | |

Status is not a column; the template's default value sets it to Submitted, and the hours rules
then apply the starting status as for hours entered by hand (R-VG5, R-VG6): the entry stays
Submitted and waits for a coordinator while Hours Require Approval is on, and is Approved by the
importing user at once when it is off. There is no Shift column: shift names repeat across
recurring shifts (ADR-0128), so a name cannot identify one, and the job is what hours need
(R-VG3). The template reaches an org through the module's post-install step, which calls Core's
`materializeDefaultsDuringInstall` (D-41), so it appears in the import wizard only where
Volunteers is installed. A row whose email or job finds nobody is rejected
(Lookup Not Found, Reject the row), and an email held by several people follows Several Matches
(R-IT9). The household on each hours record is set by the hours automation, as for hours
entered by hand.

**R-VH3 Large orgs.** A standard Email field may always be matched on (R-IT13). Where people
are person Accounts the lookup is on `PersonEmail`, which the large object guard must count as
indexed for an org of more than 100,000 accounts; the V-06 Core work adds it, by name as text.
