## 29W. Setup Change

### Definition

A copy of one row of the Salesforce Setup Audit Trail: who changed what in Setup, and when
(feature C-56, plan D-156). Salesforce keeps the trail for 180 days; BarnCRM keeps its copy for
as long as the org chooses, so a part-time administrator can answer "who changed this, and
when?" long after Setup has forgotten. The copy is read only: BarnCRM never changes Setup.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Audit trail ID | text(18) | yes | The Setup Audit Trail row's ID. Unique: a row is never stored twice. |
| Changed at | datetime | yes | When the change was made. |
| Changed by | text(121) | no | The name of the user who made it, as it was when copied. Blank when Salesforce gives no name (an automated process). |
| Delegate user | text(80) | no | The username of the person who was logged in as that user, when someone was. |
| Section | text(40) | no | The Setup area, such as Customize Accounts or Manage Users. |
| Action | text(120) | no | Salesforce's code for the kind of change, such as `changedFieldLabel`. |
| What changed | long text(1000) | no | Salesforce's own sentence for the change, such as "Changed Phone field label". |

### Rules

**R-SU1 Source.** Rows come only from `SetupAuditTrail`, read with SOQL. BarnCRM reads the
trail and writes only its own copy; it never changes Setup.

**R-SU2 Copy.** The nightly step "BarnCRM Setup Changes Copy" (1:30 in the nightly run,
R-NJ2) copies every trail row made at or after the newest kept row's Changed At,
or every row the trail holds when nothing is kept yet. A row already kept is found by its Audit
Trail ID and not stored again. An administrator can also run the same copy from the page
(**Copy New Changes Now**), which schedules the nightly run when it is not scheduled.

**R-SU3 Who can read the trail.** Salesforce lets a user read the trail only with View Setup
and Configuration. The copy runs as the user who scheduled it, or who pressed Copy New Changes
Now; when the trail cannot be read, the run writes one Error Log entry and copies nothing.

**R-SU4 Retention.** After copying, the same run deletes the kept rows whose Changed At is
older than the Org Optimizer setting Days to Keep Setup Changes
(`Setup_Change_Retention_Days__c`): 730 days unless changed, from 180 to 3,650.

**R-SU5 Administrators only.** The page and every controller method require Manage BarnCRM
Settings. Only `BarnCRM_Admin` is granted the object, Read and View All only. Rows are written
and deleted only by the copy, in system mode (the package's own copy, as ADR-0021 allows), and
nobody edits them.

**R-SU6 Filters and export.** The page lists kept rows newest first, filtered by From and To
(dates in the person's time zone, both ends included), Section (the sections kept) and Search
(case-insensitive words found in What Changed, Section, Action, Changed By or Delegate User).
It shows the newest 200 matches; **Download CSV** writes up to 5,000 with the same filters
(R-SQ3 format). One search looks at no more than 40,000 kept rows and says so when it stops.

**R-SU7 Feeds the digest.** The Weekly Admin Digest (C-54) counts the changes kept (copied into
the Setup Changes Log) within the digest window, by when each was kept, not by its Changed At.
A change copied late (after a missed night, or on the first copy) is counted once, in the next
digest. If reading the admin summary fails, the failure is logged to the Error Log and the
digest still goes, without the summary. The nightly copy does not start while a copy started by
hand is still waiting or running.

**R-SU8 Off with Org Optimizer.** While the Org Optimizer feature is off, a run (nightly or
Copy New Changes Now) copies nothing, deletes nothing and logs nothing; kept rows stay as they
are until it is turned on.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object** `Setup_Change__c`, auto number Name `SC-{000000}`, public read only sharing,
  reports on, no activities, feeds, history or search.

| Attribute | API name | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Audit trail ID | `Audit_Trail_Id__c` | Text(18) | External ID, unique, case sensitive. |
| Changed at | `Changed_At__c` | DateTime | |
| Changed by | `Changed_By__c` | Text(121) | |
| Delegate user | `Delegate_User__c` | Text(80) | |
| Section | `Section__c` | Text(40) | |
| Action | `Action__c` | Text(120) | |
| What changed | `Display__c` | LongTextArea(1000) | |

- **Classes:** `SetupChangeCopyJob` (schedulable and batchable: copy, then delete past
  retention), `SetupChangeController` (summary, search, copy now; every method requires
  `Manage_BarnCRM_Settings`). The page is the `setupChangeLog` component, the Setup Changes
  section of Org Optimizer, its only host.

## 29X. Saved Transform

### Definition

A named, reusable Super Transformer step list (plan feature C-50f1): the object, the conditions
(a Find filter document) and up to five field changes, kept as one documented JSON document so
that a person can load it on the Super Transformer page later, rename it or delete it. It is
org-wide: everyone who may use Super Transformer sees and manages every list. It holds no
records and grants access to none. Neutral: it names no nonprofit concept and is in Core.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | The list's name, 1 to 80 characters, unique among lists ignoring capitals. |
| Object Name | text | yes | The API name of the object the list changes, copied from the definition when it is saved. |
| Definition | long text | yes | The list as a version 1 JSON document (R-ST1). |

### Rules

**R-ST1 The document.** `{ "version": 1, "object": "Contact", "filter": { ...filter document of R-R2... }, "changes": [ { "field", "action", "value" | "source" | "transforms" } ] }`.
`object` is the API name of an object a bulk update may write; `filter` is optional (no filter
means every record, as on the page); `changes` holds at most 5 entries (R-BU1), each with a
`field` and an `action` of `set`, `clear`, `copy` or `transform`, carrying what that action
reads in the form R-BU1 and R-BU7 give (`value`, `source`, or `transforms` in the document of
R-IT15). The page's changes JSON is the same list, so a list is the page's state, nothing more.
**R-ST2 Checked on save, never on trust.** A save is refused when the document is not
version 1 JSON, is over 100,000 characters, names an object a bulk update may not write, has a
`filter` that is not a document, has more than 5 changes or a change with no `field` or an
unknown `action`, or has a `transform` change whose steps `DataTransform.problems` names a
problem with. The name must be 1 to 80 characters and no other list may have it (capitals
ignored). A filter's conditions and a change's fields are not checked against the object at
save: that happens when the list is loaded and when the page counts, previews and runs.
**R-ST3 Loading only fills the page in.** Loading reads the document, then the page loads the
object's fields as the person: a change whose field the person may not change on the object now
is left out and the page says how many (that only narrows what a run does). A filter condition
whose field is gone or not readable by the person (checked server-side with
`QueryFieldCatalog.resolvePath`, in user mode, returned as `missingFields`) stops the load
altogether: the page is left unchanged and a message names the fields and says to edit or delete
the list, because dropping a condition, with or without `logic`, would match more records. Nothing
runs on a load, and a preview, the confirmation and the
run check everything as the person (R-BU1 to R-BU7). A list is therefore no way past a field
or record the person cannot reach.
**R-ST4 Org-wide, one set of permissions.** Every list is visible to, and may be renamed or
deleted by, everyone who holds Bulk Update Records and Find and Export Records (the permission
set `BarnCRM_Bulk_Update` grants Read, Create, Edit, Delete, View All and Modify All, the last
two because a delete otherwise reaches only the list's owner). Reads and writes are in user
mode. Rename changes only the name; a list is saved new, never overwritten.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object** `Saved_Transform__c`, Name text (`Saved Transform Name`), public read and write
  sharing, reports on, no activities, feeds or history. `BarnCRM_Bulk_Update` and
  `BarnCRM_Admin` are granted Read, Create, Edit, Delete, View All and Modify All.

| Attribute | API name | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Object Name | `Object_Name__c` | Text(255) | |
| Definition | `Definition_JSON__c` | Long Text Area(131072) | Written only by Super Transformer. |

- **Service:** `SavedTransformService` (list, load, save, rename, delete, document checks) and
  five `@AuraEnabled` methods on `BulkUpdateController` (`getSavedLists`, `loadSavedList`,
  `saveSavedList`, `renameSavedList`, `deleteSavedList`), each requiring Bulk Update Records and
  Find and Export Records. The page is the `superTransform` component, whose Saved Step Lists
  card is the only place a list is made or used.

## 29Y. Program

### Definition

Something the organization runs for the people it serves: a food pantry, an after-school
tutoring program, a job readiness course (P-01, Programs module, ADR-0151
`0151-programs-module.md`). It is the durable thing; its services (29Z) are what it offers and
its enrollments (29ZA) are who takes part.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | What the program is called, in the words staff use for it. |
| Status | picklist(Planned, Active, Completed) | yes (defaults Active) | Where the program stands. Completed programs keep their enrollments and services. |
| Description | long text | no | What the program does and for whom. |
| Target Population | text | no | Who the program is meant for, in a sentence a funder report can quote. |
| Start Date | date | no | When the program began, or will begin. |
| End Date | date | no | When the program ended, or will end. |
| Coordinator | reference(User) | no | The staff member who runs this program. |
| Eligibility Rules | long text (JSON) | no | The program's eligibility screening rules (P-14, R-EN8): ordered rules over the enrollment's intake fields and, through its Contact lookup, the person's Contact fields (P-14b), in the documented format below. Edited in the Eligibility Rules panel, never by hand. |
| Capacity | integer | no | How many people the program can have Enrolled at once (P-09, R-EN10). Empty means no limit. |

**Eligibility rules format (version 1).** `{ "version": 1, "defaultResult": "Review",
"defaultReason": "...", "rules": [ { "id": "r1", "all": [ { "field": "Referral_Source__c",
"operator": "equals", "value": "Self" } ], "result": "Eligible", "reason": "...", "basis":
"Income" } ] }`. A rule has one to ten conditions, all of which must hold, a `result` of
Eligible, Not Eligible or Review, a `reason` of at most 255 characters and an optional `basis`
(an Eligibility Basis value). Operators: `equals`, `notEquals`, `in`, `notIn` (a list value),
`greaterThan`, `greaterOrEqual`, `lessThan`, `lessOrEqual`, `isBlank`, `isNotBlank` (no value). A
program has at most 50 rules. Field names are those of the enrollment's custom intake fields
that hold text, a choice, a number, a date or a checkbox, matched without regard to case.

### Relationships

- **Program to Service**, one to many; the service is a detail of the program.
- **Program to Enrollment**, one to many, through a required lookup (R-PG2).
- Coordinator is a User, not a person pair: a coordinator is staff who logs in.

### Rules

**R-PG1 End after start.** A program's End Date, when set, is not before its Start Date
(validation rule).

**R-PG2 A program with enrollments is kept.** It cannot be deleted while an enrollment names
it: the enrollment's lookup is required with delete Restrict, so the platform refuses, naming the
enrollments. Set Status to Completed instead. Deleting a program with no enrollments deletes its
services with it.

**R-PG3 A completed program still takes enrollments.** Nothing refuses an enrollment into a
Planned or Completed program, so history from a spreadsheet or PMM loads as it happened.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Program__c`, name field Text, label Program Name, sharing Public Read/Write.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist: Planned, Active, Completed; required, default Active |
| Description | `Description__c` | Long Text Area(32768) |
| Target Population | `Target_Population__c` | Text(255) |
| Start Date | `Start_Date__c` | Date |
| End Date | `End_Date__c` | Date |
| Coordinator | `Coordinator__c` | Lookup to User, delete constraint SetNull |
| Sample Data | `Sample_Data__c` | Checkbox, default false (release 0.12) |
| Eligibility Rules | `Eligibility_Rules__c` | Long Text Area(32768), not required (P-14, release 0.15) |
| Capacity | `Capacity__c` | Number(6, 0) (P-09) |

- **Validation rules:** `End_After_Start` (R-PG1).

## 29Z. Service

### Definition

One thing a program offers its participants: a hot meal, a tutoring hour, a bag of groceries
(P-01). Attendance and service delivery (P-02) record each time a service is given, counted in
the service's unit.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | What the service is called. |
| Program | reference(Program) | yes | The program offering it. A service is a detail of its program. |
| Description | long text | no | What the service is. |
| Unit of Measure | text | no | What one delivery counts: meals, hours, sessions, bags. |
| Active | boolean | yes (defaults true) | Whether the service is still offered. An inactive service keeps its history. |

### Relationships

- **Service to Program**, many to one, as a detail of the program.

### Rules

**R-SV1 A service follows its program.** It is seen and edited by whoever may see and edit its
program, and deleted with it.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Service__c`, name field Text, label Service Name, sharing Controlled By Parent.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Program | `Program__c` | Master-Detail to `Program__c`, relationship name Services |
| Description | `Description__c` | Long Text Area(32768) |
| Unit of Measure | `Unit_Of_Measure__c` | Text(80) |
| Active | `Active__c` | Checkbox, default true |

## 29ZA. Enrollment

### Definition

A person taking part in a program (P-01): applied, enrolled, completed or withdrawn. It is the
participant record; P-02 records what they attended and received.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | An auto number: an enrollment is identified by its person and program. |
| Program | reference(Program) | yes | The program the person takes part in. |
| Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person, where people are Contacts. |
| Account | reference(Account) | conditional | The person, where people are person Accounts. |
| Stage | picklist(Applied, Enrolled, Completed, Withdrawn, Waitlisted) | yes (defaults Enrolled) | Where the person stands in the program. Applied, Enrolled and Waitlisted are open; Completed and Withdrawn have ended. Waitlisted waits for a place (P-09, R-EN10). |
| Start Date | date | no | When the person was enrolled. |
| End Date | date | no | When the person completed or withdrew. |
| Intake Date | date | no | When the person was first seen or applied (P-07, release 0.14). |
| Referral Source | picklist(Self, Family or Friend, Another Agency, School, Health Care Provider, Faith Community, Other) | no | Who sent the person. The values are the organization's to change (P-07). |
| Eligibility Status | picklist(Not Screened, Awaiting Documents, Eligible, Not Eligible, Review) | no (defaults Not Screened) | Whether the person has been checked against the program's rules (P-07). The values are the organization's to change; Eligible and Not Eligible decide it (R-EN6); Review (P-14) means screening could not decide and a person should look. |
| Eligibility Basis | picklist(Income, Age, Residence, Referral, Other) | no | The main reason the person qualifies or not (P-07). The values are the organization's to change. |
| Eligibility Date | date | no | When eligibility was decided (R-EN6). |
| Eligibility Reason | text(255) | no | Why screening gave its result: the reason of the rule that decided it (P-14, R-EN8). Set by screening. |
| Cohort | reference(Cohort) | no | The group of the program the person takes part with (P-11, R-EN8). |

### Relationships

- **Enrollment to Program**, many to one, through a required lookup, not a detail, so the
  enrollment has sharing of its own (participant privacy, P-08; ADR-0151 decision 3).
- **Enrollment to a person**, through the Contact and Account pair (Section 4).
- **Enrollment to Goal**, one to many, master-detail: the participant's service plan (29ZA3, P-10).
- **Enrollment to Cohort**, many to one, optional, delete SetNull: the enrollment is the cohort
  membership (29ZA5, P-11).

### Rules

**R-EN1 Exactly one person.** Contact or Account, never both, never neither (validation rule,
checked only when the enrollment is new or its person changes, as R-VU1). The Account is a person
account: an organization or household account is refused on every path (tab, import, API), not
only by the pickers, when the enrollment is created or its Account changes, with the help text
`Programs_Person_NotAPerson` in `BarnHelp_Programs` (`ProgramPersonRule`, in the always-running `Enrollment_Rules`
handler; QA-F4). Whether the account is a person is read by name, so in an org without person
accounts every Account is refused.

**R-EN2 One open enrollment per person per program.** A second open enrollment (Applied or
Enrolled) for the same person in the same program is refused, naming the program: change the one
that is there instead. A person may enroll again once an earlier enrollment has ended. Every
enrollment in the org counts, one the user cannot see included. The check runs on insert, on
undelete and when the program, person or stage changes. A merge of two people, which moves
enrollments without running their automation, can leave two open ones; the next such change to
either is refused until one is ended. Enforced in Apex by an automation that always runs
(registry row `Enrollment_Rules`, ADR-0024).

**R-EN3 Stage dates are filled in.** Moving an enrollment to Enrolled, or creating it as
Enrolled, fills an empty Start Date with today; moving it to Completed or Withdrawn, or creating
it so, fills an empty End Date with today. A date already typed is kept. A switchable automation
(registry row `Enrollment_Dates`), so an import of history can turn it off.

**R-EN4 End after start.** End Date, when set, is not before Start Date (validation rule).

**R-EN5 Erasing or deleting the person keeps the enrollment.** Erasing a person (Section 29H)
keeps their enrollments, credited to the anonymous record, so program counts stand; an
enrollment holds no typed text to empty. Their case notes, which are typed text, are deleted
(R-CN4). Deleting the person empties the person on the enrollment (SetNull) and keeps it. A merge
moves the enrollments to the record kept.

**R-EN6 The eligibility date is filled in (P-07).** Creating an enrollment with an Eligibility
Status of Eligible or Not Eligible, or changing it to either, fills an empty Eligibility Date with
today. A date already typed is kept, and Not Screened or Awaiting Documents leaves it alone. Part
of the switchable `Enrollment_Dates` automation (R-EN3), so an import of history can turn it off.

**R-EN8 Screening sets the eligibility fields from the program's rules (P-14).** Screening an
enrollment (one, or the program's open ones, Applied or Enrolled, up to 200 a run) evaluates the
program's eligibility rules (Section 29Y) over the enrollment's intake fields and (release 1.19,
P-14b) the person's Contact fields, named by a path such as `Contact__r.Birthdate` and read
blank for an enrollment of an Account: the first rule
whose conditions all hold decides, else the rules' default (Review unless set). The result sets
Eligibility Status (Eligible, Not Eligible or Review), Eligibility Reason, and Eligibility Basis
when the rule names one. When the status changes, Eligibility Date becomes today for Eligible
and Not Eligible and empty for Review. A bulk run leaves enrollments already Eligible or Not
Eligible alone unless asked, so a decision made by hand stands; screening one enrollment always
applies. A program with no rules screens nothing. Read and written as the user, so the user needs
edit access to the eligibility fields. The same rules are evaluated for the preview by the
framework-free `eligibilityEngine.js` (plan 9.9); the two evaluators agree by shared test cases.

**R-EN7 Participant privacy is a preset (P-08).** Organization-wide sharing is Private. Every
enrollment is shared, Read/Write, with the public group Programs Participant Records
(`Programs_Participants`), through the Apex sharing reason `Programs_Participants__c`, written by
an automation that always runs (registry row `Enrollment_Sharing`). The Participant Privacy preset
on the Programs settings page decides who is in that group:

- **Shared (the default):** the group holds All Internal Users, so everyone with a Programs
  permission set sees every enrollment, as before P-08.
- **Private:** the group holds no one BarnCRM put there, so an enrollment is seen by its owner,
  people above the owner in the role hierarchy, and Programs Admin (View All and Modify All). An
  admin may add chosen users, roles or groups to the group in Setup; BarnCRM adds and removes
  only All Internal Users.

The preset is stored in `Programs_Settings__c`, written only by the settings page and audited as
a settings change. The group follows the preset at once when it is saved, and again at install,
at Turn on and in the hourly access check, which repairs a group changed by hand.

**Intake fields hold choices, not typed text (P-07).** The intake and eligibility fields are dates
and restricted picklists, so R-EN5 still holds: erasing a person leaves nothing on an enrollment
to empty. Notes about a person belong in case notes (P-04). The picklist values are the
organization's: an admin adds, renames or deactivates them on the field in Setup (Object Manager,
Enrollment), which the Programs settings page links to; BarnCRM reads them by value, and only
R-EN6 names two values.

**R-EN8 A cohort of the same program (P-11).** An enrollment's Cohort, when set, is a cohort of
the enrollment's program (validation rule). Moving a person into or out of a cohort changes this
one field; there is no membership record (ADR-0160 decision 10). R-EN2 already keeps a person in
one cohort of a program at a time. A cohort deleted later empties the field (SetNull).

**R-EN10 Capacity and the waitlist (P-09).** With Programs' Waitlist When Full on
(`Programs_Settings__c.Waitlist_Enabled__c`, off by default) and Capacity set, an enrollment
saved as Enrolled (new, or moved to Enrolled or to another program) is checked against the
places free, counted from every Enrolled enrollment in the org in system mode, in the order
given: one that does not fit is saved as Waitlisted instead. When places free up (an enrollment
leaves Enrolled or is deleted, or Capacity is raised) Waitlisted enrollments are moved to
Enrolled, oldest first by Created Date, through Core's `WaitlistQueue` (ADR-0198 volunteer
self-service decision 5), in system mode so one the user cannot see (R-EN7) still moves, with
R-EN3 filling the Start Date. Applied is not counted
and never promoted. With the setting off, Capacity only shows and nothing is waitlisted or
promoted. Waitlisted is open for
R-EN2, and is not counted as open on the dashboard or the person card. Cohorts have no capacity.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Enrollment__c`, name field AutoNumber `EN-{000000}`, sharing Private (Public
  Read/Write before P-08), Apex sharing reason `Programs_Participants__c` (R-EN7).

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Program | `Program__c` | Lookup to `Program__c`, required, delete constraint Restrict, relationship name Enrollments |
| Contact | `Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Enrollments |
| Account | `Account__c` | Lookup to Account, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Enrollments |
| Stage | `Stage__c` | Picklist: Applied, Enrolled, Completed, Withdrawn, Waitlisted; required, default Enrolled |
| Start Date | `Start_Date__c` | Date |
| End Date | `End_Date__c` | Date |
| Intake Date | `Intake_Date__c` | Date |
| Referral Source | `Referral_Source__c` | Picklist, restricted, not required, no default |
| Eligibility Status | `Eligibility_Status__c` | Picklist, restricted, not required, default Not Screened |
| Eligibility Basis | `Eligibility_Basis__c` | Picklist, restricted, not required, no default |
| Eligibility Date | `Eligibility_Date__c` | Date |
| Eligibility Reason | `Eligibility_Reason__c` | Text(255) (P-14, release 0.15) |
| Cohort | `Cohort__c` | Lookup to `Cohort__c`, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Enrollments |

- **Eligibility screening (R-EN8):** `EligibilityRules` (validation and evaluation of the JSON
  rules, no query or save), `EligibilityController` (state, saving rules, screening) and the
  `eligibilityRules` panel on the program record page, whose `eligibilityEngine.js` evaluates
  the same rules for the preview. Eligibility Status gains the value Review.
- **Settings page:** `ProgramsSettingsController` and the `programsSettings` panel on the
  `Programs_Settings` app page and tab (Programs Admin only), reached from the Programs section
  of BarnCRM Settings (`Setting_Definition.Programs_Settings`, a navigation row). It lists the
  intake picklists' active values and default from describe, with a link to the enrollment's
  fields in Setup (Object Manager by API name). The section name `Programs` is in Core's
  `SettingSections`. It also holds the Participant Privacy preset (R-EN7).
- **Weeks Ahead to Create Sessions:** `Programs_Settings__c` field `Session_Horizon_Weeks__c` (Number(2, 0),
  default 8, 1 to 26), set in the Programs section of BarnCRM Settings
  (`Setting_Definition.Programs_Session_Horizon_Weeks`) and read by `SessionScheduleService.horizonWeeks` (R-SS2).
- **Waitlist When Full (P-09):** `Programs_Settings__c` field `Waitlist_Enabled__c` (Checkbox,
  default false), set in the Programs section of BarnCRM Settings
  (`Setting_Definition.Programs_Waitlist_Enabled`); R-EN10 by `EnrollmentCapacity`, called from
  the always-running `Enrollment_Rules` handler, and itself the handler of the registry row
  `Program_Capacity` (`ProgramTrigger`, after update), which promotes when Capacity is raised or
  cleared.
- **Participant privacy (R-EN7, R-SD6):** the public group `Programs_Participants` (no bosses);
  the hierarchy custom setting `Programs_Settings__c` with `Private_Participants__c` (Checkbox,
  default unchecked, which is Shared); `ProgramsSharing` writes the shares (handler
  `ProgramsSharingHandler`, registry rows `Enrollment_Sharing` and `Service_Delivery_Sharing`,
  always run), sets the group's All Internal Users member (queued, as a group member is a setup
  object), and shares records that have no share yet (`ProgramsSharingBatch`, run at install
  and when the preset is saved). `ProgramsAccessStep` sets the member hourly, after Core's access sync (D-200 S1).
- **Validation rules:** `Exactly_One_Person` (R-EN1), `End_After_Start` (R-EN4),
  `Cohort_In_Program` (R-EN8).
- **Service:** `EnrollmentService` (the stage values and the roster panel's reads and writes),
  `EnrollmentRulesHandler` (R-EN2), `EnrollmentDatesHandler` (R-EN3), `EnrollmentSelector`
  (the R-EN2 check reads every enrollment in the org, without sharing, so one the user cannot see
  still counts).

### PMM mapping

The three Programs objects map onto the Program Management Module's (namespace `pmdm`) without a
new field, so the PMM migration (MIG-09, plan Section 6.1.4 item 9) is a template, not a schema
change. Nothing in BarnCRM references a PMM object. The PMM names below are from its public
repository and are checked against an org with PMM when MIG-09 is built.

| BarnCRM | PMM | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Program: Name, Status, Description, Target Population, Start Date, End Date | Program: Name, Status, Description, Target Population, Start Date, End Date | Status values match (Planned, Active, Completed) |
| Service: Name, Program, Description, Unit of Measure, Active | Service: Name, Program, Description, Unit of Measurement, Status | Status Active maps to Active checked |
| Enrollment: Program, Contact, Stage, Start Date, End Date, Cohort | Program Engagement: Program, Contact, Stage, Start Date, End Date, Program Cohort | Stages: Applied to Applied; Enrolled and Active to Enrolled; Completed to Completed; Withdrawn to Withdrawn |
| Cohort: Name, Program, Status, Start Date, End Date (29ZA5, P-11) | Program Cohort: Name, Program, Status, Start Date, End Date | Status values match (Planned, Active, Completed) |
| Session: Name, Service, Session Date, Start Time, End Time, Status (29ZA6, P-11) | Service Session: Name, Service Schedule's Service, Session Start, Session End, Status | PMM keeps a Service Schedule above its sessions; BarnCRM's Session Schedule (29ZA7) is optional, so a session names its service itself. Status: Pending to Scheduled, Complete to Held, Canceled to Cancelled |

### On a person, Health Check and sample data

**Programs on a person.** The read only `personEnrollments` card lists a person's enrollments,
open ones first, each with its program, stage and dates, on the Programs app's own Contact and
Account record pages (`Programs_Contact_Record_Page`, `Programs_Account_Record_Page`: Core's
pages plus the card, kept in step under ADR-0064). Read in user mode. On an Account it shows only
for a person account, and lists enrollments naming the account or its one contact, so it needs no
person account field. A user who cannot read enrollments gets no card. Since P-05 the card also
shows the person's last service, the latest Delivery Date of a Present delivery (29ZB), and how
many Present deliveries they have, both counted in user mode over the deliveries naming the
person, and left out for a user who cannot read deliveries or when there are none.

**Program dashboard (P-05).** The `programDashboard` panel on the `Programs_Dashboard` app page
and tab (every Programs set) answers, for a period the user picks (This Month, Last Month, This
Year, Last Year, Last 12 Months; default This Month): active programs (Status Active), open
enrollments now (Applied or Enrolled), new enrollments (Start Date in the period), completed
enrollments (Stage Completed, End Date in the period), people served (distinct people with a
Present delivery in the period, contacts and accounts counted apart, as a delivery names one or
the other, counted as people rather than by scanning every delivery, so large orgs stay within
platform query limits), services delivered (Present deliveries) and the attendance rate (Present over all
deliveries, absences included, in the period). The same figures per program, for every Active
program and any other program with activity in the period, at most 200. Read through
`ProgramDashboardController` in user mode with aggregate queries, so each user's figures follow
what they may see (Participant Privacy, R-EN7). No object or field is added; the periods are
computed in the browser by framework-free JS (plan 9.9).

**Roster import (P-06).** Programs ships two `Import_Template_Default__mdt` rows with the
Template Key `program_roster`, Person Mode Contacts and Person Accounts, of which only the one
matching the org's people is materialized (R-D3), at install through Core's
`materializeDefaultsDuringInstall`. Each is an upload of several objects (R-IT20, ADR-0147):
objects `Enrollment__c` (Insert, the Target Object) and `Program__c` (Update by a matching
field, key Name). Columns: Program (`Program__c.Name`), Email (`Enrollment__c.Contact__c` by
`Email`, or `Enrollment__c.Account__c` by `PersonEmail`), Stage, Start Date, End Date, Intake
Date, Referral Source, Eligibility Status, Eligibility Basis, Eligibility Date. The program loads
first and each enrollment links to its row's program (ADR-0147 decision 4); the program is only
found, never created, and its name is not rewritten, even when a row spells it in other
capitals. A row whose program or email finds nothing is rejected, and so is one R-EN2 refuses.
The enrollment rules run as for one made by hand (blank Stage is Enrolled, R-EN3 fills dates).
No field is added.

**Health Check.** `ProgramsHealthCheckExtension`, registered in
`HealthCheckExtensions.EXTENSION_CLASSES`, asked only of a viewer who may manage settings and not
while the module is turned off:

| Key | Severity | Finds | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `program_enrollments_open_after_end` | Info | Open enrollments (Applied or Enrolled) in a program that is Completed or whose End Date is past: they still count as open (R-EN2) and in the roster. | Links the first five enrollments. |
| `nonprofit_cloud_program_management_present` | Info (category OrgShape) | The org has the Nonprofit Cloud `Program` and `ProgramEnrollment` objects, found by describe only (QA-F5). Programs never reads or writes them, so the two share no records. | None: choose one for each program. The Integrations page lists Nonprofit Cloud Program Management as an Alternative (Integration App row `Nonprofit_Cloud_Program_Management`, detected by `Program`, shown only when installed). |

**Sample data.** The static resource `ProgramsSampleData.json`, loaded by Core's generic
`SampleDataFile` since D-200 S2 (format in data/sample/README.md), is registered in
`SampleDataModules.MODULE_CLASS_NAMES` after Volunteers; the removal is the file's `remove`
entries with partial success, naming what it kept in one Warning. Its load builds three
programs flagged `Sample_Data__c` (two Active, one Completed) with five services, then 18
enrollments of up to 12 of Core's sample people (contacts), through the enrollment rules, then
(release 0.13, P-02) 40 service deliveries (29ZB) to the people Enrolled in the two Active
programs, then (release 1.19, P-11) one Active cohort (29ZA5) of the people Enrolled in tutoring
with three sessions (29ZA6) of its Homework club service (two Held, with eight attendance deliveries, one
an Excused Absence; one Scheduled), then (P-10) one In Progress goal (29ZA3) with two steps (29ZA4) per
person Enrolled in tutoring. Release 1.25 adds a Completed cohort, Summer reading circle, holding
the four who completed summer reading; an active repeating session schedule (29ZA7) for the
homework club, Tuesdays and Thursdays for the next 60 days, whose save queues the run that
creates its sessions (R-SS3); a description and the loading person as Assigned To on every goal,
one tutoring goal with its review overdue, an Achieved goal in summer reading and an In Progress
goal in the pantry, each with two steps. Its removal, before Volunteers', Giving's and Core's, deletes one
chunk per stage: the sample people's service deliveries and enrollments in sample programs (goals
and steps go with them), then sample program sessions no delivery names, the sample programs'
session schedules, and cohorts no session or schedule names, then the sample programs with no enrollment, cohort or delivery left (their
services go with them). A sample program a real person
is enrolled in, or has a delivery in, is kept, and so is a sample program with a sample
enrollment that has a case note (whoever wrote it, even a note the remover cannot see: that
enrollment is skipped and kept); one Warning in the Error Log names each one kept.

## 29ZA1. Case Note

### Definition

A dated, typed note about a participant, written on their enrollment (P-04, release 0.14): a
check-in, a call, a home visit, an assessment. Light case notes, not case management: goals and
service plans are P-10.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | An auto number. |
| Enrollment | reference(Enrollment) | yes | The person's enrollment the note is about; the person and program come from it. |
| Note Date | date | yes (defaults today) | The day of the contact or event the note records. |
| Type | picklist(Check-in, Phone Call, Home Visit, Office Visit, Assessment, Referral, Other) | yes (defaults Check-in) | What kind of contact it records. The values are the organization's to change in Setup. |
| Subject | text(255) | no | A short line saying what the note is about. |
| Note | long text | no | What happened, what was agreed and what comes next. |
| Goal | reference(Goal) | no | The goal on the same enrollment the note is about (P-10, R-CN5). |
| Owner | reference(User) | yes | The author, who sees and edits the note. |

### Relationships

- **Case Note to Enrollment**, many to one, through a required lookup, not a detail, so a note
  has sharing of its own and is not visible to everyone who can see the enrollment.

### Rules

**R-CN1 An enrollment with case notes is kept.** The lookup's delete constraint is Restrict: an
enrollment with notes cannot be deleted; delete the notes first. A merge moves the enrollment,
and its notes with it.

**R-CN2 Private by default.** Organization-wide sharing is Private, whatever the participant
privacy preset (P-08) says: a note is seen by its owner, people above the owner in the role
hierarchy, and Programs Admin (View All and Modify All). An owner may share a note with a
colleague through the record's Sharing button, or an admin may add a sharing rule in Setup.

**R-CN3 Who may write.** Programs Staff create notes and edit their own; Programs Admin creates,
edits and deletes any; Programs Read Only has no access to case notes at all, so a Read Only user
sees neither the tab nor the related list.

**R-CN4 Erasing the person deletes their notes.** A case note is typed text about the person and
nothing else, so erasing the person (Section 29H, R-ER8) deletes every note on any of their
enrollments, read in system mode and deleted as the user; someone who may not delete them all is
refused with that reason (only Programs Admin may). Erasing a person account also finds notes
and counts enrollments recorded on that person account's own contact. The enrollments are kept (R-EN5). Deleting a
person, not erasing them, keeps the notes on the enrollment, which no longer names the person;
erase a person to remove what was written about them. Their goals (29ZA3) go too (R-GL6).

**R-CN5 A note may be about a goal (P-10).** A note may name one goal of its own enrollment
(29ZA3); a goal of another enrollment is refused (validation rule). The note stays private to its
author (R-CN2): a goal shows only the notes its viewer may see. Deleting the goal empties the
note's Goal and keeps the note.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Case_Note__c`, name field AutoNumber `CN-{000000}`, sharing Private.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Enrollment | `Enrollment__c` | Lookup to `Enrollment__c`, required, delete constraint Restrict, relationship name Case_Notes |
| Note Date | `Note_Date__c` | Date, required, default TODAY() |
| Type | `Type__c` | Picklist, restricted, required, default Check-in |
| Subject | `Subject__c` | Text(255) |
| Note | `Note__c` | Long Text Area(32768) |
| Goal | `Goal__c` | Lookup to `Goal__c`, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Case_Notes (R-CN5) |

- **Validation rule:** `Goal_On_Same_Enrollment` (R-CN5).
- **Erasure:** `ProgramsErasureExtension`, registered in Core's
  `PersonErasureExtensions.EXTENSION_CLASSES`, with `CaseNoteSelector` (without sharing, system
  mode reads only).
- **UI:** the Case Notes tab (list views All Case Notes and My Case Notes) and the Case Notes
  related list on the enrollment. No trigger.
- **PMM mapping:** none; PMM has no case note object, so MIG-09 carries none.

---

## 29ZA2. Referral

### Definition

A person sent to another organization (Out) or sent to this one (In), with where the referral
stands and how it turned out (P-13, release 0.15). The fields are generic so a later partner
portal (PB-05) can show the same records. Not case management and not a referral to a funder.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | An auto number. |
| Direction | picklist(Out, In) | yes (defaults Out) | Out: the person was sent to another organization. In: another organization sent the person here. |
| Referral Date | date | yes (defaults today) | The day the referral was made or received. |
| Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person, where people are Contacts. |
| Account | reference(Account) | conditional | The person, where people are person Accounts. |
| Enrollment | reference(Enrollment) | no | The person's enrollment the referral belongs to, if any. |
| Other Organization | text(255) | no | The organization the person was sent to (Out) or came from (In). |
| Status | picklist(Open, Accepted, Closed) | yes (defaults Open) | Where the referral stands. The values are the organization's to change. |
| Outcome | picklist(Service Received, Declined by Organization, Declined by Person, Unable to Reach, No Capacity, Other) | no | How it turned out, once closed. The values are the organization's to change. |
| Notes | long text | no | What was agreed, what was sent and what comes next. |
| Owner | reference(User) | yes | The staff member who made or received it, who sees and edits it. |

### Relationships

- **Referral to a person**, through the Contact and Account pair (Section 4), delete SetNull.
- **Referral to Enrollment**, many to one, optional, delete SetNull.

### Rules

**R-RF1 Exactly one person.** Contact or Account, never both, never neither (validation rule,
checked only when the referral is new or its person changes, as R-EN1).

**R-RF2 Private, as a case note.** Organization-wide sharing is Private, whatever the participant
privacy preset says (R-CN2): the owner, people above them in the role hierarchy and Programs
Admin (View All and Modify All) see a referral.

**R-RF3 Who may write.** Programs Staff create referrals and edit their own and never delete;
Programs Admin creates, edits and deletes any; Programs Read Only has no access at all.

**R-RF4 Erasing the person deletes their referrals.** A referral is typed text about the person
(the other organization, the notes), so erasing the person (Section 29H, R-ER8) deletes every
referral naming them or, for a person account, its own contacts: read in system mode and deleted
as the user, so only Programs Admin can, and anyone else erasing is refused with that reason.
Deleting a person, not erasing them, keeps the referral, which no longer names the person.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Referral__c`, name field AutoNumber `RF-{000000}`, sharing Private.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Direction | `Direction__c` | Picklist, restricted, required, default Out |
| Referral Date | `Referral_Date__c` | Date, required, default `TODAY()` |
| Contact | `Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Referrals |
| Account | `Account__c` | Lookup to Account, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Referrals |
| Enrollment | `Enrollment__c` | Lookup to `Enrollment__c`, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Referrals |
| Other Organization | `Other_Organization__c` | Text(255) |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist, restricted, required, default Open |
| Outcome | `Outcome__c` | Picklist, restricted, not required |
| Notes | `Notes__c` | Long Text Area(32768) |
| Partner Organization | `Partner_Organization__c` | Lookup to Account, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Partner_Referrals (PB-05, R-RF5) |
| Shared With Partner | `Shared_With_Partner__c` | Checkbox, default false (PB-05, R-RF5) |

**R-RF5 A partner sees only what is shared (PB-05).** The partner portal shows a referral to a
person with a Current affiliation to its Partner Organization only while Shared With Partner is on,
and never its notes.

- **Validation rules:** `Exactly_One_Person` (R-RF1).
- **Erasure:** `ProgramsErasureExtension` with `ReferralSelector` (without sharing, system mode
  reads only).
- **UI:** the Referrals tab (list views All Referrals and Open Referrals) and the Referrals
  related list on the enrollment. No trigger.

## 29ZA3. Goal

### Definition

Something a participant is working toward within their enrollment, with the steps to get there
(P-10, release 0.15, ADR-0160 `0160-programs-service-plans-cohorts-sessions.md`): find stable
housing, pass the high school equivalency test, open a bank account. A participant's service plan
is the set of goals on their enrollment; there is no plan record (ADR-0160 decision 1). Case
management lite: who is responsible, by when, how it stands, and when it is next reviewed.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text(80) | yes | The goal, in a line the participant would recognize. |
| Enrollment | reference(Enrollment) | yes | The enrollment, and through it the person and program, the goal belongs to. |
| Description | long text | no | What success looks like and anything agreed about it. |
| Status | picklist(Not Started, In Progress, Achieved, Not Achieved) | yes (defaults Not Started) | Where the goal stands. Achieved and Not Achieved are closed. |
| Target Date | date | no | When the goal should be reached. |
| Assigned To | reference(User) | no | The staff member responsible for the goal. |
| Last Reviewed | date | no | When the goal was last reviewed with the participant. |
| Next Review | date | no | When the goal is next to be reviewed. |
| Closed Date | date | no | When the goal was Achieved or Not Achieved (R-GL2). |
| Outcome Id | text(18) | no | The Logic Models outcome the goal works toward, by record identifier (R-GL5). |

### Relationships

- **Goal to Enrollment**, many to one, master-detail: the goal's visibility is the enrollment's
  (R-GL1).
- **Goal to Goal Step**, one to many (29ZA4).
- **Goal to Case Note**, one to many, through the note's optional lookup (R-CN5).
- **Goal to a Logic Models outcome**, by record identifier only, never a lookup (R-GL5).

### Rules

**R-GL1 A goal is seen as its enrollment is.** Goal is a detail of Enrollment, so whoever sees
the enrollment under the Participant Privacy preset (R-EN7) sees its goals, and editing a goal
needs edit access to the enrollment. No sharing code. Deleting an enrollment deletes its goals and
their steps.

**R-GL2 The closed date is filled in.** Moving a goal to Achieved or Not Achieved, or creating it
so, fills an empty Closed Date with today; moving it back to Not Started or In Progress empties
it. A switchable automation (registry row `Goal_Dates`), so an import of history can turn it off.

**R-GL3 Reviews.** Mark Reviewed on the Service Plan panel sets Last Reviewed to today and Next
Review to the date the user confirms, offered three months on. An open goal whose Next Review is
before today is due for review: flagged on the panel and listed by the Reviews Due list view.
Both dates may also be typed on the record.

**R-GL4 Who may write.** Programs Admin creates, edits and deletes goals and steps; Programs Staff
create and edit them, never delete (close a goal as Not Achieved instead); Programs Read Only
reads them.

**R-GL5 Outcome by record identifier.** Outcome Id names a Logic Model Element of type Outcome
(29ZD) by its Id, as text (ADR-0014; ADR-0154 decision 5 is the same pattern the other way).
Programs never references Logic Models' schema: the Service Plan panel offers the outcome picker
only where `Logic_Model_Element__c` exists and the user can read it, lists the outcomes of the
logic model whose program is the enrollment's program, then the organization's model, and saves
only the Id of an outcome it found that way. An outcome deleted later is shown as missing.

**R-GL6 Erasing the person deletes their goals.** A goal is typed text about the person, so
erasing the person (Section 29H) deletes the goals on all their enrollments, and their steps with
them, as R-CN4; the enrollments are kept (R-EN5). Only someone who may delete them (Programs Admin)
can erase a person who has goals.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Goal__c`, name field Text(80) labelled Goal, sharing Controlled by Parent.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Enrollment | `Enrollment__c` | Master-Detail to `Enrollment__c`, relationship name Goals, not reparentable |
| Description | `Description__c` | Long Text Area(32768) |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist, restricted, required, default Not Started |
| Target Date | `Target_Date__c` | Date |
| Assigned To | `Assigned_To__c` | Lookup to User, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Assigned_Goals |
| Last Reviewed | `Last_Review_Date__c` | Date |
| Next Review | `Next_Review_Date__c` | Date |
| Closed Date | `Closed_Date__c` | Date |
| Outcome Id | `Outcome_Id__c` | Text(18) |

- **Automation:** trigger `GoalTrigger` through `TriggerDispatcher`, handler
  `ServicePlanDatesHandler` (registry row `Goal_Dates`, switchable, R-GL2).
- **List views:** All Goals, Open Goals, Reviews Due (open, Next Review before today).
- **Service Plan panel:** the `servicePlan` panel on the enrollment page
  (`Enrollment_Record_Page`) through `ServicePlanController` (thin, plain JSON, user mode): goals
  open first, each with its steps, status, target date, who is responsible, review dates, its
  outcome and the case notes about it the user may see; add and edit goals and steps, mark a step
  done, Mark Reviewed and New Note. Sorting, flags and default dates are worked out in the
  framework-free module `servicePlan/plan.js` (plan 9.9).
- **Erasure:** `ProgramsErasureExtension` deletes the goals (R-GL6), found by `CaseNoteSelector`.
- **PMM mapping:** none; PMM has no goal object.

## 29ZA4. Goal Step

### Definition

One action toward a goal (P-10): fill in the housing application, book the test, bring proof of
address.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text(80) | yes | The step, as a short action. |
| Goal | reference(Goal) | yes | The goal the step leads to. |
| Status | picklist(Not Started, In Progress, Done) | yes (defaults Not Started) | Where the step stands. |
| Assigned To | reference(User) | no | The staff member responsible for the step. |
| Target Date | date | no | When the step should be done. |
| Completed Date | date | no | When the step was Done (R-GS1). |

### Relationships

- **Goal Step to Goal**, many to one, master-detail: visibility follows the goal and so the
  enrollment (R-GL1).

### Rules

**R-GS1 The completed date is filled in.** Moving a step to Done, or creating it so, fills an empty
Completed Date with today; moving it back empties it. A switchable automation (registry row
`Goal_Step_Dates`).

R-GL1, R-GL4 and R-GL6 apply to steps through their goal.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Goal_Step__c`, name field Text(80) labelled Step, sharing Controlled by Parent.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Goal | `Goal__c` | Master-Detail to `Goal__c`, relationship name Steps, not reparentable |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist, restricted, required, default Not Started |
| Assigned To | `Assigned_To__c` | Lookup to User, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Assigned_Goal_Steps |
| Target Date | `Target_Date__c` | Date |
| Completed Date | `Completed_Date__c` | Date |

- **Automation:** trigger `GoalStepTrigger`, handler `ServicePlanDatesHandler` (registry row
  `Goal_Step_Dates`, switchable, R-GS1).
- **PMM mapping:** none.

## 29ZA5. Cohort

### Definition

A group of participants who go through a program together (P-11, release 0.15, ADR-0160
`0160-programs-service-plans-cohorts-sessions.md`): the spring class of a job readiness course,
the Tuesday group of a tutoring program. Its members are the enrollments that name it (R-EN8);
there is no membership record.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text(80) | yes | What the cohort is called. |
| Program | reference(Program) | yes | The program the cohort belongs to. |
| Status | picklist(Planned, Active, Completed) | yes (defaults Active) | Where the cohort stands. |
| Start Date | date | no | When the cohort starts. |
| End Date | date | no | When the cohort ends. |

### Relationships

- **Cohort to Program**, many to one, through a required lookup with delete Restrict: a program
  with cohorts cannot be deleted until they are.
- **Cohort to Enrollment**, one to many, through the enrollment's Cohort (R-EN8): the members.
- **Cohort to Session**, one to many, through the session's Cohort (29ZA6).
- **Cohort to Session Schedule**, one to many, through the schedule's Cohort (29ZA7), delete
  Restrict.

### Rules

**R-CO1 A cohort holds no participant data.** It names a group, so it is shared as Program is
(Public Read/Write); who is in it is seen through the enrollments, under the Participant Privacy
preset (R-EN7). Programs Admin creates, edits and deletes cohorts; Programs Staff create and edit
them; Programs Read Only reads them.

**R-CO2 End after start.** End Date, when set, is not before Start Date (validation rule).

**R-CO3 Mass enrollment.** The Cohort Members panel adds many people at once: each person picked
and each open enrollment of the program not yet in a cohort that is ticked. A person with an open
enrollment in the program is moved into the cohort (its Cohort is set); a person without one is
enrolled at stage Enrolled, in the cohort, through the enrollment rules (R-EN1 to R-EN3). Each
person succeeds or fails alone, and the panel lists who failed and why. Removing a member empties
the enrollment's Cohort and keeps the enrollment. At most 200 people are added in one action.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Cohort__c`, name field Text(80) labelled Cohort Name, sharing Public Read/Write.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Program | `Program__c` | Lookup to `Program__c`, required, delete constraint Restrict, relationship name Cohorts |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist, restricted, required, default Active |
| Start Date | `Start_Date__c` | Date |
| End Date | `End_Date__c` | Date |

- **Validation rule:** `End_After_Start` (R-CO2).
- **Cohort page:** `Cohort_Record_Page` with the `cohortMembers` panel (R-CO3) and the
  `sessionScheduler` panel (R-SE4), through `CohortController` (thin, plain JSON, user mode).
- **PMM mapping:** Program Cohort (29ZA, PMM mapping).

---

## 29ZA6. Session

### Definition

One scheduled occurrence of a service (P-11): the 6 pm class on 3 March, Tuesday's tutoring hour.
Attendance at a session is recorded as Service Delivery (29ZB), so a session has no attendance
record of its own (ADR-0160 decision 12).

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text(80) | yes | What the session is called; scheduling names it after its service and date. |
| Service | reference(Service) | yes | The service given at the session, and through it the program. |
| Cohort | reference(Cohort) | no | The cohort the session is for, a cohort of the service's program (R-SE1). Empty: for everyone enrolled in the program. |
| Session Date | date | yes | The day of the session. |
| Start Time | time | no | When the session starts. |
| End Time | time | no | When the session ends, later the same day (R-SE6). |
| Status | picklist(Scheduled, Held, Cancelled) | yes (defaults Scheduled) | Whether the session is still to come, took place or was called off. |
| Session Schedule | reference(Session Schedule) | no | The repeating schedule that created the session (29ZA7). Empty for a session made by hand or by the Schedule Sessions panel. |

### Relationships

- **Session to Service**, many to one, through a required lookup with delete Restrict, not a
  detail, so a service keeps its sessions' history: a service with sessions cannot be deleted;
  clear its Active box instead.
- **Session to Cohort**, many to one, optional, delete SetNull.
- **Session to Session Schedule**, many to one, optional, delete SetNull: deleting a schedule
  keeps its sessions.
- **Session to Service Delivery**, one to many, through the delivery's Session (R-SD7).

### Rules

**R-SE1 A cohort of the same program.** A session's Cohort, when set, is a cohort of its
service's program (validation rule).

**R-SE2 Attendance is taken on the session.** The Service Delivery Log on the session page lists
the cohort's open enrollments (the program's when the session has no cohort) and saves their
deliveries with the session named (R-SD7). Saving attendance on a Scheduled session marks it Held.

**R-SE3 A cancelled session takes no attendance.** The log on a Cancelled session shows what was
recorded and saves nothing.

**R-SE4 Sessions are scheduled in a batch, not by a rule.** The Schedule Sessions panel (on a
cohort, and on a program for sessions with no cohort) creates one Scheduled session for each
chosen weekday between two dates, with a start and end time, at most 200 at a time. The dates are worked
out in a framework-free module (plan 9.9); the server checks again that the service is the
program's, the cohort is the program's, and the count. The panel keeps no pattern itself: each
session it makes is edited or cancelled on its own, and scheduling again adds more. Save as
Repeating Schedule saves the panel's pattern as a Session Schedule (29ZA7, R-SS6) instead.

**R-SE5 Who.** As R-CO1: sessions hold no participant data and are shared as Program is. A
session with deliveries cannot be deleted (Restrict on the delivery's Session); cancel it instead.

**R-SE6 End after start.** End Time, when both times are set, is after Start Time (validation
rule; modules-24, D-183). Either may be empty.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Session__c`, name field Text(80) labelled Session Name, sharing Public Read/Write.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Service | `Service__c` | Lookup to `Service__c`, required, delete constraint Restrict, relationship name Sessions |
| Cohort | `Cohort__c` | Lookup to `Cohort__c`, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Sessions |
| Session Date | `Session_Date__c` | Date, required |
| Start Time | `Start_Time__c` | Time |
| End Time | `End_Time__c` | Time |
| Status | `Status__c` | Picklist, restricted, required, default Scheduled |
| Session Schedule | `Session_Schedule__c` | Lookup to `Session_Schedule__c`, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Sessions |

- **Validation rules:** `Cohort_In_Program` (R-SE1), `End_After_Start` (R-SE6).
- **List views:** All Sessions, Upcoming Sessions (Scheduled, from today).
- **Session page:** `Session_Record_Page` with the `serviceDeliveryLog` panel in its session
  form (R-SE2, R-SE3), through `ServiceDeliveryLogController.getSessionLog` and `saveSession`.
- **PMM mapping:** Service Session (29ZA, PMM mapping).

---

## 29ZA7. Session Schedule

### Definition

A repeating pattern of sessions for one service, for a cohort or for everyone in the program:
"Tutoring, Tuesdays and Thursdays, 16:00 to 17:30" (modules-24, owner decision D-183). It
creates ordinary sessions a set number of weeks ahead, as a Shift Schedule creates shifts (29T),
and never deletes one on its own. ADR-0171 records why.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text(80) | yes | What staff call the schedule, for example "Spring tutoring". |
| Program | reference(Program) | yes | The program the schedule belongs to. |
| Service | reference(Service) | yes | The service of the program its sessions give (R-SS1). |
| Cohort | reference(Cohort) | no | The cohort of the program its sessions are for (R-SS1). Empty: for everyone enrolled in the program. |
| Days of the Week | multi-select(Monday to Sunday) | yes | The days of the week a session falls on. |
| Repeat Every (Weeks) | integer | yes (defaults 1) | 1 for every week, 2 for every other week, and so on, counted from the week of Start Date. |
| Start Time | time | no | Copied to each session's Start Time. |
| End Time | time | no | Copied to each session's End Time; after Start Time when both are set. |
| Start Date | date | yes | The first day a session may fall on. |
| End Date | date | no | The last day a session may fall on; empty means until the schedule is ended. |
| Active | boolean | yes (defaults true) | Whether the schedule still creates sessions. |
| Created Through | date | computed | The last day the schedule has created sessions for. Kept by the run; never edited. |

### Relationships

- **Session Schedule to Program**, many to one, master-detail: shared as its program is; deleting
  the program deletes its schedules.
- **Session Schedule to Service** and **to Cohort**, many to one, delete Restrict: a service or
  cohort with schedules cannot be deleted until they are.
- **Session Schedule to Session**, one to many, through the session's Session Schedule.

### Rules

**R-SS1 Valid pattern.** The service and the cohort, when set, are the program's; at least one
day; Repeat Every 1 to 52; End Time after Start Time when both are set; End Date not before
Start Date (validation rule).

**R-SS2 Which days and how far.** A day is a session day by R-SSC1's rule (29T). An active
schedule keeps sessions created from today to `Programs_Settings__c.Session_Horizon_Weeks__c`
weeks ahead (Weeks Ahead to Create Sessions, 1 to 26, default 8; blank or out of range reads
as 8). Each run creates the session days after Created Through (or from today, or Start
Date, if later) up to the horizon and End Date, and moves Created Through forward. A day is
skipped when it already has a session of this schedule (any status) or a session, not
Cancelled, of the same service for the same cohort (none: a program-wide session), including
one created earlier in the same run by another schedule. Each new
session is Scheduled, takes the schedule's service, cohort and times, links to the schedule,
and is named as the panel names one (service and date).

**R-SS3 When it runs.** Saving an active schedule queues a run for it, except the run's own save
of Created Through (`Session_Schedule_Rules`). The Programs nightly step runs every active
schedule, ten per transaction. Create Sessions Now on the schedule page runs it at once. A run
locks the schedule rows first, so two runs never create the same day. Nothing runs while the
module is turned off.

**R-SS4 Editing and ending never delete.** A change to the pattern applies to the days after
Created Through. Clearing Active, an earlier End Date or deleting the schedule only stops new
sessions; the sessions it made stay (a deleted schedule's lose their link).

**R-SS5 Remove Future Sessions.** On the schedule page, after a confirm, deletes the schedule's
sessions dated after today that are Scheduled and have no service delivery, in user mode (only
a user who may delete sessions sees it), sets Created Through to today, and runs an active
schedule, which recreates those days from its current pattern. Held, Cancelled and attended
sessions are kept, and their days are not given a second session.

**R-SS6 From the panel.** Save as Repeating Schedule on the Schedule Sessions panel creates an
active weekly schedule from the panel's service, cohort, From and To dates, days and times,
named after the service (and cohort), and runs it at once.

**R-SS7 Who.** As R-CO1: Programs Admin creates, edits and deletes schedules; Programs Staff
create and edit them; Programs Read Only reads them. Created Through is read only in every
permission set and written by the run in system mode.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Session_Schedule__c`, name field Text(80) labelled Schedule Name, sharing
  controlled by the program.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Program | `Program__c` | Master-Detail to `Program__c`, relationship name Session_Schedules |
| Service | `Service__c` | Lookup to `Service__c`, required, delete constraint Restrict, relationship name Session_Schedules |
| Cohort | `Cohort__c` | Lookup to `Cohort__c`, delete constraint Restrict, relationship name Session_Schedules |
| Days of the Week | `Weekdays__c` | Multi-Select Picklist: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday |
| Repeat Every (Weeks) | `Every_N_Weeks__c` | Number (2, 0), required, default 1 |
| Start Time | `Start_Time__c` | Time |
| End Time | `End_Time__c` | Time |
| Start Date | `Start_Date__c` | Date, required |
| End Date | `End_Date__c` | Date |
| Active | `Active__c` | Checkbox, default true |
| Created Through | `Created_Through__c` | Date, read only in every permission set |

- **Validation rule:** `Session_Schedule_Valid` (R-SS1).
- **Automation:** registry row `Session_Schedule_Rules` (`SessionScheduleTriggerHandler`), which
  queues `SessionScheduleJob`; nightly batch `SessionScheduleBatch`, started at 3:10 AM by
  `ProgramsScheduler` (job name `BarnCRM Session Schedules`), which
  `ProgramsNightlyJobProvider` supplies as a step of the nightly run (Section 29ZR). Run and
  removal in `SessionScheduleService`; queries in `SessionScheduleSelector`.
- **Schedule page:** `Session_Schedule_Record_Page` with the `sessionScheduleSessions` panel
  (preview, Create Sessions Now, Remove Future Sessions) through `SessionScheduleController`.
  Schedules are listed on the program and cohort pages; there is no tab.

## 29ZB. Service Delivery

### Definition

One service given to one person on one day, or their absence from it (P-02, Programs module):
a hot meal, two tutoring hours, a missed session. It is both attendance and service delivery, as
PMM's Service Delivery is: the attendance says whether the person came, the quantity counts what
they received in the service's unit. A delivery may name the session it was given at (P-11,
R-SD7): attendance at a session is a delivery, not a record of its own.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | An auto number: a delivery is identified by its person, service and date. |
| Service | reference(Service) | yes | The service given, and through it the program. |
| Enrollment | reference(Enrollment) | no | The person's enrollment in the service's program. Filled in when left empty (R-SD3). |
| Contact | reference(Contact) | conditional | The person, where people are Contacts. |
| Account | reference(Account) | conditional | The person, where people are person Accounts. |
| Delivery Date | date | yes (defaults today) | The day the service was given, or missed. |
| Attendance | picklist(Present, Excused Absence, Unexcused Absence) | yes (defaults Present) | Whether the person came. |
| Quantity | number | yes (defaults 1) | How much was given, in the service's unit of measure. 0 for an absence. |
| Session | reference(Session) | no | The session of the same service the delivery was given at (P-11, R-SD7). |

### Relationships

- **Service Delivery to Service**, many to one, through a required lookup with delete Restrict, not
  a detail, so participant privacy (P-08) can set deliveries apart from the program as it does
  enrollments. A service with deliveries cannot be deleted; clear its Active box instead.
- **Service Delivery to Enrollment**, many to one, optional, delete SetNull.
- **Service Delivery to a person**, through the Contact and Account pair (Section 4).
- **Service Delivery to Session**, many to one, optional, delete Restrict: a session with
  attendance cannot be deleted (29ZA6).

### Rules

**R-SD1 Exactly one person.** Contact or Account, never both, never neither (validation rule,
checked only when the delivery is new or its person changes, as R-EN1). The Account is a person
account, as R-EN1 (`ProgramPersonRule` in the always-running `Service_Delivery_Rules` handler;
QA-F4).

**R-SD2 An absence delivers nothing.** Quantity is never negative (validation rule). Saving a
delivery with an absence (Excused or Unexcused) sets its Quantity to 0. Always runs (registry
row `Service_Delivery_Rules`): totals would otherwise count services nobody received.

**R-SD3 The enrollment is filled in.** A delivery saved with no enrollment is linked to the
person's enrollment in the service's program: the open one, or else the one that started last.
A person with no enrollment there is still recorded; the delivery simply has none. Same
always-run row, as the link is what the roster and the P-05 dashboard count by.

**R-SD4 One row per person, service and day, from the grid.** The Service Delivery Log
(below) keeps one delivery per person per service per day, changing the row that is there
instead of adding another. Nothing refuses a second row entered by hand: two separate meals on
one day are two deliveries. When the log saves a new delivery for a person, service and day
that already has one the saving user cannot see (under the Private Participant Privacy preset, a
delivery another staff member logged is hidden), that delivery's Attendance and Quantity are
changed instead of a second row being added; the hidden delivery is still not shown to the user.
This needs update access to Service Delivery Attendance and Quantity.

**R-SD6 Participant privacy (P-08).** As R-EN7: sharing Private, every delivery shared with
`Programs_Participants` through the reason `Programs_Participants__c` (registry row
`Service_Delivery_Sharing`, always runs), so the Participant Privacy preset decides who sees
deliveries as it does enrollments.

**R-SD5 Erasing or deleting the person keeps the delivery.** As R-EN5: erasure credits it to the
anonymous record; deleting the person empties the person (SetNull) and keeps the counts.

**R-SD7 Attendance at a session (P-11).** A delivery's Session, when set, is a session of the
delivery's service (validation rule). The Service Delivery Log on a session page keeps one
delivery per person per session, with the session's service and date: a new row for a person who
already has a delivery of that session changes it instead, and a person's delivery for the same
service and day that names no session is adopted by the session (its Session is set) rather than
a second row being added. A hidden delivery is changed as in R-SD4, its Session included. The
program's log still keeps one row per person, service and day, whichever session it names.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Service_Delivery__c`, name field AutoNumber `SD-{000000}`, sharing Private
  (Public Read/Write before P-08), Apex sharing reason `Programs_Participants__c` (R-SD6).

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Service | `Service__c` | Lookup to `Service__c`, required, delete constraint Restrict, relationship name Service_Deliveries |
| Enrollment | `Enrollment__c` | Lookup to `Enrollment__c`, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Service_Deliveries |
| Contact | `Contact__c` | Lookup to Contact, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Service_Deliveries |
| Account | `Account__c` | Lookup to Account, delete constraint SetNull, relationship name Service_Deliveries |
| Delivery Date | `Delivery_Date__c` | Date, required, default `TODAY()` |
| Attendance | `Attendance__c` | Picklist: Present, Excused Absence, Unexcused Absence; required, default Present |
| Quantity | `Quantity__c` | Number(10, 2), required, default 1 |
| Session | `Session__c` | Lookup to `Session__c`, delete constraint Restrict, relationship name Service_Deliveries |

- **Validation rules:** `Exactly_One_Person` (R-SD1), `Quantity_Not_Negative` (R-SD2),
  `Session_Matches_Service` (R-SD7).
- **Service:** `ServiceDeliveryRulesHandler` (R-SD2, R-SD3) with `ServiceDeliveryService` and
  `ServiceDeliverySelector`, trigger `ServiceDeliveryTrigger` through `TriggerDispatcher`.
- **Service Delivery Log:** the `serviceDeliveryLog` panel on the program page
  (`ServiceDeliveryLogController`): pick an active service and a day, and every open
  enrollment (Applied or Enrolled) is listed with its attendance and quantity for that day, saved
  in one go (R-SD4). It works the same on a phone. On a session page the same panel takes the
  service and day from the session and lists the cohort (R-SE2, R-SD7), through
  `getSessionLog` and `saveSession`; `ServiceDeliveryIntegrity` finds and changes a hidden
  delivery of the session or of its service and day.

### PMM mapping

| BarnCRM | PMM | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Service Delivery: Service, Enrollment, Contact, Delivery Date, Attendance, Quantity, Session | Service Delivery: Service, Program Engagement, Contact, Delivery Date, Attendance Status, Quantity, Service Session | Attendance values match PMM's Present, Excused Absence and Unexcused Absence. Checked against an org with PMM with MIG-09. |

## 29ZB1. Service Count

### Definition

How many people a service served on a day, without naming them (P-12, release 0.15): a walk-in
meal, a pantry line, a clinic drop-in. Kept apart from Service Delivery (29ZB), which names each
person, so counts of unnamed people are never mistaken for, or added to, named people served.

### Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | yes | An auto number. |
| Service | reference(Service) | yes | The service the people were served by, and through it the program. |
| Count Date | date | yes (defaults today) | The day the people were served. |
| People Served | number(10, 0) | yes (defaults 1) | How many people, not named. Never negative; 0 is allowed. |
| Note | text(255) | no | Anything worth saying about the count, such as a shift or a site. |

### Relationships

- **Service Count to Service**, many to one, through a required lookup with delete Restrict. A
  service with counts cannot be deleted; clear its Active box instead.

### Rules

**R-SC1 Never negative.** People Served is not negative (validation rule).

**R-SC2 Counts add up.** A service and day may have several counts (two shifts, two sites); the
Service Delivery Log adds a row for each count entered, and every total adds the rows.

**R-SC3 Counted apart from named people.** The Programs Dashboard shows the sum of People Served
in the period as Counted Without Names, per program and in total. It is never added to People
Served (named people with a Present delivery).

**R-SC4 No person, so no privacy or erasure rule.** A count names no one, so organization-wide
sharing is Public Read/Write (object permissions decide who may add and change: Programs Admin
and Staff create and edit, Admin alone deletes, Read Only reads) and erasing a person never
reaches a count.

### Salesforce implementation

- **Object:** `Service_Count__c`, name field AutoNumber `SC-{000000}`, sharing Public Read/Write.

| Attribute | API name | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Service | `Service__c` | Lookup to `Service__c`, required, delete constraint Restrict, relationship name Service_Counts |
| Count Date | `Count_Date__c` | Date, required, default `TODAY()` |
| People Served | `People_Served__c` | Number(10, 0), required, default 1 |
| Note | `Note__c` | Text(255) |

- **Validation rules:** `People_Not_Negative` (R-SC1).
- **Service Delivery Log:** `ServiceDeliveryLogController.addCount` inserts a count as the user;
  `ServiceCountSelector` totals a service and day. The dashboard sums them in
  `ProgramDashboardController`.
- **UI:** the Service Counts tab (list views All Service Counts and This Week) and the Service
  Counts related list on the service. No trigger.
